`sandbox/specialist/Dockerfile`:

```
# The specialist image: the pinned base pulled from GHCR (adr:0012-pull-the-specialists-base-image-from-ghcr)
# plus the pinned Claude Code CLI for Linux, verified at build time against the release manifest,
# whose gpg signature is checked against Anthropic's release key
# (adr:0006-run-the-specialist-inside-a-container-per-task, specs/task-sandbox R2.6). Built locally,
# so the binary is never redistributed.

ARG BASE

FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS verify
ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION
ARG REPOSITORY=https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases
ARG RELEASE_SIGNER_URL=https://downloads.claude.ai/keys/claude-code.asc
# The fingerprint published on Claude Code's setup page.
ARG FINGERPRINT=31DDDE24DDFAB679F42D7BD2BAA929FF1A7ECACE
ARG PLATFORM=linux-x64

RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl gnupg jq \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /verify
RUN test -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION" \
 && export GNUPGHOME="$(mktemp -d)" \
 && curl -fsSL "$RELEASE_SIGNER_URL" -o key.asc \
 && gpg --batch --import key.asc \
 && curl -fsSL "$REPOSITORY/$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION/manifest.json" -o manifest.json \
 && curl -fsSL "$REPOSITORY/$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION/manifest.json.sig" -o manifest.json.sig \
 && gpg --batch --status-fd 1 --verify manifest.json.sig manifest.json > status.txt \
 && grep -E "^\[GNUPG:\] VALIDSIG .* $FINGERPRINT$|^\[GNUPG:\] VALIDSIG $FINGERPRINT " status.txt \
 && test "$(jq -r .version manifest.json)" = "$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION" \
 && checksum="$(jq -r --arg p "$PLATFORM" '.platforms[$p].checksum' manifest.json)" \
 && echo "$checksum" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' \
 && curl -fsSL "$REPOSITORY/$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION/$PLATFORM/claude" -o claude \
 && echo "$checksum  claude" | sha256sum -c - \
 && chmod 0755 claude

FROM ${BASE}
ARG BASE
ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION
LABEL hfr.claude-code="$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION" hfr.base="$BASE"

COPY --from=verify /verify/claude /usr/local/bin/claude

```

`scripts/build-cli.ts`:

```ts
// Builds the CLI/TUI with Bun (specs/release R1.3, R2.4):
//
//   bun scripts/build-cli.ts package                 the npm package in tui/: dist/main.js, sandbox/, the version
//   bun scripts/build-cli.ts binary <target> <out>   a standalone binary for a `--compile` target such as
//                                                    bun-windows-x64, bun-darwin-arm64 or bun-darwin-x64, with
//                                                    sandbox/ beside it in <out>
import { cpSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path"
import type { BunPlugin } from "bun"
import { CLI_SANDBOX } from "./cli-sandbox"

const root = join(import.meta.dir, "..")
const version = (JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, "package.json"), "utf8")) as { version: string }).version
const entry = join(root, "tui", "src", "main.tsx")

/** Vite's `?raw` imports — the specialist's operating guide — as the file's text, which Bun's bundler does not do itself. */
const raw: BunPlugin = {
  name: "raw",
  setup(build) {
    build.onResolve({ filter: /\?raw$/ }, (a) => ({ path: resolve(dirname(a.importer), a.path.slice(0, -"?raw".length)), namespace: "raw" }))
    build.onLoad({ filter: /.*/, namespace: "raw" }, (a) => ({ contents: `export default ${JSON.stringify(readFileSync(a.path, "utf8"))}`, loader: "js" }))
  },
}

/** Only the parts of sandbox/ the CLI reads at run time (scripts/cli-sandbox.ts). */
function copySandbox(to: string) {
  rmSync(join(to, "sandbox"), { recursive: true, force: true })
  for (const part of CLI_SANDBOX) cpSync(join(root, "sandbox", part), join(to, "sandbox", part), { recursive: true })
}

/**
  OpenTUI React's devtools and their WebSocket, imported only when its DEV switch is on, which the TUI never sets:
  built as empty modules rather than installed (adr:0023-build-the-tui-on-opentuis-react-layer).
*/
const devtools: BunPlugin = {
  name: "devtools",
  setup(build) {
    build.onResolve({ filter: /^(react-devtools-core|ws)$/ }, (a) => ({ path: a.path, namespace: "devtools" }))
    build.onLoad({ filter: /.*/, namespace: "devtools" }, () => ({ contents: "export default { initialize() {}, connectToDevTools() {} }", loader: "js" }))
  },
}

function check(r: { success: boolean; logs: unknown[] }) {
  if (r.success) return
  for (const l of r.logs) console.error(l)
  process.exit(1)
}

const [mode, target, out] = process.argv.slice(2)
if (mode === "package") {
  const tui = join(root, "tui")
  rmSync(join(tui, "dist"), { recursive: true, force: true })
  // OpenTUI stays a dependency: npm installs its library for the user's platform.
  check(
    await Bun.build({
      entrypoints: [entry],
      target: "bun",
      outdir: join(tui, "dist"),
      naming: "main.js",
      external: ["@opentui/core", "@napi-rs/keyring"],
      plugins: [raw, devtools],
    }),
  )
  copySandbox(tui)
  const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(tui, "package.json"), "utf8"))
  writeFileSync(join(tui, "package.json"), `${JSON.stringify({ ...manifest, version }, null, 2)}\n`)
  console.log(`harness-for-rea ${version}: tui/ is ready to pack`)
} else if (mode === "binary" && target && out) {
  mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true })
  const outfile = join(out, target.includes("windows") ? "harness-for-rea.exe" : "harness-for-rea")
  check(await Bun.build({ entrypoints: [entry], compile: { target: target as Bun.Build.CompileTarget, outfile }, plugins: [raw, devtools] }))
  copySandbox(out)
  console.log(`${outfile} built for ${target}`)
} else {
  console.error("Usage: bun scripts/build-cli.ts package | binary <target> <out dir>")
  process.exit(2)
}

```

`scripts/context-hash.mjs`:

```mjs
// The hash of a Docker build context (specs/sandbox-images R1.1): every file sorted by path, each
// as its path, NUL, its content with CRLF folded to LF, NUL, so a Windows checkout and CI agree.
import { createHash } from "node:crypto"
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { join, relative } from "node:path"
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"

function files(dir) {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((e) => (e.isDirectory() ? files(join(dir, e.name)) : [join(dir, e.name)]))
}

export function contextHash(dir) {
  const h = createHash("sha256")
  const all = files(dir)
    .map((f) => ({ f, rel: relative(dir, f).split("\\").join("/") }))
    .sort((a, b) => (a.rel < b.rel ? -1 : a.rel > b.rel ? 1 : 0))
  for (const { f, rel } of all) {
    h.update(`${rel}\0`)
    h.update(readFileSync(f).toString("latin1").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n"), "latin1")
    h.update("\0")
  }
  return h.digest("hex")
}

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? "").href) process.stdout.write(`${contextHash(process.argv[2])}\n`)

```

`scripts/pin-images.mjs`:

// Pins the specialist's base image (specs/sandbox-images R1.3): resolves the tag of the current build
// context's hash on GHCR to its digest and rewrites sandbox/images.json. Run after the Images workflow
// has published the context.
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process"
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { contextHash } from "./context-hash.mjs"

const ROOT = join(import.meta.dirname, "..")
const REPOSITORY = "ghcr.io/protonspy/hfr-specialist-base"

const context = contextHash(join(ROOT, "sandbox", "specialist-base"))
const manifest = JSON.parse(
  execFileSync("docker", ["buildx", "imagetools", "inspect", `${REPOSITORY}:${context}`, "--format", "{{json .Manifest}}"], { encoding: "utf8" }),
)
if (!/^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(manifest.digest)) throw new Error(`No digest for ${REPOSITORY}:${context}`)
const pins = { specialistBase: { ref: `${REPOSITORY}@${manifest.digest}`, context } }
writeFileSync(join(ROOT, "sandbox", "images.json"), `${JSON.stringify(pins, null, 2)}\n`)
process.stdout.write(`${pins.specialistBase.ref}\n`)

`scripts/test-gate.mjs`:

```mjs
// The test gate: run the suite with coverage, then print the one line `scc check` reads,
// {"total": N, "coverage": P}, and exit with the suite's own status.
//
// With HFR_BUN=1 (CI sets it), the tests that need Bun count too (plans/tui-revamp 1.5): Vitest runs the Bun core
// tests in tests/bun-core.test.ts, and `bun test tui/test` runs the TUI's screen tests on OpenTUI's test renderer.
// Bun is the one on PATH, or 1.4.4 fetched through npx.

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process"
import { existsSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from "node:fs"
import path from "node:path"

const root = path.join(import.meta.dirname, "..")
const results = path.join(root, "coverage", "results.json")
const summary = path.join(root, "coverage", "coverage-summary.json")
const bunResults = path.join(root, "coverage", "bun-results.xml")
rmSync(results, { force: true })
rmSync(bunResults, { force: true })

const vitest = path.join(root, "node_modules", "vitest", "vitest.mjs")
const run = spawnSync(process.execPath, [vitest, "run", "--coverage", "--reporter=default", "--reporter=json", `--outputFile.json=${results}`], {
  cwd: root,
  stdio: "inherit",
})

let total = existsSync(results) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(results, "utf8")).numTotalTests : 0
let status = run.status ?? 1

if (process.env.HFR_BUN) {
  const shell = process.platform === "win32"
  const onPath = spawnSync("bun", ["--version"], { encoding: "utf8", shell }).status === 0
  const [cmd, pre] = onPath ? ["bun", []] : ["npx", ["-y", "bun@1.4.4"]]
  const screens = spawnSync(cmd, [...pre, "test", "tui/test", "--reporter=junit", `--reporter-outfile=${bunResults}`], { cwd: root, stdio: "inherit", shell })
  const xml = existsSync(bunResults) ? readFileSync(bunResults, "utf8") : ""
  const counted = Number(/<testsuites[^>]*\btests="(\d+)"/.exec(xml)?.[1] ?? 0)
  total += counted
  // No screen test counted is a renderer that did not start: the gate fails rather than passing on Vitest alone.
  if (screens.status !== 0 || counted === 0) status = status || screens.status || 1
}

const coverage = existsSync(summary) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(summary, "utf8")).total.lines.pct : 0
console.log(JSON.stringify({ total, coverage }))
process.exit(status)

```

# Analysis contract — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1–R2.5.

- `src/shared/contract.ts` (new) — `ContractSchema` (zod) and `readContract(report)`: the last fenced
  ```` ```json ```` block of the report, parsed and validated; the problems, one line each, when it
  is missing or invalid (R1.2).
- `src/main/sandbox/prompt.ts` — the system prompt states the contract's shape and that it ends the
  report, whatever report format the package names (R1.1). `renderPrompt` gains a section listing
  the project's open unknowns by id, with how to close one (R2.4).
- `src/main/delegation.ts` — after the first answer, up to `CONTRACT_ROUNDS` (2) further turns in
  the same session carry the problems back (R1.3), each logged as `contract.rejected`. The step
  records `contract` or `contractProblems` (R1.4). Usage is counted from every turn's result event,
  no longer from the last result alone. With a project, open unknowns go into the prompt and a valid
  contract updates the ledger (R2.1–R2.3).
- `src/main/db.ts` — migration 4: `unknowns (id, project_id, question, severity, probes, settle,
  raised_by, closed_by, resolution, created_at, updated_at)`.
- `src/main/unknowns.ts` (new) — the ledger: `open(projectId)`, `list(projectId)`, and
  `record(projectId, stepId, contract)` which adds and closes, returning what it ignored (R2.1–R2.3).
- `src/main/orchestrator/tools.ts` — `delegate_to_specialist` returns `contract` (or
  `contractProblems`) beside the report (R1.5).
- `src/shared/api.ts`, `src/main/index.ts`, `ProjectView.tsx` — `getProject` also returns the
  project's unknowns, open first, which the view lists; it already reloads when a delegation moves
  (R2.5).

## Data

```json
{
  "functions": [{ "name": "", "inputs": [""], "outputs": [""], "sideEffects": [""], "source": "" }],
  "constants": [{ "name": "", "value": 0, "source": "path:10-12 | path@0x… | ev_…", "estimated": false }],
  "unknowns": [{ "question": "", "severity": "low | medium | high", "probes": [""], "settle": "" }],
  "closes": [{ "id": "", "resolution": "", "source": "" }]
}
```

Every list defaults to empty, so a step that maps nothing still returns `{}`.

# Analysis contract — requirements

## Purpose

Makes an analysis checkable by the app rather than read from prose: the specialist ends each report
with a machine-readable contract — the functions it mapped, the constants it found, each tied to a
source or marked estimated, and the questions it left open or closed — which the app validates and
sends back when it fails. What one analysis leaves open is kept per project, in an unknowns ledger,
and handed to the next delegation of the project. Drawn from [[craft-anything]]'s contract and
ledger; for the orchestrator consolidating analyses and the user following a project.

## R1 · The contract

- **R1.1** (MODIFIED) The specialist's instructions shall ask for a report that ends with a JSON contract listing the functions mapped with their inputs, outputs and side effects, the constants found each with a source or marked estimated, the unknowns opened, the earlier unknowns closed, and the test vectors observed (specs/vector-replay R1.2).
- **R1.2** When a delegation's report arrives, the delegation shall validate its contract, refusing a constant that has neither a source nor `estimated: true`.
- **R1.3** If a report's contract is missing or invalid, then the delegation shall return the problems to the specialist in the same session for a corrected report, at most twice.
- **R1.4** If the contract is still invalid after the last correction, then the delegation shall finish with the last report and record that its contract failed, with the problems.
- **R1.5** The delegation shall give the orchestrator the validated contract with the report.

## R2 · The unknowns ledger

- **R2.1** When a delegation of a project returns a valid contract, the app shall add each unknown it opened to the project's unknowns ledger, tied to that analysis.
- **R2.2** When a contract closes an open unknown of the project by its id, the app shall mark it closed with its resolution and the analysis that closed it.
- **R2.3** If a contract closes an unknown that is not open in the project, then the app shall leave the ledger unchanged for that item and record why.
- **R2.4** When a delegation of a project starts, the app shall put the project's open unknowns into its context package.
- **R2.5** The desktop UI shall show a project's unknowns, open and closed, on the project's view.

## Out of scope

- Checking that a sourced constant appears in the orchestrator's code.
- Feeding REA's own `record_unknown` into the ledger.

```

`specs/app-shell/design.md`:

```md
# App shell — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R2.1, R2.2, R2.3, R2.4, R3.1, R3.2, R3.3, R4.1, R4.2.

The project skeleton is carried over from `study-lab` (electron-vite, one
`@shared` alias for main, preload and renderer) with the hardened window of the
MagnoTech desktop app (`janela.ts`). Tests run on Vitest with V8 coverage instead
of `node:test`, because the gate reads a coverage figure; `electron` is aliased
to a stub so main-process code runs under plain Node.

## Boundaries and contracts

`src/shared/api.ts` is the whole contract: one zod schema per method for its
arguments, the method names derived from that table, and the union of pushed
messages. The preload builds the bridge from the method names, so a method that is
not in the table does not exist in the renderer. The main process dispatches every
call through one `ipcMain.handle("api", …)` that checks the sender's frame URL
against the app's page, looks the method up, parses the arguments and only then
runs the handler.

```
renderer ── window.hfr.api.<method>(...args) ──▶ preload ── invoke("api", method, ...args) ──▶ dispatch
renderer ◀── window.hfr.onPush(fn) ── preload ◀── webContents.send("push", message) ──────── main
```

The OpenRouter key lives in the settings table as base64 of
`safeStorage.encryptString`; with encryption unavailable `saveKey` throws, unlike
`study-lab`, which fell back to base64 of the plain key.

`scripts/test-gate.mjs` runs `vitest run --coverage` with the JSON summary
reporter and prints the one line the gate reads, exiting with Vitest's status.

## Risks

- Coverage counts `src/main` and `src/shared` and the renderer's `lib/`; the
  Electron entry point and React views are exercised by running the app, not by
  the suite, so the figure says nothing about them.

```

# App shell — requirements

## Purpose

The Electron skeleton every other feature runs in: a window the renderer cannot
escape from, one typed and validated IPC contract between renderer and main, a
credential store that never writes the OpenRouter key in plain text, and the
build, format, lint and test commands the delivery gate runs.

## R1 · Window

- **R1.1** The app shell shall create its window with context isolation, the renderer sandbox, web security on, and Node integration and web views off.
- **R1.2** If the renderer navigates away from the app's page or opens a new window, then the app shell shall block it.
- **R1.3** The app shell shall load the renderer under a Content Security Policy that allows scripts only from the app itself.
- **R1.4** (MODIFIED) When the desktop app is launched while it is already running, the app shell shall focus the running window and quit the second launch before it starts any service, while terminal UIs run beside it (specs/shared-data-folder R4.4).

## R2 · IPC

- **R2.1** The app shell shall expose to the renderer only the methods named in the shared API contract, through the preload bridge.
- **R2.2** When the renderer calls a method, the app shell shall validate its arguments against that method's schema before running it.
- **R2.3** If a call names an unknown method, fails validation, or comes from a frame other than the app's page, then the app shell shall reject it with an error and not run it.
- **R2.4** When the main process has a new event or state change, the app shell shall push it to the renderer as an incremental message.

## R3 · Credentials

- **R3.1** (MODIFIED) The app shell shall store each provider's API key in the OS-keychain store the terminal UI reads too, moving a key it kept with Electron's `safeStorage` into it (specs/shared-data-folder R5).
- **R3.2** (MODIFIED) If the OS keychain is unavailable, then the app shell shall refuse to store the key and report why, without writing it in plain text.
- **R3.3** The app shell shall never return the stored key to the renderer, only whether one is set and a masked hint.

## R4 · Delivery gate

- **R4.1** The app shell shall provide build, format check, lint and test commands, the test command printing `{"total": N, "coverage": P}` and keeping the suite's exit status.
- **R4.2** When a branch is pushed, the CI workflow shall run the build, format check, lint and test on Windows.

## Out of scope

- Auto-update and code signing of the installer.

```

# Chat timeline — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1–R3.4, with deltas to `specs/event-log/` (paged reads both ways) and `specs/desktop-ui/` (the timeline in the task view).

- `src/main/events/log.ts` — `history(taskId, { beforeEvent | afterEvent, limit })`. Without a
  cursor it returns the newest page; `beforeEvent` the page just older; `afterEvent` the page just
  newer, as today. `hasMore` speaks for the direction asked (R2.1). It also returns `usage`, each
  agent's calls, tokens and cost summed in SQLite over the whole task (R3.3); steps were already
  read whole.
- `src/main/orchestrator/runner.ts`, `tools.ts`, `delegation.ts` — the orchestrator's `tool.call`
  and `tool.result` events carry LangChain's `toolCallId` as `callId`, and a delegation step
  records the `callId` of the call that started it. The timeline pairs a result with its call, and
  a delegation with its call, by that id rather than by counting earlier calls, which a page that
  starts mid-task cannot do (R1.1). Events written before this change still pair by order.
- `src/renderer/src/lib/timeline.ts` (new) — a fold kept between renders: `append(events)` folds
  only the new events into the existing entries (R3.2); `prepend(events)` refolds from the older
  page, which happens once per page the user asks for. Specialist events (any event with a
  delegation's `stepId` whose agent is the specialist) become children of that delegation's entry
  (R1.1, R1.3). `chat.ts`'s `conversation` stays the pure fold the timeline is built on.
- `src/renderer/src/lib/virtual.ts` (new) — the window of entries to render from measured heights,
  an estimate for the rest, the scroll offset and an overscan (R3.1), and the scroll correction
  that keeps content in place when a page is prepended (R2.3).
- `src/renderer/src/views/TaskView.tsx` and `components/chat/` — the timeline rendered through
  the window, rows measured with a `ResizeObserver`, a sentinel at the top that loads the previous
  page (R2.2, R2.3), delegations as cards whose specialist entries are collapsed rows (R1.2), usage
  from `history.usage` and step state from the steps (R3.3).

## Data

`TaskHistory` gains `usage: AgentUsage[]` and `hasOlder: boolean`; `hasMore` keeps meaning newer
events exist after the page. `getTask`'s options gain `beforeEvent`, exclusive of `afterEvent`.

## Alternatives considered

- A virtual-list library: one component's worth of code, against a new dependency and its
  ADR. The window is a pure function, tested in `lib/`.
- CSS `content-visibility: auto` alone: it skips layout and paint off screen but still builds a
  DOM node per entry, which is the cost at 10,000 events.

```

# Chat timeline — requirements

## Purpose

The task view as a chat timeline in the style of Claude Code Web and Codex Web, built to hold
long runs: a task with tens of thousands of events opens at once, scrolls smoothly, and still
shows each agent's turns, tool calls and delegations, the specialist's own work nested under the
delegation that ran it. It is for the user watching or reviewing a task.

## R1 · The timeline

- **R1.1** The task view shall show the task as a chat timeline: the user's messages, the orchestrator's turns, tool calls and delegations in order, and each specialist's text, thinking and tool calls nested under the delegation that ran them.
- **R1.2** (MODIFIED) The task view shall show each tool call's input and output, each delegation, and each specialist entry's payload — its text, reasoning and tool calls — expanded from the start, each collapsible by the user.
- **R1.3** When a specialist event arrives for a delegation on screen, the task view shall add it under that delegation.
- **R1.4** (ADDED) While a specialist's tool call runs, the task view shall show how long it has run, from Claude Code's progress heartbeats, which shall never appear as entries of their own.

## R2 · Paging

- **R2.1** The event log shall return a task's events in pages before or after a given event id, oldest first within a page, saying whether more exist in the direction asked.
- **R2.2** When a task opens, the task view shall load its newest page of events.
- **R2.3** When the user scrolls to the top of the timeline while older events exist, the task view shall load the previous page and keep what was on screen where it was.

## R3 · Holding long runs

- **R3.1** The task view shall render only the timeline entries near the viewport.
- **R3.2** When events arrive, the task view shall fold only the new events into the timeline.
- **R3.3** The task view shall show each agent's usage and each step's state as the main process reports them for the whole task, never as counted from the loaded events.
- **R3.4** While a task holds over 10,000 events, the task view shall open it in under a second and scroll it within a frame budget.

## Out of scope

- Searching or filtering the timeline.
- Changing what the event log stores: only how it is read.

`specs/chat/design.md`:

```md
# Chat — design

## What changes

Serves R1–R7. The task stops being one request with one answer and becomes a
conversation: `src/main/orchestrator/runner.ts` keeps a task's agent, thread and
container alive across turns, and the renderer's `TaskView` becomes a chat surface.
Two changes cross the sandbox boundary the project guards and each gets an ADR; the
rest is lifecycle and UI.

## Turn lifecycle (R1, R2, R3)

`TaskRunner` today runs one `drive()` per task and disposes the workspace on done.

- A turn that ends with no interrupt leaves the task `awaiting-user`, keeping the
  `Live` entry, the thread and the container. `sendMessage(taskId, text)` with no
  live turn starts a new `drive()` with `{ messages: [new HumanMessage(text)] }` on
  the same `thread_id`; the checkpointer resumes the prior state (R1.1, R1.2, R1.4).
- **Mid-turn messages** — the `Live` entry gains an inbox. A langchain middleware
  `beforeModel` hook drains the inbox into user messages before each model call and
  records a `message.read` event (R2.1, R2.2). The inbox is the orchestrator's only;
  a running delegation is not interrupted (R2.3). A rejected gated call resumes with
  `jumpTo: model`, past every `beforeModel` hook, so what the user wrote while the turn
  waited rides on the rejection's message instead (n-0007). A message sent during the
  turn's last model call opens the next turn rather than waiting for one.
- **Stop** reuses the abort controller but is non-terminal: the turn is marked
  `stopped`, delegations abort, and `continueTurn(taskId)` starts a turn that resumes
  from the checkpoint (R3.1, R3.2). A stop the stream does not observe within a bound
  still settles the turn (R3.3), as `cancel` does now.
- The container is disposed on explicit close (`closeTask`, from awaiting-user or
  stopped), on cancel, or at app quit — not at the end of a turn. At startup a task left
  awaiting the user is closed with its answer kept; one left stopped is interrupted.

## Approval and questions (R4, R5)

- **Gated tools** — the desktop app starts every task with `auto`, so `interruptOn` is empty and no call pauses (R4.1); the runner still takes a gated set, built from the task's chosen tools rather than
  the fixed `apply_patch`, each with `allowedDecisions: ["approve", "edit", "reject"]`; `apply_patch` takes
  approve or reject only, since a patch is decided as the specialist proposed it.
  The pending-decision machinery in `runner.ts` already carries one decision per
  action request; it extends to carry `edited_action` for edit and `message` for
  reject, resumed with `new Command({ resume: { decisions } })` (R4.1–R4.4). The
  approval timeout rejects a stale call with origin `timeout` (R4.5).
- **The orchestrator's question** — an `ask_user` tool returns a promise held in the
  `Live` entry beside the patch pending-list; the UI answers over IPC and the promise
  resolves, so no checkpoint resume is needed. Timeout resolves the default (R5.1,
  R5.4, R5.5).
- **The specialist's question** — the specialist runs in a networkless container
  (adr:0006-run-the-specialist-inside-a-container-per-task). It asks over a file
  channel in the run directory, which is already bind-mounted; see
  **adr:0008-ask-the-user-from-the-specialist-over-the-run-channel** (R5.2). Kinds,
  reason, default and the cap are shared by both tools in `src/shared/` (R5.3, R5.5).

## The division of labour (R6)

- The orchestrator's system prompt (`agent.ts`) delegates every analysis to the
  specialist and forbids the orchestrator from stating conclusions about code it only
  read (R6.1).
- The orchestrator writes and runs code on the specialist's findings in a writable
  scratch separate from the read-only source mount; see
  **adr:0009-give-the-orchestrator-a-writable-scratch**. Source stays read-only, and a
  change to it is still a specialist patch through the existing approval (R6.2–R6.4).
- A middleware in `agent.ts` holds the orchestrator to an allowlist: `write_todos`, `ls`,
  `glob`, `read_file`, `grep`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `execute`,
  `delegate_to_specialist`, `propose_patch`, `apply_patch` and `ask_user`. It hides every
  other tool — DeepAgents' `task` subagent and `delete` among them — from the model and
  refuses a call to one. The orchestrator is a coding assistant that reads the user's
  code to write and integrate its own; the instructions send every analysis of the
  target to the specialist, which does the reverse engineering; see
  **adr:0011-limit-the-orchestrator-to-planning-delegation-and-its-own-code** (R6.5).
- `propose_patch` reads the named files out of `/scratch`, resolves each target with
  `resolveTarget`, and writes a patch the way `makePatch` does, base hashes taken from
  the originals now; it is recorded under a `patch` step of the orchestrator, and
  `apply_patch` then takes it through the same approval (R6.6).
- A delegation's `files` may name files under `/scratch`; `delegate_to_specialist` reads
  them out of the task container and `prepareWorkspace` writes them under `.orchestrator/`
  in the workspace, outside the snapshot and its manifest, and `makePatch` leaves that
  folder out, so what the orchestrator prepared reaches the specialist and never the
  source (R6.7).

## IPC (R7)

`src/shared/api.ts` gains, each with its zod schema: `sendMessage(taskId, text)`,
`stopTurn(taskId)`, `continueTurn(taskId)`, `closeTask(taskId)`,
`decideTool(taskId, callId, decision)` carrying `args` for edit and `message` for reject,
and `answerQuestion(taskId, questionId, answer)`. `startTask` gains the chosen gated-tool
set; `getTask` carries the turn state derived from the checkpointer (R1.5). The renderer renders messages, tool-call
cards, an approve/edit/reject card and a per-kind question card, keeps the message box
enabled while a turn runs, and shows stop, continue and your-turn controls (R7.1–R7.5).
The conversation is folded from the event log by a pure function in
`src/renderer/src/lib/chat.ts`, so live and reopened tasks render alike.

The surface is built from shadcn/ui components on Radix, kept as source in
`src/renderer/src/components/ui/`, and the theme moves to shadcn/ui's token names; see
**adr:0010-build-the-renderer-on-shadcn-ui-and-radix**.

## Alternatives considered

- **The specialist asks over a local socket** rather than the run-channel file —
  rejected in adr:0008 for a second reason the file channel avoids: a socket is
  another thing to confine in the container.
- **A SQLite checkpointer** so a continued turn survives a restart — rejected as in
  specs/orchestrator: the sandbox's live state does not survive the restart either,
  and a stopped turn across a restart becomes a retry.

```

# Chat — requirements

## Purpose

Turn a task from one request and one answer into a conversation the user stays in: a
multi-turn chat on the task's thread, where the user sends follow-up messages while
the agent works, stops and continues a run, approves, edits or rejects the tool calls
they chose to gate, and answers questions the agent asks mid-run. It sets the division
of labour the harness is built on — the specialist reasons about the target code, the
orchestrator dispatches, organises files and writes code on the specialist's findings
— and gives both agents a way to ask the user. Builds on the orchestrator's interrupt
and checkpointer (specs/orchestrator R3) and the live task view (specs/desktop-ui R2).

## R1 · The conversation

- **R1.1** The chat shall run every turn of a task on one thread keyed by the task id, so each turn resumes the agent's state through the checkpointer rather than starting over.
- **R1.2** When the user sends a message on a task whose turn has ended, the chat shall start a new turn from that message on the same thread.
- **R1.3** The chat shall record each user message and each agent message as events in the task's log, ordered with the task's other events.
- **R1.4** When a turn ends with no interrupt pending, the chat shall mark the task awaiting the user rather than done, and the user's next message continues the conversation.
- **R1.5** The chat shall derive a turn's running, waiting and awaiting-user state from the checkpointer and the event log, so a reopened task shows where the conversation stands.

## R2 · Messages sent mid-turn

- **R2.1** While a turn is running, the chat shall accept a message from the user and deliver it to the agent before its next model call as a user message.
- **R2.2** When the agent reads a message delivered mid-turn, the chat shall record an event the UI shows as the agent having read it.
- **R2.3** The chat shall apply R2.1 to the orchestrator only; a message never reaches a specialist delegation in progress.

## R3 · Stop and continue

- **R3.1** While a turn is running or waiting, the chat shall let the user stop it, aborting the model call and every running delegation and marking the turn stopped.
- **R3.2** When a turn is stopped, the chat shall offer to continue it, and on the user's choice start a turn that resumes from the checkpoint.
- **R3.3** If the agent does not observe a stop within a bounded interval, then the chat shall still mark the turn stopped and release the task's resources.

## R4 · Approving tool calls

- **R4.1** (MODIFIED) The chat shall start every task with no tool gated, running each of the orchestrator's tool calls, `apply_patch` included, without pausing for a decision; a task retried keeps running without asking unless it was started with gates.
- **R4.2** When a gated tool is about to run, the chat shall interrupt the turn, record the call with its arguments, and wait for the user's decision.
- **R4.3** The chat shall accept one of approve, edit or reject for a gated call: edit carries replacement arguments the agent runs instead, and reject carries a message returned to the agent in place of the result.
- **R4.4** When the user decides every pending call, the chat shall resume the turn from the checkpointer with those decisions.
- **R4.5** If a gated call waits longer than the task's approval timeout, then the chat shall reject it and record the decision's origin as the timeout.

## R5 · Asking the user

- **R5.1** The chat shall give the orchestrator a tool to ask the user a question, pausing the turn until the user answers and returning the answer to the agent.
- **R5.2** (MODIFIED) When the specialist asks a question from inside its sandbox, the chat shall put it first to one call of the orchestrator's model with the delegation's context package, and shall return that answer across the sandbox boundary to the delegation without granting the specialist any other channel out (adr:0021-answer-the-specialist-from-the-orchestrator-and-let-the-user-decide-a-refusal).
- **R5.6** (ADDED) If the orchestrator's model judges that a specialist's question needs a fact only the user has, or it cannot answer it, then the chat shall put the question to the user.
- **R5.3** The chat shall require each question to carry a prompt, a reason, a kind — choice, yes/no, number or free text — and a default, and shall present the input the kind calls for.
- **R5.4** (MODIFIED) When a question is answered, the chat shall return the answer and record its origin as the orchestrator or the user who answered it; if a question put to the user is unanswered within its timeout, then the chat shall return the default and record the origin as the timeout.
- **R5.5** (MODIFIED) The chat shall cap the number of questions an agent may put to the user within one turn and return the default once the cap is reached, counting neither the questions the orchestrator's model answers nor the choice a safeguard refusal waits on.

## R6 · The division of labour

- **R6.1** The orchestrator's instructions shall delegate every analysis of the target's behaviour or structure to the specialist, and the orchestrator shall not state conclusions about the code it has only read itself.
- **R6.2** The orchestrator shall dispatch, organise the files a delegation needs, and write code that builds on the specialist's findings, including scripts it runs to test a hypothesis.
- **R6.3** The orchestrator shall run the code it writes in a writable scratch area in its task container that is separate from the read-only source mount, so no experiment it runs can change the user's files.
- **R6.4** When the orchestrator produces a change to the user's source, the chat shall carry it as a patch through the existing patch approval, leaving the source read-only to the orchestrator.
- **R6.5** The orchestrator shall have only the tools for planning, listing, finding, reading and searching files, writing and running code in its scratch area, delegating to the specialist, proposing and applying a patch, and asking the user; a call to any other tool shall be refused.
- **R6.6** When the orchestrator proposes files from its scratch area as a change to the user's source, the chat shall record them as a patch against the current originals and carry it through the existing patch approval.
- **R6.7** When the orchestrator delegates, the specialist's workspace shall also hold the files the orchestrator names from its scratch area, apart from the source's files and never part of a patch.

## R7 · The chat surface

- **R7.1** The desktop UI shall show the task as a conversation: user and agent messages, the agent's tool calls and results, and its questions, in the order they occurred.
- **R7.2** While a turn is running or waiting, the desktop UI shall keep the message box enabled for a mid-turn message and show the turn's state.
- **R7.3** When a tool call awaits a decision, the desktop UI shall show the call with its arguments and offer approve, edit and reject.
- **R7.4** When the agent asks a question, the desktop UI shall show it with the input its kind calls for and a control to answer.
- **R7.5** When a turn is stopped, the desktop UI shall offer to continue it; when a turn ends awaiting the user, the desktop UI shall show that it is the user's turn.
- **R7.6** (ADDED) The desktop UI shall show the agent's and the user's messages and the specialist's report as markdown, without interpreting HTML, following links or loading images, and the code blocks in them with syntax colors from CodeMirror's Lezer parsers.

## Out of scope

- Resuming a Claude Code session cut off mid-delegation (specs/task-persistence out of scope).
- Several tasks sharing one conversation; a thread is one task.
- Streaming the model's tokens as they generate; the UI advances on node updates and recorded events (specs/desktop-ui R2.2).

```

```md
# Cheat engine — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1–R3.4, the first integration of specs/mcp-integrations/, under
adr:0026-proxy-host-engines-to-the-agents-as-mcp-integrations.

- `sandbox/cheat-engine/hfr-bridge.lua` (new) — the bridge, derived from
  `miscusi-peek/cheatengine-mcp-bridge` at commit `6bd7ce90479250a9b4b75e7944df9c105ecb2572`
  (2026-08-14), with its MIT notice and that commit in its header (R2.3). It keeps the upstream
  transport — a named pipe, each message a 4-byte little-endian length and a JSON-RPC 2.0 body —
  on its own pipe, `\\.\pipe\hfr-cheat-engine`, so it never answers for the upstream bridge. Its
  `commandHandlers` table holds only the catalog's methods plus `ping`, `open_process` and
  `get_opened_process_id`; every other upstream handler is deleted, not disabled, and an unknown
  method gets `-32601` (R2.1, R2.2). `ping` returns the bridge's version and Cheat Engine's.
  Its handlers are locals and its start and stop are `HfrBridgeStart`/`HfrBridgeStop`, so it
  loads beside the upstream bridge in the same Lua state without either replacing the other's.
  `open_process` drops the last value scan, so a process never reads another's scan results.
  Shipped under `sandbox/`, which `electron-builder.yml` already packs and `host.sandboxDir`
  already locates.
- `src/shared/cheatengine.ts` (new) — the integration's `IntegrationInfo`: the executable path
  as its setting (R1.1), the process target `{ pid }` (R3.1), the install action, and the
  catalog: `status`, `get_process_list` and the read commands of R2.1, each with its bridge
  method and argument schema, `read_memory`'s length capped at 64 KB. Every schema is strict, and
  an address is a number or an address expression with no parentheses, quotes, commas or
  semicolons; a module or symbol name has no brackets either. The executable is a local `.exe`,
  never a network path. `validate_pointer_chains` takes `target_address`, passed to the bridge as its
  `target`, so it never reads as the integration's target. `status` and `get_process_list`
  default to the orchestrator and need no target (R2.5, R3.2).
- `src/main/cheatengine/pipe.ts` (new) — the pipe client: `net.connect` on the pipe path
  (injectable, so tests use a local socket), the framing, one call in flight at a time, a
  timeout per call counted from when it is queued, so a call that waited it out is dropped unsent,
  and `exclusive` for calls that must run with nothing between them.
- `src/main/cheatengine/integration.ts` (new) — the host side the registry calls:
  - `checks`: the executable exists, the bridge is in `<Cheat Engine folder>/autorun/`, and
    `ping` answers with the app's bridge version, each failure with its fix (R1.2);
  - the install action copies the bridge there, and on a write error returns the paths to copy
    by hand (R1.3, R1.4);
  - `status` answers R2.4 from `ping` and the catalog;
  - `describeTarget` reads the process's name and executable path for the approval (R3.1), and
    `identify` adds its start time, so an approval of a pid Windows reused is asked again (R3.4);
  - `session(pid)` opens the process in the bridge, and before every call checks that the PID is
    alive and, in one exclusive unit with the call, that `get_opened_process_id` is still the PID,
    so another session's `open_process` cannot land between the check and the read (R3.3, R3.4).

## Testing

- The integration's checks, install, status and session run in Vitest against a fake bridge on
  a local socket that speaks the same framing.
- A test reads `hfr-bridge.lua`'s `commandHandlers` keys and holds them equal to the catalog's
  methods plus `ping`, `open_process` and `get_opened_process_id`, so a handler added to the
  Lua without the catalog fails.
- The bridge inside a real Cheat Engine is checked by running the app.

```

# Cheat engine — requirements

## Purpose

Cheat Engine is the first MCP integration (specs/mcp-integrations/): the agents read the live
memory of a Windows process the user approved, through Cheat Engine on the host. The app ships its
own bridge, derived from `miscusi-peek/cheatengine-mcp-bridge`, that answers read-only commands
only (adr:0026-proxy-host-engines-to-the-agents-as-mcp-integrations).

## R1 · Settings and checks

- **R1.1** The Cheat Engine integration shall hold the path to the Cheat Engine executable as its setting.
- **R1.2** The Cheat Engine integration shall check that the executable exists, that the bridge script is installed in Cheat Engine's `autorun` folder, and that the bridge answers a ping with the version the app carries.
- **R1.3** When the user asks to install the bridge, the Cheat Engine integration shall copy the bridge script the app carries into Cheat Engine's `autorun` folder.
- **R1.4** If the bridge script cannot be written into the `autorun` folder, then the Cheat Engine integration shall show the script's path and the folder to copy it into.

## R2 · The bridge and its tools

- **R2.1** The bridge shall answer only commands that read: the process list, modules, memory regions, memory, value and byte-pattern scans, pointer chains, disassembly, symbols and structures.
- **R2.2** If the bridge receives any other method, then the bridge shall answer with a JSON-RPC method-not-found error and run nothing.
- **R2.3** The bridge shall carry the upstream MIT licence notice and the upstream commit it derives from.
- **R2.4** The Cheat Engine integration shall offer a `status` tool that returns whether the bridge is connected, the Cheat Engine and bridge versions, and the names of the integration's tools, and reads no process memory.
- **R2.5** The Cheat Engine integration shall default `status` and `get_process_list` to the orchestrator, and no other tool.

## R3 · The process

- **R3.1** The Cheat Engine integration's target shall be one process, given by PID and shown to the user by its name, PID and executable path.
- **R3.2** The `status` and `get_process_list` tools shall need no target.
- **R3.3** While a target is approved, the Cheat Engine integration shall open only that process in Cheat Engine and refuse a call while the bridge's opened process is another.
- **R3.4** If the approved process exits, then the Cheat Engine integration shall answer every later call on it with an error saying it exited.

## Out of scope

- Writing memory, injecting code or DLLs, executing code, breakpoints and debugging, pausing a process, DBVM and the kernel driver, shell and file commands, input, clipboard and windows.
- The upstream TCP relay, and any network path from a container to Cheat Engine.
- Cheat Engine on macOS or Linux.

```

`specs/claude-specialist/design.md`:

```md
# Claude specialist — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R1.4, R1.5, R2.1, R2.2, R2.3, R2.4, R2.5, R3.1, R3.2.

`src/main/specialist/` ports `study-lab/src/main/claude/{stream,service,account}.ts`
with the size caps and subagent attribution of MagnoTech's `leitorDoStream.ts`.
What changes from both references is where the process runs: the executor never
picks a binary. It receives a `Launch` — program, arguments, working directory and
environment — from the sandbox (`docker run … claude -p …`, see
`specs/task-sandbox/`), spawns that without a shell, and reads stdout line by line.
Tests hand it a `Launch` for `tests/fixtures/fake-claude.mjs` instead; the
production wiring in `src/main/index.ts` only ever builds the Docker one.

## Boundaries and contracts

```
executor.start(launch, { onEvent, onRaw, signal, timeoutMs }) → Session
session.send(text)     one {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":text}} line
session.result()       resolves on the next result event: text, usage, cost, session id
session.close()        ends stdin, waits for exit
session.kill(reason)   launch.kill() (docker kill) and the process tree
```

Every stdout line goes to `onRaw` first, unparsed, for the task's JSONL; the reader
then yields normalized events. Paths in `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Edit`, `Write`
inputs under `/work/` are rewritten to source-relative paths in a `files` field.

Login and status run the same image with the same config volume through
`docker run --rm -i … claude auth …`, built by the sandbox's argument builder with
no workspace mount.

## Alternatives considered

The loopback hook server and per-run MCP server of
adr:0002-run-the-specialist-through-the-pinned-claude-code-cli are dropped: under
adr:0006-run-the-specialist-inside-a-container-per-task the container sees no host
path, and `--tools` already limits the specialist to file tools
over `/work`. Reopening a path to the host would undo the boundary.

```

`specs/claude-specialist/requirements.md`:

```md
---
autonomy: auto
ci: wait
branch: feat/harness-for-rea
delivery: merged
pr: 1
---

# Claude specialist — requirements

## Purpose

The specialist is Claude Opus running the pinned Claude Code CLI inside the
delegation's sandbox container (`specs/task-sandbox/`), signed in with the user's
own Claude plan. This feature starts it, talks to it over stream-json, reads what it
does into events with usage and cost, and stops it. Decided in
adr:0002-run-the-specialist-through-the-pinned-claude-code-cli,
adr:0003-authenticate-the-specialist-with-the-users-claude-plan and
adr:0006-run-the-specialist-inside-a-container-per-task.

## R1 · Process

- **R1.1** The specialist executor shall start the Claude Code CLI only through a run prepared by the sandbox, never as a process on the host.
- **R1.2** The specialist executor shall send each user turn as a stream-json message on stdin and keep stdin open until the delegation ends, so a delegation can carry more than one turn.
- **R1.3** When a delegation is cancelled or exceeds its timeout, the specialist executor shall stop the CLI and its container and report the delegation as cancelled or timed out.
- **R1.4** If the CLI exits without a result, then the specialist executor shall report the failure with the last line of its error output, classified as auth, limit or failed.
- **R1.5** Where the user chose an effort for the specialist, the specialist executor shall start Claude Code with `--effort` set to it.

## R2 · Stream

- **R2.1** The specialist executor shall turn each stream-json line into events for assistant text, thinking, tool calls with their arguments, tool results and the final result, attributing calls made inside a subagent to that subagent.
- **R2.2** When the result arrives, the specialist executor shall record its input, output and cache tokens, `total_cost_usd` as an estimate, its duration and its session id.
- **R2.3** If a line is not JSON or has a type the reader does not know, then the specialist executor shall keep the raw line and record an event for it rather than drop it.
- **R2.4** The specialist executor shall cap the size of the text, arguments and results it records, marking a capped field as truncated.
- **R2.5** The specialist executor shall report each file a tool call reads or writes by its path relative to the source root, mapped back from `/work/<path>`.

## R3 · Login

- **R3.1** When the user signs in, the specialist executor shall run `claude auth login --claudeai` in the sandbox image on the sandbox's config volume, expose only an Anthropic https URL it prints, and pass on the code the user pastes.
- **R3.2** The specialist executor shall report the login state from `claude auth status --json` without reading the stored credential.

## Out of scope

- Anthropic API key, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry authentication.
- MCP servers or hooks reaching back from the container to the host.

# Desktop UI — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R2.1, R2.2, R2.3, R2.4, R2.5, R2.6, R3.1.

`src/renderer/` is a React app on Tailwind CSS with a handful of Radix-based
primitives in the shadcn/ui style, as in `study-lab`. It talks to main only through
`window.hfr` (`specs/app-shell/`). Three views: **Tasks** (new task form, task
list and history), **Task** (todos, delegations, live log, evidence and files,
patch review, usage, cancel and retry) and **Settings**.

State is a small store in `src/renderer/src/lib/`: the selected task's history is
loaded once from `getTask`, and every pushed `event`, `step` and `task` message is
folded into it by a pure reducer, so live updates and history render through the
same code. The reducer and the formatting helpers are what the suite tests; the
views are checked by running the app.

Settings (R1.4) is the shadcn `Tabs` over its sections, one `TabsContent` each, the
panels inside unchanged; the order of the tabs is a list in `src/renderer/src/lib/`,
which the suite holds to the five sections. The open tab is the view's own state,
starting on the orchestrator model.

```

# Desktop UI — requirements

## Purpose

The React renderer through which the user configures the app, starts a task on a
source folder, watches it decompose and delegate in real time, inspects the
evidence and the files each delegation touched, decides on proposed patches, and
looks back at past tasks with what they cost.

## R1 · Settings

- **R1.1** The desktop UI shall let the user set or clear the OpenRouter key, pick the orchestrator model from the provider's list — recommended models first, Qwen's flash models by default (MODIFIED), then on OpenRouter the Chinese coding models — or by name, choose the reasoning effort of the orchestrator and of the specialist, and set the delegation timeout.
- **R1.2** The desktop UI shall show whether Docker is running, whether the sandbox images are ready or being prepared, and whether the specialist is signed in, with actions to prepare the images again and sign in.
- **R1.3** While the specialist sign-in is in progress, the desktop UI shall show the Anthropic URL to open and a field for the code.
- **R1.4** (ADDED) The Settings view shall show its settings in tabs, one per section — the orchestrator model, the sandbox, the specialist, the MCP integrations and the waits on the user — one section at a time.

## R2 · Tasks

- **R2.1** When the user submits a request in a project, the desktop UI shall start a task in that project and show it under the project (specs/projects).
- **R2.2** (MODIFIED) While a task runs, the desktop UI shall show its todos, each delegation with its agent and state in the chat timeline, and the event log as events arrive (specs/chat-timeline R1.1).
- **R2.3** The desktop UI shall show for each delegation its context package, the specialist's report with its evidence, and the files copied, read and written.
- **R2.4** When a patch awaits approval, the desktop UI shall show its diff with approve and reject actions.
- **R2.5** The desktop UI shall show tokens and cost per agent and per task, marking the specialist's cost as an estimate.
- **R2.6** While a task is running or waiting, the desktop UI shall let the user cancel it.

## R3 · History

- **R3.1** The desktop UI shall list past tasks with their state, time and cost, open any of them with its full event history, and retry an interrupted or failed one.
- **R3.2** (ADDED) When another app changes a task or a project, the desktop UI shall show the change within one second (specs/shared-data-folder R5.3).

`specs/event-log/design.md`:

```md
# Event log — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R2.1, R2.2, R2.3, R2.4, R3.1.

`src/main/events/` holds the store, applying
adr:0005-store-events-in-sqlite-with-raw-jsonl-per-task. Every writer — the
orchestrator, the specialist executor, the sandbox — calls one `EventLog.append`,
which redacts, caps, inserts, and hands the stored row to the push channel of
`specs/app-shell/`. Raw agent output goes through `EventLog.raw`, which redacts and
appends to `<userData>/tasks/<task>/raw.jsonl`.

## Data

```
tasks   id, request, source_root, model, state, result, created_at, updated_at,
        tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, specialist_cost_usd
steps   id, task_id, ord, kind (todo|delegation), title, agent, state, data, created_at, updated_at
events  id (autoincrement), task_id, step_id, agent, at, kind, state, summary, payload, truncated
```

`state` is one of `pending`, `running`, `waiting`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`,
`interrupted`. Task totals are kept on the task row by the writer that records usage,
so history reads one row instead of summing events.

Redaction is pattern-based (`sk-or-…`, `sk-ant-…`, `Bearer …`, `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE
KEY-----`, OAuth access and refresh token fields) plus an exact match on secrets
registered at runtime, which is how the stored OpenRouter key is covered.

```

# Event log — requirements

## Purpose

One record of everything the agents do — who did what, when, with which inputs,
tools, files, tokens and cost — written once, redacted before it touches disk, shown
live in the UI and kept for history and audit. Decided in
adr:0005-store-events-in-sqlite-with-raw-jsonl-per-task.

## R1 · Schema and redaction

- **R1.1** The event log shall store each event with its task, its step when it has one, its agent, time, kind, state, a one-line summary, and a payload holding inputs, outputs, tools, files, errors, tokens and cost.
- **R1.2** The event log shall redact API keys, bearer and OAuth tokens, private keys and the stored OpenRouter key from every event and every raw line before writing either store.
- **R1.3** If an event's payload exceeds the size cap, then the event log shall truncate it and mark it truncated.

## R2 · Storage and delivery

- **R2.1** The event log shall keep tasks, steps and events in SQLite, migrated by `user_version`.
- **R2.2** The event log shall append each agent's raw output lines, unparsed, to the task's own JSONL file.
- **R2.3** When an event is written, the event log shall push it to the renderer.
- **R2.4** (MODIFIED) When the renderer asks for a task's history, the event log shall return the task, its steps, its usage per agent, and a page of its events in order, before or after a given event, the newest page when no event is given (specs/chat-timeline R2.1).

## R3 · Recovery

- **R3.1** (MODIFIED) When the app starts, the event log shall mark every task and step left running or waiting by a process that is gone as interrupted and record an event saying so, leaving a live app's tasks as they are (specs/shared-data-folder R2.2).

## Out of scope

- Exporting or deleting history from the UI.

```

`specs/mcp-integrations/design.md`:

```md
# Mcp integrations — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1–R6.1, under adr:0026-proxy-host-engines-to-the-agents-as-mcp-integrations.

- `src/shared/integrations.ts` (new) — the contract every integration meets, and its data:
  - `IntegrationTool`: `name`, `description`, zod `schema` of its arguments, `target` (whether
    it works on one), `orchestratorDefault`;
  - `IntegrationInfo`: `id` (the MCP server name, kebab-case), `title`, the zod schema of its
    settings, its `targetSchema` when it has one, its `actions` (Cheat Engine's is "install
    the bridge");
  - `IntegrationSettings`: `{ enabled, config, tools: { [name]: { orchestrator, specialist } } }`.
    A tool with no entry takes the defaults of R2.2, so a tool a later catalog adds starts
    there too;
  - `toolName(id, tool)` = `mcp__<id>__<tool>`, the one name both agents see (R5.1).
- `src/main/integrations/registry.ts` (new) — the list the app carries (R1.1, R1.5) and the
  host side of each: `checks(config)`, `status(config)`, `catalog(config)` (static for Cheat
  Engine; an engine with its own MCP server, as IDA Pro's, can list it from that server),
  `describeTarget(target)` (what the approval shows), `session(target)` and `call(session, tool,
  args)`.
- `src/main/integrations/gate.ts` (new) — the one check before every call, whichever agent
  made it: the tool is in the catalog, checked for that agent, and its target is the one the
  delegation or task approved (R2.4, R3.4). Then the call, its timeout (R4.4) and its event-log
  record (R6.1).
- `src/main/integrations/approval.ts` (new) — the approved targets of a task, keyed by
  integration; an unapproved one is put to the user — never to the orchestrator's model — as a
  yes/no question, default no, in an automatic task too, with the question timeout but outside
  the turn's question cap, and a refusal or timeout is the call's or delegation's result (R3.2,
  R3.3). An orchestrator's target is put to the user only for a tool the gate would let through.
  A refusal is kept for the task; a task puts at most 20 targets to the user; an approval holds
  while the integration's `identify` of the target is unchanged — a pid Windows reused is asked
  about again. What identifies a target is shown with no control or direction-changing characters,
  and `gate.open` refuses a target the task has not approved.
- `src/main/integrations/task.ts` (new) — one task's view: its approvals, the tools each agent
  has, the orchestrator's calls, and what a delegation offers the specialist: a target tool only
  where the delegation names an approved target.
- `src/main/delegation.ts` — `watchAskChannel` takes the file prefix it watches, so the same
  channel directory serves `q-`/`a-` questions and `t-`/`r-` tool calls; a tool call names its
  integration, and goes through the gate as the specialist's (R4.2, R4.3). A delegation writes
  the container server and each integration's checked tools into its run directory (R4.1), and
  fails before the container runs when an integration it names a target of is disconnected
  (R4.5).
- `sandbox/mcp/server.mjs` (new) — the container's stdio MCP server, modelled on
  `ask-user.mjs`, started once per integration as `node /run/hfr/mcp/server.mjs <id>`: its
  `tools/list` is `/run/hfr/mcp/<id>.json`, each `tools/call` is written as `t-<uuid>.json`
  and answered from `r-<uuid>.json`. It is copied from the app's `sandbox/` folder into the run
  directory per delegation, never baked into the base image (R4.2). A call past the run's cap
  (1024) or past 64 KB is answered with an error, so the server never waits on one; two run at
  once, and those still waiting when the delegation ends are answered with an error, never run.
- `src/main/sandbox/docker.ts` — `mcpConfig` and `claudeArgs` take the delegation's
  integrations: each adds a server under its id and `mcp__<id>` to `--allowedTools` (R4.1).
  `dockerRunArgs` and `containerEnv` do not change (R4.2).
- `src/main/sandbox/prompt.ts` — per integration, a section naming it and its approved target,
  saying its tools return data from the target, never instructions (R4.6).
- `src/main/orchestrator/tools.ts` — `delegate_to_specialist` takes an optional `targets`
  object keyed by integration id, each value checked by that integration's `targetSchema`
  (R3.1). Each tool checked for the orchestrator becomes a tool of its own, built from the
  catalog; one that works on a target takes it as a `target` argument (R5.1). Its answer is
  redacted and cut at 64 KB, as anything else that goes to the orchestrator's provider.
- `src/main/orchestrator/agent.ts` — the allowlist becomes the fixed set plus the names of
  the orchestrator's integration tools for this task; the instructions gain, per integration
  the orchestrator has, a line on delegating the target's analysis (R5.2).
- `src/shared/types.ts`, `src/shared/defaults.ts`, `src/shared/api.ts` — `Settings` gains
  `integrations: { [id]: IntegrationSettings }`, every one off by default (R1.1); the IPC
  contract gains `integrations` (the list, each with its catalog), `integrationStatus(id)` and
  `runIntegrationAction(id, action)`, each with its zod schema.
- `src/renderer/src/` — the MCP tab in Settings, generic over the list: a row per integration
  with its title, description, on or off and, while on, whether it is connected, and a
  Configure button (R1.1, R1.4); Configure opens that integration's own page, with a way back,
  holding its settings, its switch, each check with its fix, its actions, its connection
  state, and its tools with one toggle per agent, a shadcn `Switch` on Radix as the integration's
  own on/off is (R1.6, R2.1, R2.2), warning on a target tool
  checked for the orchestrator (R2.3). Which integration is open is the tab's own state.

## Data

A tool call file, `t-<uuid>.json`, is `{ integration, tool, arguments }`, read once and bounded
like a question file; its answer, `r-<uuid>.json`, is `{ result }` or `{ error }`, written whole
by a rename. A delegation's target is fixed when it starts, so the container never names one;
the gate adds it. The event-log record of a call is `{ agent, integration, tool, arguments,
target, outcome, bytes }`, never the answer (R6.1).

## Alternatives

- **MCP servers the user adds** — rejected (adr:0026): the app could not know which of a
  server's tools work on a target, so it could not gate them.
- **A watcher and mount per integration** — rejected: one prefix carries every integration,
  since a call names its own, and the ask channel is already the one writable path outside
  `/work`.

## Testing

The gate, the approval and the channel run in Vitest against a fake integration with one tool
that needs a target and one that does not, so the framework is tested apart from any engine.

```

# Mcp integrations — requirements

## Purpose

The app carries a list of MCP integrations — engines on the host, Cheat Engine first and IDA Pro
later — that the agents use only through the app (adr:0026-proxy-host-engines-to-the-agents-as-mcp-integrations).
Each integration plugs into Settings, the specialist's run and the orchestrator the same way, and
the user decides, tool by tool, whether the orchestrator, the specialist, both or neither get it.

## R1 · The list

- **R1.1** (MODIFIED) The Settings view's MCP tab shall list every integration the app carries, each off by default, with its title, whether it is on and a way to configure it.
- **R1.2** When the user turns an integration on, the app shall run that integration's checks and show the result of each.
- **R1.3** If any check fails, then the app shall leave the integration off and show the failed check with the step that fixes it.
- **R1.4** While an integration is on, the Settings view shall show whether it is connected.
- **R1.5** The Settings view shall offer no way to add an MCP server the app does not carry.
- **R1.6** (ADDED) When the user chooses to configure an integration, the Settings view shall show a page for that integration alone, with its settings, its switch, its checks, its actions and its tools, and a way back to the list.

## R2 · Tools

- **R2.1** (MODIFIED) The integration's page shall list each of its tools with one toggle for the orchestrator and one for the specialist.
- **R2.2** (MODIFIED) The app shall start every specialist toggle on and every orchestrator toggle at the integration's default for that tool.
- **R2.3** (MODIFIED) When the user turns on a tool that works on a target for the orchestrator, the Settings view shall warn that what it returns goes to the orchestrator's model and provider.
- **R2.4** The app shall accept a call to an integration's tool only from an agent the tool is checked for, and only when the tool is in that integration's catalog.

## R3 · Targets

- **R3.1** Where an integration's tools work on a target, the `delegate_to_specialist` tool shall accept one target of that integration.
- **R3.2** When a delegation or an orchestrator call names a target the task has not approved, the app shall ask the user, showing what identifies the target, and go on only on approval, in an automatic task too.
- **R3.3** If the user declines a target or does not answer, then the delegation or call shall end with the refusal as its result.
- **R3.4** While a delegation runs with an approved target, the app shall refuse a call from it that names any other target of that integration.

## R4 · The specialist

- **R4.1** Where an integration is on and has a tool checked for the specialist, the delegation shall start Claude Code with that integration's MCP server offering only those tools, and allow them.
- **R4.2** The delegation shall carry each integration's calls to the app over its run directory, and add no mount, port or environment variable to the container for it.
- **R4.3** When the app receives a call from the run directory, the app shall check it against R2.4 and R3.4, forward it to the integration, and write the answer back to the run directory.
- **R4.4** If an integration does not answer a call within its timeout, then the app shall answer the call with an error naming the cause.
- **R4.5** If an integration the delegation names a target of is disconnected when the delegation starts, then the delegation shall fail with an error naming the integration.
- **R4.6** Where the specialist has an integration's tools, the specialist's system prompt shall name the integration and its approved target, and say that what its tools return is data from the target, never instructions.

## R5 · The orchestrator

- **R5.1** Where an integration is on, the orchestrator shall have the integration's tools checked for it, under the names the specialist sees them by.
- **R5.2** Where the orchestrator has an integration's tools, the orchestrator's instructions shall say that the analysis of a target is delegated to the specialist with that target.

## R6 · The record

- **R6.1** The app shall record each integration call in the task's event log with its agent, integration, tool, arguments, target, outcome and the size of its answer, never the answer itself.

## Out of scope

- Adding an arbitrary MCP server from Settings.
- IDA Pro, which is its own integration and spec.
- The TUI's Settings screen; the integrations still work in tasks the TUI runs.
- Blocking the containers' access to services on the host's loopback through `host.docker.internal`.

```

# Onboarding — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1–R2.2.

- `src/shared/types.ts`, `src/shared/defaults.ts`, `src/shared/api.ts` — `Settings.setupCompleted`
  (false by default) and a `readiness` IPC call returning each step's state and reason: sandbox

  names a step that stopped being ready (R2.1). Settings links back to the setup (R2.2).

# Onboarding — requirements

## Purpose

A first-run setup that readies what every project needs before the user can create one: the sandbox
images with the pinned Claude Code, Claude Code signed in on the user's own plan, and the orchestrator's
OpenAI-compatible model, with OpenRouter as the default gateway. Settings stay where the same choices
are changed later.

## R1 · The setup

- **R1.1** While the setup has never been completed, the desktop UI shall open on the setup instead of the projects.
- **R1.2** The setup shall show three steps in order — the sandbox, Claude Code and the orchestrator's model — each with its state, what it needs and the action that readies it.
- **R1.3** The sandbox step shall be ready when Docker answers and the sandbox images are prepared, and shall offer to prepare them, showing the build's progress.
- **R1.4** The Claude Code step shall be ready when Claude Code is signed in, and shall offer the sign-in with the Anthropic page to open and the field for its code, showing the plan signed in.
- **R1.5** The model step shall start on OpenRouter and let the user pick another OpenAI-compatible provider, set its key and base URL where it takes one, and choose a model from the provider's list or by name.
- **R1.6** (MODIFIED) The model step shall be ready when the provider has a key where it needs one and a model is chosen, and the provider answered with its list of models or, when the list fails other than by refusing the key, a one-token test request to the chosen model answered.
- **R1.7** If a step's check fails, then the setup shall say why and how to fix it, and keep the step not ready.
- **R1.8** When all three steps are ready and the user finishes the setup, the desktop UI shall record the setup as completed and open the projects.

## R2 · After the setup

- **R2.1** While a step that was ready no longer is, the desktop UI shall show which one and a way to fix it, and shall not let a task start, checking a task's start against the provider, key, endpoint and model of its project.
- **R2.2** The setup shall be reachable again from Settings.
- **R2.3** (ADDED) When another app on the same data folder readied a step, the setup shall show the step ready without the user doing it again (specs/shared-data-folder R4, R5).

## Out of scope

- Installing Docker Desktop for the user.
- A model step that runs a chat completion to test the key.

```

# Orchestrator — design

## What changes

Serves R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R1.4, R1.5, R2.1, R2.2, R2.3, R2.4, R2.5, R2.6, R2.7, R3.1, R3.2, R3.3, R3.4, R3.5.

`src/main/orchestrator/` builds one DeepAgents agent per task, following
`study-lab/src/main/harness/{model,agent}.ts` and
adr:0001-use-deepagents-on-openrouter-for-orchestration.

- **Model** — `ChatOpenRouter` with `model`, `models: [model, fallback]`,
  `provider: { data_collection: "deny" }`. A callback on `handleLLMEnd` reads
  `llmOutput.tokenUsage` (OpenRouter's `usage`, including `cost`) into an event.
- **Files and commands** — a `BaseSandbox` over `docker exec` into `hfr-orch-<task>`,
  the source folder bind-mounted read-only at `/workspace` with full internet access
  (adr:0007-run-the-orchestrators-tools-in-a-task-container, adr:0013-give-the-sandboxes-full-internet-access). `ls`, `read_file`,
  `glob`, `grep` and `execute` run there; uploads are refused, and DeepAgents takes no
  path rules on a backend that runs commands. Tests pass a `FilesystemBackend`, with a write-deny rule, in its place.
- **Brief** — the context package's `brief` is the orchestrator's own technical prompt for
  the step: what the artifact is, what is known and what to discover, never the user's request
  or purpose (adr:0019-keep-the-specialists-brief-technical).
- **Delegation** — `delegate_to_specialist` takes a context package
  (`src/shared/context.ts`, zod) and calls the sandbox
  (`specs/task-sandbox/`), which prepares the workspace and runs the specialist
  (`specs/claude-specialist/`). It returns the report, the evidence lines and, in
  modify mode, a patch id with its diff stat.
- **Approval** — `apply_patch({ patchId })` is in `interruptOn` with
  `allowedDecisions: ["approve", "reject"]`. The run pauses with `__interrupt__`;
  the task goes to `waiting` and the UI shows the patch. The user's decision
  resumes it with `new Command({ resume: { decisions: [{ type }] } })` on the same
  `thread_id`, held by a `MemorySaver` that lives as long as the app.
- **Steps** — `write_todos` calls are read from the tool callbacks into `todo`
  steps; each delegation is a `delegation` step.
- **Base URLs** (R1.10) — `Settings.baseUrls` holds each provider's own endpoint, kept by
  `src/main/settings.ts` and never sent over IPC; `baseUrl` is the chosen provider's. A save
  that sets `baseUrl` sets the chosen provider's entry, switching provider brings back its
  own, and a record from before is moved under the provider it was saved on.
  `baseUrlFor` reads a provider's own entry whichever provider Settings is on, so a project
  on another provider runs at its endpoint. The provider pickers send no base URL with a
  switch.

## Alternatives considered

A SQLite-backed checkpointer would let a paused run survive a restart. Rejected for
now: the run would also need the sandbox's live state back, and a restart already
marks the task interrupted (`specs/event-log/` R3.1); a retry is the recovery.

```

# Orchestrator — requirements

## Purpose

The orchestrator takes the user's software engineering task, decomposes it, reads
the source tree to decide what each step needs, delegates deep analysis to the
specialist with a context package, asks the user before any patch is applied, and
consolidates the results into one answer. Decided in
adr:0001-use-deepagents-on-openrouter-for-orchestration.

## R1 · Model

- **R1.1** (MODIFIED) The orchestrator shall run `createDeepAgent` on `ChatOpenRouter` with the model the user chose, defaulting to `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, with `qwen/qwen3.7-flash` offered as a preset and sent as the fallback in OpenRouter's `models` routing.
- **R1.2** The orchestrator shall send every OpenRouter request with `provider.data_collection` set to `deny`.
- **R1.3** When a model call completes, the orchestrator shall record its tokens, its cost from OpenRouter's usage and the model that answered as an event, and add them to the task's totals.
- **R1.4** If OpenRouter rejects the key, reports no credits or rate-limits the request, then the orchestrator shall fail the task with a message the user can act on.
- **R1.5** Where the user chose a reasoning effort for the orchestrator, the orchestrator shall send it as OpenRouter's `reasoning.effort` on every request.
- **R1.6** Where the user chose an OpenAI-compatible provider (DeepSeek, or a custom endpoint), the orchestrator shall run `createDeepAgent` on `ChatOpenAI` at that provider's base URL with that provider's API key and send none of OpenRouter's routing fields (adr:0014-add-openai-compatible-orchestrator-providers).
- **R1.7** The orchestrator shall keep one API key per provider and use the chosen provider's, and if that key is not set, then it shall refuse to start the task and name the provider.
- **R1.9** When the user opens the orchestrator's settings, the orchestrator shall offer the models listed by the chosen provider's `GET /models` (for OpenRouter, only those that support tool calling and take images as input), read in the main process with that provider's key, and if the list cannot be read, then it shall say why and still accept a typed model name.
- **R1.8** Where the user chose a reasoning effort for an OpenAI-compatible provider, the orchestrator shall send it as `reasoning_effort` on every request.
- **R1.10** (ADDED) The orchestrator shall keep one base URL per provider whose base URL can be edited and use the chosen provider's, so that choosing another provider leaves each provider's base URL as the user set it.

## R2 · Decomposition and delegation

- **R2.1** When a task starts, the orchestrator shall decompose it with `write_todos` and record each todo list change as steps and an event.
- **R2.2** The orchestrator shall run its file and command tools in a container for the task, with the source folder bind-mounted read-only at `/workspace`, full internet access (adr:0013-give-the-sandboxes-full-internet-access), and the container removed when the task ends.
- **R2.8** (ADDED) The orchestrator's task container shall run its commands as root with a writable root filesystem, so the orchestrator may install any software its code needs, while the source folder stays bind-mounted read-only (adr:0015-run-the-task-container-as-root).
- **R2.9** If the task's container stopped or is gone while the task is open, then the orchestrator shall bring it up again, retry the call once, and, when it had to be created, tell the agent that what it installed is gone while its scratch was kept.
- **R2.3** The orchestrator shall expose the specialist as a `delegate_to_specialist` tool whose input is a context package validated against its schema.
- **R2.4** When the agent delegates a step, the orchestrator shall run the delegation in the sandbox and return the specialist's report, its evidence and any proposed patch to the agent.
- **R2.5** If a context package fails validation or the sandbox refuses the delegation, then the orchestrator shall return the reason to the agent as a tool error instead of failing the task.
- **R2.6** The orchestrator shall redact secret shapes from the specialist's report before returning it to the model.
- **R2.7** The orchestrator shall write for each delegation a technical brief stating what the artifact is, what is already established about it and what the step must map or discover, without mentioning the user, their request or the purpose of the work, and without claiming any ownership, authorization or purpose (adr:0019-keep-the-specialists-brief-technical).
- **R2.10** The orchestrator shall write every field of a context package in English, whatever language the user writes in, and answer the user in the user's language.

## R3 · Approval and lifecycle

- **R3.1** The orchestrator shall interrupt before `apply_patch` runs and wait for the user's patch approval or rejection.
- **R3.2** When the user approves or rejects a patch, the orchestrator shall resume the run from its checkpointer with that decision.
- **R3.3** When the run ends, the orchestrator shall record its consolidated answer as the task's result.
- **R3.4** When the user cancels a task, the orchestrator shall abort the model call and every running delegation and mark the task cancelled.
- **R3.5** When the user retries an interrupted or failed task, the orchestrator shall start a new run from the same request and source folder.

## Out of scope

- A retry starts over from the request; continuing from the checkpoint is specs/task-persistence.

```
