`src/main/sandbox/specialistbox.ts`:

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto"
import { existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { getDb } from "../db"
import type { EventLog } from "../events/log"
import { identity, limitArgs, loginVolume, mountSource, SPECIALIST_IMAGE } from "./docker"
import { bringUp, labelled, OUTPUT_CAP, type ExecBuffer } from "./taskbox"
import {
  addFiles,
  askDir,
  createWorkspace,
  discardWorkspace,
  readManifest,
  workspaceDirs,
  type CopiedFile,
  type PreparedFile,
  type Workspace,
} from "./workspace"

/*
  The sandboxes the orchestrator creates for the specialist (adr:0016-let-the-orchestrator-run-the-specialists-sandbox,
  specs/specialist-sandbox): one long-lived root container per sandbox, with the limits the orchestrator chose,
  its workspace at /work, files copied in from the source folder or the orchestrator's scratch, commands run in it
  as root, delegations run in it one at a time, and its disk watched against its limit. One `SpecialistBoxes` per
  task. A sandbox is recorded in the database and its folders live in the task's own, so it is stopped at the
  task's end, brought up again when the task reopens, and created again over the same folders when Docker no
  longer has it; only deleting the task removes it
  (adr:0017-keep-a-tasks-conversation-containers-and-files-until-it-is-deleted, specs/task-persistence R3).
*/

const MB = 1024 * 1024
/** How often a running sandbox's disk is measured besides after each call (specs/specialist-sandbox R3.2). */
export const DISK_EVERY_MS = 15_000
/** A command's time limit when the orchestrator gives none, and the most it may give (R2.4). */
export const COMMAND_DEFAULT_S = 600
export const COMMAND_MAX_S = 86_400

/** What the orchestrator chose; each one left out is no limit, and no disk watch without `diskMb` (R1.5). */
export interface BoxLimits {
  cpus?: number
  memoryMb?: number
  diskMb?: number
  pidsLimit?: number
}

export interface Box {
  id: string
  name: string
  ws: Workspace
  limits: BoxLimits
  /** a delegation runs in it */
  busy: boolean
  /** why it was stopped, once it was */
  stopped: string | null
  timer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null
  /** the container runs in this process; false for one recorded by an earlier run of the task */
  up: boolean
  /** where the specialist keeps what it extracts and builds, bound at /root/out */
  outDir: string
  /** the task that used it last, which a watch that stops it reports against */
  lastTask?: string
}

/** A call the orchestrator made that the sandbox service refuses; its message goes back to the orchestrator. */
export class SandboxError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message)
    this.name = "SandboxError"
  }
}

export function sandboxName(id: string): string {
  return `hfr-sbx-${id}`
}

/**
  `docker run` for a sandbox (R1.1–R1.3): root with the install capabilities and a writable root, Docker's default
  network, the login volume, and only its workspace, run directory, ask channel and output folder bound; never
  privileged, never the Docker socket. `/tmp` is no tmpfs, so what is written there counts toward the disk. Kept
  when stopped (specs/task-persistence R3.4).
*/
export function sandboxArgs(name: string, ws: Workspace, limits: BoxLimits, outDir: string): string[] {
  return [
    "run",
    "-d",
    "--name",
    name,
    "--hostname",
    "sandbox",
    // a PID 1 that reaps what `docker exec` and `timeout` leave behind
    "--init",
    ...identity(true),
    ...limitArgs(limits),
    ...loginVolume(),
    "--mount",
    `type=bind,source=${mountSource(ws.workspace)},target=/work`,
    "--mount",
    `type=bind,source=${mountSource(ws.runDir)},target=/run/hfr,readonly`,
    "--mount",
    `type=bind,source=${mountSource(askDir(ws.runDir))},target=/run/hfr-ask`,
    "--mount",
    `type=bind,source=${mountSource(outDir)},target=/root/out`,
    "-w",
    "/work",
    "--entrypoint",
    "sleep",
    SPECIALIST_IMAGE,
    "infinity",
  ]
}

/** Most entries one measurement of a workspace visits; past it the size is unknown. */
export const FOLDER_ENTRY_CAP = 200_000

/**
  Bytes of regular files under a folder, links not followed, or null when it cannot be told: the sandbox changes
  the folder while it is walked, so an entry gone between listing and reading is skipped, and a tree past the
  entry cap is not walked to its end on the app's main thread.
*/
export function folderSize(dir: string, budget = { entries: FOLDER_ENTRY_CAP }): number | null {
  let total = 0
  let names: string[] = []
  try {
    names = readdirSync(dir)
  } catch {
    return 0
  }
  for (const name of names) {
    if (--budget.entries < 0) return null
    let st
    try {
      st = lstatSync(join(dir, name))
    } catch {
      continue
    }
    if (st.isDirectory()) {
      const sub = folderSize(join(dir, name), budget)
      if (sub === null) return null
      total += sub
    } else if (st.isFile()) total += st.size
  }
  return total
}

/** The limits as the orchestrator chose them, for the event log. */
export function describeLimits(l: BoxLimits): string {
  const part = (v: number | undefined, unit: string) => (v === undefined ? `no ${unit} limit` : `${v} ${unit}`)
  return [part(l.cpus, "CPU"), part(l.memoryMb, "MB memory"), part(l.diskMb, "MB disk"), part(l.pidsLimit, "processes")].join(", ")
}

const lastLine = (s: string) => s.trim().split("\n").pop()?.trim() ?? ""

export interface BoxesDeps {
  exec: ExecBuffer
  log: EventLog
  /** the project's folder, where each sandbox's folders live (specs/projects R2.3) */
  dir: string
  sourceRoot: string
  /** the project whose tasks share these sandboxes */
  projectId: string
  everyMs?: number
  /** the task a call made without one is recorded against; none in the app, where every call names its task */
  actor?: string
  /** an earlier instance of the project's sandboxes still stopping: no Docker call is made before it settles */
  after?: Promise<void>
}

/** A project's sandboxes as one of its tasks uses them: every call is recorded against that task. */
export interface TaskSandboxes {
  create(limits: BoxLimits): Promise<Box>
  usable(id: string): Box
  copy(id: string, requested: string[], prepared: PreparedFile[]): Promise<CopiedFile[] & { notice?: string }>
  run(id: string, command: string, timeoutS?: number): Promise<{ output: string; exitCode: number; truncated: boolean }>
  hold(id: string): Promise<{ box: Box; release: () => Promise<void> }>
  destroy(id: string): Promise<void>
  ids(): string[]
}

/** A sandbox created again over its folders after Docker lost it: what the orchestrator is told. */
export const recreated = (id: string) => `[Sandbox ${id} was created again: /work and /root/out were kept, anything installed is gone.]`

export class SpecialistBoxes {
  private readonly boxes = new Map<string, Box>()
  private readonly d: BoxesDeps
  /** the task ended: a sandbox still starting is stopped rather than kept running */
  private ended = false

  /** The project's sandboxes, those an earlier run of any of its tasks recorded included (R3.6, specs/projects R2.3). */
  constructor(deps: BoxesDeps) {
    this.d = deps
    for (const r of getDb()
      .prepare(
        "SELECT s.id, s.created_by, s.limits, t.id AS task FROM sandboxes s LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.id = s.created_by WHERE s.project_id = ? ORDER BY s.created_at",
      )
      .all(deps.projectId) as Record<string, unknown>[]) {
      const id = String(r.id)
      // A sandbox from before projects lives under the folder of the task that created it (specs/projects R3.3).
      const dirs = [workspaceDirs(deps.dir, id), workspaceDirs(join(deps.dir, "tasks", String(r.created_by)), id)].find((d) => existsSync(d.workspace))
      if (!dirs) continue
      const ws: Workspace = { id, ...dirs, files: [] }
      // A snapshot that cannot be read leaves the sandbox reachable, its files unknown until copied again.
      let manifest: Record<string, string> = {}
      try {
        manifest = readManifest(ws.snapshot)
      } catch {
        manifest = {}
      }
      for (const [path, sha256] of Object.entries(manifest)) ws.files.push({ path, sha256, size: 0 })
      const box = this.box(id, ws, JSON.parse(String(r.limits)) as BoxLimits, false)
      // What happens to it before a task uses it again, a disk stop included, is recorded against the task that made it.
      if (r.task) box.lastTask = String(r.task)
      this.boxes.set(id, box)
    }
  }

  /** Docker, once an earlier instance of these sandboxes finished stopping. */
  private readonly exec: ExecBuffer = async (args, timeoutMs, input) => {
    await this.d.after
    return this.d.exec(args, timeoutMs, input)
  }

  private box(id: string, ws: Workspace, limits: BoxLimits, up: boolean): Box {
    return { id, name: sandboxName(id), ws, limits, busy: false, stopped: null, timer: null, up, outDir: ws.out }
  }

  /** What happened to a sandbox, recorded against the task that did it, or the last one that used it. */
  private event(kind: string, summary: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>, taskId?: string, box?: Box) {
    const who = taskId ?? box?.lastTask ?? this.d.actor
    if (box && taskId) box.lastTask = taskId
    if (who) this.d.log.append({ taskId: who, agent: "sandbox", kind, summary, payload })
  }

  /** The sandboxes as one task uses them, so each call is recorded against it. */
  forTask(taskId: string): TaskSandboxes {
    return {
      create: (limits) => this.create(limits, taskId),
      usable: (id) => this.usable(id),
      copy: (id, requested, prepared) => this.copy(id, requested, prepared, taskId),
      run: (id, command, timeoutS) => this.run(id, command, timeoutS, taskId),
      hold: (id) => this.hold(id),
      destroy: (id) => this.destroy(id, taskId),
      ids: () => this.ids(),
    }
  }

  /** Only a disk limit is watched; without one the sandbox takes what Docker has (R1.5). */
  private watch(box: Box) {
    if (box.limits.diskMb === undefined || box.timer) return
    box.timer = setInterval(() => void this.checkDisk(box).catch(() => undefined), this.d.everyMs ?? DISK_EVERY_MS)
    box.timer.unref?.()
  }

  /** Start a sandbox with the orchestrator's limits; Docker's refusal comes back as the error, leaving nothing (R1.1, R1.4). */
  async create(limits: BoxLimits, taskId?: string): Promise<Box> {
    const id = randomUUID()
    const ws = createWorkspace(this.d.dir, id)
    const box = this.box(id, ws, limits, true)
    mkdirSync(box.outDir, { recursive: true })
    // The workspace's folders, its output folder among them.
    const forget = () => discardWorkspace(this.d.dir, id)
    let args: string[]
    try {
      args = sandboxArgs(box.name, ws, limits, box.outDir)
    } catch (e) {
      forget()
      throw new SandboxError((e as Error).message)
    }
    const r = await this.exec(labelled(args))
    if (r.code !== 0 || this.ended) {
      await this.exec(["rm", "-f", box.name])
      forget()
      throw new SandboxError(
        r.code !== 0 ? `Docker did not start the sandbox: ${lastLine(r.stderr) || `exit ${r.code}`}` : "The task ended while the sandbox was starting.",
      )
    }
    getDb()
      .prepare("INSERT INTO sandboxes (id, project_id, created_by, limits, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")
      .run(id, this.d.projectId, taskId ?? null, JSON.stringify(limits), Date.now())
    this.watch(box)
    this.boxes.set(id, box)
    this.event("sandbox.created", `Created sandbox ${id}: ${describeLimits(limits)}`, { sandbox: id, ...limits }, taskId, box)
    return box
  }

  /** The sandbox by id, refusing one this task does not have or that was stopped (R2.8). */
  usable(id: string): Box {
    const box = this.boxes.get(id)
    if (!box) throw new SandboxError(`There is no sandbox ${id} in this project; create one with sandbox_create.`)
    if (box.stopped) throw new SandboxError(`Sandbox ${id} was stopped: ${box.stopped}. Destroy it and create another.`)
    return box
  }

  /**
    The sandbox, running: one recorded by an earlier run of the task is started, or created again over its folders
    when Docker no longer has it (specs/task-persistence R3.5); the notice says what the orchestrator lost.
  */
  async open(id: string): Promise<{ box: Box; notice: string }> {
    const box = this.usable(id)
    if (box.up) return { box, notice: "" }
    let created: boolean
    try {
      mkdirSync(box.outDir, { recursive: true })
      ;({ created } = await bringUp((args, t, input) => this.exec(args, t, input), box.name, sandboxArgs(box.name, box.ws, box.limits, box.outDir)))
    } catch (e) {
      throw new SandboxError(`Sandbox ${id} could not be brought up again: ${(e as Error).message}`)
    }
    box.up = true
    this.watch(box)
    this.event(
      "sandbox.reopened",
      created ? `Created sandbox ${id} again over its folders` : `Started sandbox ${id} again`,
      { sandbox: id, created },
      undefined,
      box,
    )
    return { box, notice: created ? recreated(id) : "" }
  }

  /** Copy files from the source folder and the scratch into /work, all or none, within the disk left (R2.1–R2.3). */
  async copy(id: string, requested: string[], prepared: PreparedFile[], taskId?: string): Promise<CopiedFile[] & { notice?: string }> {
    const { box, notice } = await this.open(id)
    const disk = box.limits.diskMb
    const used = disk === undefined ? 0 : await this.usage(box)
    // A size that cannot be told does not block a copy; the watch stops the sandbox if it passes the limit.
    const left = disk === undefined ? Infinity : Math.max(0, disk * MB - (used ?? 0))
    const files: CopiedFile[] & { notice?: string } = addFiles(box.ws, this.d.sourceRoot, requested, prepared, left, `${disk} MB disk limit of sandbox ${id}`)
    this.event(
      "sandbox.copy",
      `Copied ${files.length} file(s) into sandbox ${id}`,
      { sandbox: id, files: files.map((f) => ({ path: f.path, op: "copy" })), sha256: Object.fromEntries(files.map((f) => [f.path, f.sha256])) },
      taskId,
      box,
    )
    await this.checkDisk(box)
    if (notice) files.notice = notice
    return files
  }

  /** Run a command as root in /work, stopped at its time limit, its output capped (R2.4). */
  async run(id: string, command: string, timeoutS = COMMAND_DEFAULT_S, taskId?: string): Promise<{ output: string; exitCode: number; truncated: boolean }> {
    const { box, notice } = await this.open(id)
    const limit = Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.floor(timeoutS)), COMMAND_MAX_S)
    const r = await this.exec(["exec", "-w", "/work", box.name, "timeout", "-s", "KILL", String(limit), "sh", "-c", command], (limit + 10) * 1000)
    let output = (notice ? `${notice} ` : "") + r.stdout.toString("utf8") + r.stderr
    const truncated = r.overflow === true || output.length > OUTPUT_CAP
    if (truncated) output = output.slice(0, OUTPUT_CAP)
    this.event(
      "sandbox.exec",
      `Ran in sandbox ${id}: ${command.slice(0, 120)}`,
      { sandbox: id, command, exitCode: r.code, output: output.slice(0, 4000) },
      taskId,
      box,
    )
    await this.checkDisk(box)
    if (box.stopped) output += `\n[Sandbox ${id} was stopped: ${box.stopped}]`
    return { output, exitCode: r.code, truncated }
  }

  /**
    Bytes the sandbox uses: its container's writable layer plus its workspace and its output folder, both on the host
    (R3.1, specs/rea-native R2.4), or null when any cannot be told.
  */
  async usage(box: Box): Promise<number | null> {
    const r = await this.exec(["container", "inspect", "--size", "--format", "{{.SizeRw}}", box.name])
    const layer = r.code === 0 ? Number(r.stdout.toString("utf8").trim()) : NaN
    const work = folderSize(box.ws.workspace)
    const out = folderSize(box.outDir)
    return Number.isFinite(layer) && work !== null && out !== null ? layer + work + out : null
  }

  /** Measure the disk and stop the sandbox past its limit (R3.2, R3.3); a stopped sandbox is not measured again. */
  async checkDisk(box: Box): Promise<void> {
    const disk = box.limits.diskMb
    if (disk === undefined || box.stopped || !box.up || !this.boxes.has(box.id)) return
    const used = await this.usage(box)
    // Destroyed while measured, or not measurable this time: the next check decides.
    if (used === null || used <= disk * MB || box.stopped || !this.boxes.has(box.id)) return
    const usedMb = Math.ceil(used / MB)
    box.stopped = `it used ${usedMb} MB of disk, past its ${disk} MB limit`
    if (box.timer) clearInterval(box.timer)
    box.timer = null
    await this.exec(["kill", box.name])
    this.event("sandbox.stopped", `Stopped sandbox ${box.id}: ${box.stopped}`, { sandbox: box.id, usedMb, diskMb: box.limits.diskMb }, undefined, box)
  }

  /** Hold the sandbox, running, for one delegation; refused while another runs in it (specs/specialist-sandbox R4.2). */
  async hold(id: string): Promise<{ box: Box; release: () => Promise<void> }> {
    const box = this.usable(id)
    if (box.busy) throw new SandboxError(`Sandbox ${id} is already running a delegation; wait for it to end.`)
    box.busy = true
    try {
      await this.open(id)
    } catch (e) {
      box.busy = false
      throw e
    }
    let released = false
    return {
      box,
      // Once: the delegation releases on failure to read the sandbox's state, and again on its way out.
      release: async () => {
        if (released) return
        released = true
        box.busy = false
        await this.checkDisk(box)
      },
    }
  }

  /**
    Remove the sandbox's container and its record, keeping its folders for the task (R2.5, specs/task-persistence
    R4.3). The orchestrator cannot remove one a delegation runs in.
  */
  async destroy(id: string, taskId?: string): Promise<void> {
    const box = this.boxes.get(id)
    if (!box) throw new SandboxError(`There is no sandbox ${id} in this project.`)
    if (box.busy) throw new SandboxError(`Sandbox ${id} is running a delegation; destroy it once the delegation ends.`)
    this.forget(box)
    await this.exec(["rm", "-f", box.name])
    getDb().prepare("DELETE FROM sandboxes WHERE id = ?").run(id)
    this.event("sandbox.destroyed", `Destroyed sandbox ${id}`, { sandbox: id }, taskId, box)
  }

  private forget(box: Box) {
    this.boxes.delete(box.id)
    if (box.timer) clearInterval(box.timer)
    box.timer = null
  }

  /** Stop every running sandbox of the project, keeping it, its record and its folders (R2.6, specs/task-persistence R3.4). */
  async stopAll(): Promise<void> {
    this.ended = true
    const up = [...this.boxes.values()].filter((b) => b.up)
    for (const box of up) {
      if (box.timer) clearInterval(box.timer)
      box.timer = null
      box.up = false
    }
    if (up.length) await this.exec(["stop", "-t", "2", ...up.map((b) => b.name)])
  }

  /**
    Remove every container of the project after a forced stop, keeping their records and their folders, so the next
    task to open creates them again over the same `/work` and `/root/out` (specs/task-persistence R3.8).
  */
  async dropAll(): Promise<void> {
    this.ended = true
    for (const box of [...this.boxes.values()]) {
      if (box.timer) clearInterval(box.timer)
      box.timer = null
      box.up = false
    }
    const recorded = (getDb().prepare("SELECT id FROM sandboxes WHERE project_id = ?").all(this.d.projectId) as Record<string, unknown>[]).map((r) =>
      sandboxName(String(r.id)),
    )
    if (recorded.length) await this.exec(["rm", "-f", ...recorded])
  }

  /**
    Remove every container of a project being deleted, every one its records name included (specs/projects R3.2);
    throws, keeping the records, when Docker fails to remove one it still has.
  */
  async removeAll(): Promise<void> {
    this.ended = true
    for (const box of [...this.boxes.values()]) this.forget(box)
    const recorded = (getDb().prepare("SELECT id FROM sandboxes WHERE project_id = ?").all(this.d.projectId) as Record<string, unknown>[]).map((r) =>
      sandboxName(String(r.id)),
    )
    if (recorded.length) {
      const r = await this.exec(["rm", "-f", ...recorded])
      if (r.code !== 0 && !/No such container/i.test(r.stderr)) throw new Error(`The project's sandboxes could not be removed: ${lastLine(r.stderr)}`)
    }
    getDb().prepare("DELETE FROM sandboxes WHERE project_id = ?").run(this.d.projectId)
  }

  ids(): string[] {
    return [...this.boxes.keys()]
  }

  /**
    Remove the sandboxes a gone process left running, keeping their records and folders (R2.7, specs/task-persistence
    R3.8); those of a project a live app holds are left alone (specs/shared-data-folder R2.3). `heldByLive` answers
    for a sandbox id.
  */
  static async sweep(exec: ExecBuffer, heldByLive: (sandboxId: string) => boolean = () => false): Promise<number> {
    const r = await exec(["ps", "--filter", "name=^hfr-sbx-", "--format", "{{.Names}}"])
    const names =
      r.code === 0
        ? r.stdout
            .toString("utf8")
            .split(/\s+/)
            .filter((n) => n.startsWith("hfr-sbx-"))
        : []
    const stale = names.filter((n) => !heldByLive(n.slice("hfr-sbx-".length)))
    // Their records stay: a reopened task creates them again over their folders (specs/task-persistence R3.8).
    if (stale.length) await exec(["rm", "-f", ...stale])
    return stale.length
  }
}

/**
  One `SpecialistBoxes` per project while any of its tasks is open, so the one-delegation-at-a-time rule holds across
  them (specs/projects R2.3, adr:0020-group-tasks-into-projects-that-share-their-analyses). The project owns no
  container: the last task to close stops its sandboxes, and the next task to open brings them up again.
*/
export class SandboxRegistry {
  private readonly open = new Map<string, { boxes: SpecialistBoxes; refs: number }>()
  /** a project whose last task closed, its sandboxes still stopping */
  private readonly stopping = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()
  constructor(private readonly make: (project: { id: string; folder: string; sourceRoot: string }, after?: Promise<void>) => SpecialistBoxes) {}

  acquire(project: { id: string; folder: string; sourceRoot: string }): { boxes: SpecialistBoxes; release: (o?: { remove?: boolean }) => Promise<void> } {
    let entry = this.open.get(project.id)
    if (!entry) {
      // A task opening while the last one's stop is in flight waits for it, so the stop cannot take its sandbox down.
      entry = { boxes: this.make(project, this.stopping.get(project.id)), refs: 0 }
      this.open.set(project.id, entry)
    }
    entry.refs++
    const held = entry
    let released = false
    return {
      boxes: held.boxes,
      // The last task to close stops the sandboxes; after a forced stop it removes them, records kept (specs/task-persistence R3.8).
      release: async (o = {}) => {
        if (released) return
        released = true
        held.refs--
        if (held.refs > 0 || this.open.get(project.id) !== held) return
        this.open.delete(project.id)
        const stop = (o.remove ? held.boxes.dropAll() : held.boxes.stopAll()).finally(
          () => this.stopping.get(project.id) === stop && this.stopping.delete(project.id),
        )
        this.stopping.set(project.id, stop)
        await stop
      },
    }
  }

  /** Remove every sandbox of a project being deleted, with an instance of its own when none is open. */
  async remove(project: { id: string; folder: string; sourceRoot: string }): Promise<void> {
    const entry = this.open.get(project.id)
    this.open.delete(project.id)
    await (entry?.boxes ?? this.make(project, this.stopping.get(project.id))).removeAll()
  }
}
```

`src/main/sandbox/taskbox.ts`:

```ts
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
import { createHash } from "node:crypto"
import { mkdirSync } from "node:fs"
import { posix } from "node:path"
import { BaseSandbox } from "deepagents"
import { identity, mountSource, SPECIALIST_IMAGE } from "./docker"

/*
  The orchestrator's container for one task (adr:0007-run-the-orchestrators-tools-in-a-task-container):
  the source folder bind-mounted read-only at /workspace, full internet access
  (adr:0013-give-the-sandboxes-full-internet-access), confined like the specialist's.
  DeepAgents reaches it as a sandbox backend, so its file tools and `execute` all run there through
  `docker exec`, and no tool of the orchestrator writes the user's files. It writes and runs its own code in
  /scratch (adr:0009-give-the-orchestrator-a-writable-scratch, specs/chat R6.3), bound from the task's own
  folder, and the container is stopped rather than removed when the task ends, so both outlive it until the
  task is deleted (adr:0017-keep-a-tasks-conversation-containers-and-files-until-it-is-deleted).
*/

export const WORKSPACE = "/workspace"
export const SCRATCH = "/scratch"
/** Largest command output returned to the agent. */
export const OUTPUT_CAP = 100_000
const EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000
/** A command's own time limit inside the container, under the client's, so it never outlives the call. */
const COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S = 110
/** Largest stdout kept from one `docker exec`: a file read whole, or a command's output before truncation. */
export const BUFFER_CAP = 16 * 1024 * 1024

export interface BufferResult {
  code: number
  stdout: Buffer
  stderr: string
  /** the output passed the cap and the command was stopped */
  overflow?: boolean
}

/** Runs `docker` with these arguments, feeding `input` to its stdin when given. */
export type ExecBuffer = (args: string[], timeoutMs?: number, input?: Uint8Array) => Promise<BufferResult>

export const dockerExecBuffer: ExecBuffer = (args, timeoutMs = EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS, input) =>
  new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn("docker", args, { windowsHide: true, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] })
    child.stdin.on("error", () => undefined)
    child.stdin.end(input)
    const out: Buffer[] = []
    let size = 0
    let overflow = false
    let stderr = ""
    const timer = setTimeout(() => child.kill(), timeoutMs)
    // The output lands in the app's own memory, outside the container's limits: stop at the cap.
    child.stdout.on("data", (c: Buffer) => {
      if (overflow) return
      out.push(c)
      size += c.length
      if (size > BUFFER_CAP) {
        overflow = true
        child.kill()
      }
    })
    child.stderr.on("data", (c: Buffer) => {
      if (stderr.length < OUTPUT_CAP) stderr += c.toString("utf8")
    })
    child.on("error", (e) => {
      clearTimeout(timer)
      resolve({ code: -1, stdout: Buffer.concat(out), stderr: e.message, overflow })
    })
    child.on("close", (code) => {
      clearTimeout(timer)
      resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout: Buffer.concat(out), stderr, overflow })
    })
  })

export function taskBoxName(taskId: string): string {
  return `hfr-orch-${taskId}`
}

/**
  `docker run` for a task's container: the source read-only at /workspace, full internet access, and root
  with a writable root filesystem so the orchestrator can install what its code needs
  (adr:0015-run-the-task-container-as-root); never privileged, never a host path but the source. No memory, CPU,
  process or size limit: /scratch and /tmp are folders on the writable root, on Docker's disk rather than in memory
  (specs/specialist-sandbox R6.1, R6.2).
*/
export function taskBoxArgs(taskId: string, sourceRoot: string, scratchDir: string): string[] {
  return [
    "run",
    "-d",
    "--name",
    taskBoxName(taskId),
    "--hostname",
    "workspace",
    // a PID 1 that reaps what `docker exec` and `timeout` leave behind
    "--init",
    // Root with what apt, dpkg, pip and npm need, and nothing else: no NET_RAW, MKNOD or SYS_CHROOT.
    ...identity(true),
    "--mount",
    `type=bind,source=${mountSource(sourceRoot)},target=${WORKSPACE},readonly,bind-propagation=rprivate,bind-recursive=readonly`,
    "--mount",
    `type=bind,source=${mountSource(scratchDir)},target=${SCRATCH}`,
    "-w",
    WORKSPACE,
    "--entrypoint",
    "sleep",
    SPECIALIST_IMAGE,
    "infinity",
  ]
}

/** What the orchestrator reads once a container Docker had removed was created again. */
export const RESTARTED = "[The task's sandbox was created again: /scratch was kept, anything installed is gone.]"

const lastLine = (s: string) => s.trim().split("\n").pop() || ""

/** The label a container carries of the arguments it was created with, so one made by an older app is not reused. */
export const CONFIG_LABEL = "hfr.config"

/** `docker run` arguments with the label of their own fingerprint, which covers the image and every flag and mount. */
export function labelled(args: string[]): string[] {
  const fingerprint = createHash("sha256").update(args.join("\0")).digest("hex").slice(0, 16)
  return [...args.slice(0, 2), "--label", `${CONFIG_LABEL}=${fingerprint}`, ...args.slice(2)]
}

/**
  Bring a task's container up: start it when Docker still has it as these arguments would make it, or create it over
  the same folders when Docker no longer has it or it was made otherwise — by an older app with another image or
  boundary (specs/task-persistence R3.5). Returns whether it was created, or throws with Docker's reason.
*/
export async function bringUp(exec: ExecBuffer, name: string, args: string[]): Promise<{ created: boolean }> {
  const run = labelled(args)
  const want = run[3]
  const has = await exec(["inspect", "--format", `${CONFIG_LABEL}={{index .Config.Labels "${CONFIG_LABEL}"}}`, name])
  if (has.code === 0 && has.stdout.toString("utf8").trim() === want) {
    const started = await exec(["start", name])
    if (started.code === 0) return { created: false }
    if (!/No such container/i.test(started.stderr)) throw new Error(lastLine(started.stderr) || `exit ${started.code}`)
  } else if (has.code === 0) {
    // made with another image or boundary: replaced, its folders kept
    const gone = await exec(["rm", "-f", name])
    if (gone.code !== 0 && !/No such container/i.test(gone.stderr)) throw new Error(lastLine(gone.stderr) || `exit ${gone.code}`)
  }
  const r = await exec(run)
  if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(lastLine(r.stderr) || `exit ${r.code}`)
  return { created: true }
}

export class TaskBox extends BaseSandbox {
  readonly id: string
  private readonly exec: ExecBuffer
  /** brings the container up again when it stopped or went away; whether it had to be created, or null when it could not */
  private readonly revive: () => Promise<{ created: boolean } | null>
  private disposed = false
  /** the container was created rather than started when the task opened: what was installed is gone */
  created = false

  constructor(exec: ExecBuffer, taskId: string, revive: () => Promise<{ created: boolean } | null> = async () => null) {
    super()
    this.exec = exec
    this.id = taskBoxName(taskId)
    this.revive = revive
  }

  /**
    Bring the task's container up, started again when Docker still has it (specs/task-persistence R3.5); throws with
    Docker's reason when it cannot. A container that stops or goes away later is brought up again.
  */
  static async start(exec: ExecBuffer, taskId: string, sourceRoot: string, scratchDir: string): Promise<TaskBox> {
    mkdirSync(scratchDir, { recursive: true })
    const up = () => bringUp(exec, taskBoxName(taskId), taskBoxArgs(taskId, sourceRoot, scratchDir))
    let first: { created: boolean }
    try {
      first = await up()
    } catch (e) {
      throw new Error(`The task's sandbox did not start: ${(e as Error).message}`, { cause: e })
    }
    const box = new TaskBox(exec, taskId, () => up().catch(() => null))
    box.created = first.created
    return box
  }

  /**
    One `docker exec` into the container. When the container stopped or is gone — stopped by the app's start, removed
    by Docker or by a crash — it is brought up again once and the call retried; /scratch is the task's folder, so it
    is still there.
  */
  private async inBox(args: string[], input?: Uint8Array): Promise<BufferResult & { restarted?: boolean }> {
    const r = await this.exec(args, undefined, input)
    if (this.disposed || r.code === 0 || !/No such container|is not running/i.test(r.stderr)) return r
    const up = await this.revive()
    if (!up) return r
    return { ...(await this.exec(args, undefined, input)), restarted: up.created }
  }

  async execute(command: string) {
    const r = await this.inBox(["exec", this.id, "timeout", "-s", "KILL", String(COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S), "sh", "-c", command])
    let output = (r.restarted ? RESTARTED + " " : "") + r.stdout.toString("utf8") + r.stderr
    const truncated = r.overflow === true || output.length > OUTPUT_CAP
    if (truncated) output = output.slice(0, OUTPUT_CAP)
    return { output, exitCode: r.code, truncated }
  }

  /** Writes land in /scratch only; the source is mounted read-only and nothing is uploaded to it (specs/chat R6.4). */
  async uploadFiles(files: Array<[string, Uint8Array]>) {
    const out = []
    for (const [path, content] of files) {
      const inScratch = path.startsWith("/") && posix.normalize(path).startsWith(`${SCRATCH}/`) && posix.normalize(path) === path
      const r = inScratch ? await this.inBox(["exec", "-i", this.id, "sh", "-c", 'mkdir -p "$(dirname "$1")" && cat > "$1"', "sh", path], content) : null
      out.push({ path, error: r?.code === 0 ? null : ("permission_denied" as const) })
    }
    return out
  }

  async downloadFiles(paths: string[]) {
    const out = []
    for (const path of paths) {
      const r = await this.inBox(["exec", this.id, "cat", "--", path])
      out.push(
        r.code === 0 && !r.overflow
          ? { path, content: new Uint8Array(r.stdout), error: null }
          : { path, content: null, error: /Is a directory/.test(r.stderr) ? ("is_directory" as const) : ("file_not_found" as const) },
      )
    }
    return out
  }

  /**
    Remove the task containers a gone process left running, e.g. after a crash — the tasks' files stay on the host
    (specs/task-persistence R3.8); those of a task a live app has open are left alone (specs/shared-data-folder R2.3).
    `ownedByLive` answers for a task id.
  */
  static async sweep(exec: ExecBuffer, ownedByLive: (taskId: string) => boolean = () => false): Promise<number> {
    // Running only: their tasks were interrupted, and a stopped container keeps what was installed in it.
    const r = await exec(["ps", "--filter", "name=^hfr-orch-", "--format", "{{.Names}}"])
    const names =
      r.code === 0
        ? r.stdout
            .toString("utf8")
            .split(/\s+/)
            .filter((n) => n.startsWith("hfr-orch-"))
        : []
    const stale = names.filter((n) => !ownedByLive(n.slice("hfr-orch-".length)))
    // A gone process's stop was forced: its containers go, the tasks' files stay (specs/task-persistence R3.8).
    if (stale.length) await exec(["rm", "-f", ...stale])
    return stale.length
  }

  /**
    Stop the container and keep it, with what was installed, for when the task reopens (specs/task-persistence R3.4);
    on a forced stop, remove it — `/scratch` is the task's folder on the host, so nothing of the task's is lost (R3.8).
  */
  async dispose(o: { remove?: boolean } = {}): Promise<void> {
    this.disposed = true
    await this.exec(o.remove ? ["rm", "-f", this.id] : ["stop", "-t", "2", this.id])
  }

  /** Remove the container of a task being deleted; one already gone is not an error (R4.1). */
  static async remove(exec: ExecBuffer, taskId: string): Promise<void> {
    const r = await exec(["rm", "-f", taskBoxName(taskId)])
    if (r.code !== 0 && !/No such container/i.test(r.stderr)) throw new Error(`The task's container could not be removed: ${lastLine(r.stderr)}`)
  }
}
```

`src/main/sandbox/workspace.ts`:

```ts
import { createHash, randomUUID } from "node:crypto"
import { existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { dirname, join } from "node:path"
import { PathRejected, resolveRequested, UNSAFE_NAME } from "./paths"

/*
  One delegation's directories under the app's data folder (specs/task-sandbox R1):

    workspace/<uuid>/   copies of the named files, mounted at /work
    runs/<uuid>/        the rendered system prompt, mounted read-only at /run/hfr
    runs/<uuid>/ask/    the specialist's questions and the user's answers, mounted writable at /run/hfr-ask
    snapshots/<uuid>/   pristine copies and manifest.json {path: sha256}, never mounted
*/

/** The workspace folder holding the files the orchestrator prepared in its scratch (specs/chat R6.7). */
export const PREPARED = ".orchestrator"

/** A file from the orchestrator's scratch, by its path under the scratch. */
export interface PreparedFile {
  path: string
  content: Buffer
}

export interface CopiedFile {
  path: string
  sha256: string
  size: number
}

export interface Workspace {
  id: string
  workspace: string
  runDir: string
  snapshot: string
  /** what the specialist extracts, builds or exports, mounted at /root/out (specs/rea-native R2.4) */
  out: string
  files: CopiedFile[]
}

export function sha256(data: Buffer | string): string {
  return createHash("sha256").update(data).digest("hex")
}

/** The run's two-way question channel (adr:0008-ask-the-user-from-the-specialist-over-the-run-channel). */
export function askDir(runDir: string): string {
  return join(runDir, "ask")
}

export function workspaceDirs(dataDir: string, id: string) {
  return {
    workspace: join(dataDir, "workspace", id),
    runDir: join(dataDir, "runs", id),
    snapshot: join(dataDir, "snapshots", id),
    out: join(dataDir, "outputs", id),
  }
}

interface Plan {
  /** source files by their path relative to the source folder */
  resolved: Map<string, string>
  prepared: PreparedFile[]
}

/**
  Resolve every requested file and check the total against the cap before anything is written, so a rejected
  path or a call past the cap copies nothing (specs/specialist-sandbox R2.2, R2.3).
*/
function planFiles(sourceRoot: string, requested: string[], prepared: PreparedFile[], cap: number, limit: string): Plan {
  const resolved = new Map<string, string>()
  // Windows paths are case-insensitive: `A.ts` and `a.ts` are one file and must be one copy.
  const seen = new Set<string>()
  let total = 0
  const preparedNames = new Set(prepared.map((p) => `${PREPARED}/${p.path}`))
  for (const r of requested) {
    if (preparedNames.has(r)) continue
    const { rel, abs } = resolveRequested(sourceRoot, r)
    // The folder belongs to the orchestrator's files, in any case, so no source file shares it.
    if (rel.toLowerCase().startsWith(`${PREPARED}/`)) throw new PathRejected(r, `is under ${PREPARED}/, which holds the files the orchestrator prepares`)
    const key = process.platform === "win32" ? rel.toLowerCase() : rel
    if (seen.has(key)) continue
    seen.add(key)
    total += statSync(abs).size
    if (total > cap) throw new PathRejected(r, `the files exceed the ${limit}`)
    resolved.set(rel, abs)
  }
  for (const p of prepared) {
    if (p.path.split("/").some((name) => !name || name === "." || name === ".." || UNSAFE_NAME.test(name)))
      throw new PathRejected(p.path, "is not a name the workspace may hold")
    total += p.content.length
    if (total > cap) throw new PathRejected(p.path, `the files exceed the ${limit}`)
  }
  return { resolved, prepared }
}

/**
  Refuse a target whose folders under the workspace include a link: a sandbox's root processes can plant one in
  /work after it starts, and the app must not write through it to the host.
*/
function assertNoLink(root: string, rel: string) {
  let dir = root
  for (const name of rel.split("/").slice(0, -1)) {
    dir = join(dir, name)
    let st
    try {
      st = lstatSync(dir)
    } catch {
      return
    }
    if (st.isSymbolicLink() || !st.isDirectory()) throw new PathRejected(rel, `cannot be written: ${name} in the workspace is not a folder`)
  }
  const target = join(root, rel)
  if (existsSync(target) && !lstatSync(target).isFile()) throw new PathRejected(rel, "cannot be written: it is not a file in the workspace")
}

/** Copy planned files into the workspace; source files also into the snapshot and its manifest. */
function writeFiles(ws: Workspace, plan: Plan): CopiedFile[] {
  for (const rel of [...plan.resolved.keys(), ...plan.prepared.map((p) => `${PREPARED}/${p.path}`)]) assertNoLink(ws.workspace, rel)
  const manifest = readManifest(ws.snapshot)
  const files: CopiedFile[] = []
  for (const [rel, abs] of plan.resolved) {
    const data = readFileSync(abs)
    for (const target of [join(ws.workspace, rel), join(ws.snapshot, "files", rel)]) {
      mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true })
      writeFileSync(target, data)
    }
    manifest[rel] = sha256(data)
    files.push({ path: rel, sha256: manifest[rel], size: data.length })
  }
  writeManifest(ws.snapshot, manifest)
  // What the orchestrator prepared goes to the specialist only: no snapshot, no manifest, never a patch.
  for (const p of plan.prepared) {
    const rel = `${PREPARED}/${p.path}`
    const target = join(ws.workspace, ...rel.split("/"))
    mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true })
    writeFileSync(target, p.content)
    files.push({ path: rel, sha256: sha256(p.content), size: p.content.length })
  }
  ws.files.push(...files)
  return files
}

function writeManifest(snapshot: string, manifest: Record<string, string>) {
  writeFileSync(join(snapshot, "manifest.json"), JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2))
}

/** The directories of a workspace with an empty snapshot, under a fresh UUID unless one is given. */
export function createWorkspace(dataDir: string, id: string = randomUUID()): Workspace {
  const dirs = workspaceDirs(dataDir, id)
  for (const d of [...Object.values(dirs), askDir(dirs.runDir)]) mkdirSync(d, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeManifest(dirs.snapshot, {})
  return { id, ...dirs, files: [] }
}

/**
  Resolve every requested file first, so a rejected path creates nothing, then copy each into the
  workspace and the snapshot and write the manifest.
*/
export function prepareWorkspace(dataDir: string, sourceRoot: string, requested: string[], prepared: PreparedFile[] = []): Workspace {
  const plan = planFiles(sourceRoot, requested, prepared, Infinity, "")
  const ws = createWorkspace(dataDir)
  try {
    writeFiles(ws, plan)
  } catch (e) {
    discardWorkspace(dataDir, ws.id)
    throw e
  }
  return ws
}

/**
  Copy more files into an existing workspace, a sandbox's (specs/specialist-sandbox R2.1–R2.3): every path is
  resolved and the total checked against `cap` bytes before anything is written.
*/
export function addFiles(ws: Workspace, sourceRoot: string, requested: string[], prepared: PreparedFile[], cap: number, limit: string): CopiedFile[] {
  return writeFiles(ws, planFiles(sourceRoot, requested, prepared, cap, limit))
}

/**
  Take the workspace as it stands as the snapshot for the files a patch changed, so the next patch from the same
  sandbox is made against it (specs/specialist-sandbox R4.5).
*/
export function rebaseSnapshot(ws: Workspace, changes: { path: string; status: "added" | "modified" | "deleted" }[]) {
  const manifest = readManifest(ws.snapshot)
  for (const c of changes) {
    const target = join(ws.snapshot, "files", c.path)
    if (c.status === "deleted") {
      delete manifest[c.path]
      rmSync(target, { force: true })
      continue
    }
    // Only a regular file becomes the base: what the sandbox left in its place is dropped from the snapshot.
    const source = join(ws.workspace, c.path)
    if (!lstatSync(source, { throwIfNoEntry: false })?.isFile()) {
      delete manifest[c.path]
      rmSync(target, { force: true })
      continue
    }
    const data = readFileSync(source)
    mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true })
    writeFileSync(target, data)
    manifest[c.path] = sha256(data)
  }
  writeManifest(ws.snapshot, manifest)
}

export function readManifest(snapshot: string): Record<string, string> {
  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(snapshot, "manifest.json"), "utf8")) as Record<string, string>
}

/** Write the run's rendered system prompt where the container reads it, outside /work. */
export function writeSystemPrompt(ws: Workspace, system: string): string {
  const file = join(ws.runDir, "system.md")
  writeFileSync(file, system, { encoding: "utf8", mode: 0o600 })
  return file
}

/** Delete the workspace, run directory and snapshot of a delegation (specs/task-sandbox R1.4). */
export function discardWorkspace(dataDir: string, id: string) {
  for (const d of Object.values(workspaceDirs(dataDir, id))) rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true })
}
```

`src/main/settings.ts`:

```ts
import { DEFAULT_SETTINGS } from "@shared/defaults"
import type { Settings } from "@shared/types"
import { getSetting, setSetting } from "./db"

/*
  The user's settings, stored as one record over the defaults. Arguments are validated at the IPC boundary. Each
  provider keeps its own base URL (specs/orchestrator R1.10): `baseUrl` is the chosen provider's, and switching
  provider brings back the one it had.
*/

const KEY = "app.settings"

export function getSettings(): Settings {
  const stored = getSetting<Partial<Settings>>(KEY, {})
  const s = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...stored }
  // Settings saved before base URLs were kept per provider hold only the one of the provider they were on.
  const baseUrls = stored.baseUrls ?? (s.baseUrl ? { [s.provider]: s.baseUrl } : {})
  return { ...s, baseUrls, baseUrl: baseUrls[s.provider] ?? "" }
}

export function saveSettings(patch: Partial<Settings>): Settings {
  const current = getSettings()
  const provider = patch.provider ?? current.provider
  const baseUrls = { ...current.baseUrls, ...(patch.baseUrl !== undefined ? { [provider]: patch.baseUrl } : {}) }
  const next = { ...current, ...patch, baseUrls, baseUrl: baseUrls[provider] ?? "" }
  setSetting(KEY, next)
  return next
}
```

`src/main/specialist/account.ts`:

```ts
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
import type { Readable, Writable } from "node:stream"

/*
  The user's Claude login, always inside the sandbox image on its config volume (specs/claude-specialist
  R3; adr:0003-authenticate-the-specialist-with-the-users-claude-plan). The app never reads the
  credential: it asks `claude auth status --json`, runs `claude auth login --claudeai`, exposes only
  the Anthropic page that login prints, and passes on the code the user pastes. Ported from
  study-lab's `account.ts`.
*/

export interface AccountState {
  loggedIn: boolean
  method: string
  plan?: string
  email?: string
}

export interface ChildLike {
  stdout: Readable | null
  stderr: Readable | null
  stdin: Writable | null
  kill(): boolean
  on(event: "close", fn: (code: number | null) => void): unknown
  on(event: "error", fn: (err: Error) => void): unknown
}

/** Start `claude auth <sub…>` — in the app, `docker run … claude auth …`. */
export type StartAuth = (sub: string[]) => ChildLike

/**
  Spawn `command` with the arguments `prepare` gives for each auth command. Killing the child also
  calls `stop`, since killing the `docker` client does not stop the container it started.
*/
export function spawnStart(command: string, prepare: (sub: string[]) => { args: string[]; stop?: () => void }): StartAuth {
  return (sub) => {
    const p = prepare(sub)
    const child = spawn(command, p.args, { windowsHide: true, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] })
    const kill = child.kill.bind(child)
    child.kill = () => {
      p.stop?.()
      return kill()
    }
    return child
  }
}

/** Strip terminal escapes (colour, OSC 8 links) and control characters. */
export function cleanText(text: string): string {
  return text
    .replace(/\x1b\][^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\)/g, "")
    .replace(/\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]/g, "")
    .replace(/[\x00-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]/g, "")
}

const ANTHROPIC_HOSTS = ["claude.com", "claude.ai", "anthropic.com"]

export function isAnthropicUrl(url: string): boolean {
  try {
    const u = new URL(url)
    return u.protocol === "https:" && ANTHROPIC_HOSTS.some((h) => u.hostname === h || u.hostname.endsWith(`.${h}`))
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}

/** The sign-in address the login printed, when it is Anthropic's. */
export function loginUrl(text: string): string | null {
  for (const m of cleanText(text).matchAll(/https:\/\/[^\s"'<>]+/g)) if (isAnthropicUrl(m[0])) return m[0]
  return null
}

export function validCode(code: string): boolean {
  return /^[A-Za-z0-9#_\-.~]{8,512}$/.test(code.trim())
}

/** `claude auth status --json`, which the pinned CLI prints over several lines. */
export function parseStatus(out: string): AccountState {
  const d = JSON.parse(out.slice(out.indexOf("{"), out.lastIndexOf("}") + 1)) as {
    loggedIn?: unknown
    authMethod?: unknown
    subscriptionType?: unknown
    email?: unknown
  }
  return {
    loggedIn: d.loggedIn === true,
    method: typeof d.authMethod === "string" ? d.authMethod : "none",
    plan: typeof d.subscriptionType === "string" ? d.subscriptionType : undefined,
    email: typeof d.email === "string" ? d.email : undefined,
  }
}

const INSTRUCTIONS = [/^Opening browser/i, /didn't open/i, /^https:\/\//]
/** The prompt Claude Code prints without a newline, so its outcome follows on the same line. */
const PROMPT = /^Paste code here if prompted\s*>\s*/i

/** The last line Claude Code wrote that says what went wrong. */
export function failureReason(text: string): string {
  const lines = cleanText(text)
    .split("\n")
    .map((l) => l.trim().replace(PROMPT, ""))
    .filter((l) => l && !INSTRUCTIONS.some((r) => r.test(l)))
  return lines.pop() ?? "The sign-in did not finish."
}

export interface LoginInProgress {
  sendCode(code: string): void
  cancel(): void
  done: Promise<{ ok: boolean; text: string }>
}

function collect(child: ChildLike): Promise<{ code: number | null; out: string }> {
  let out = ""
  child.stdout?.on("data", (c: Buffer) => (out += c.toString("utf8")))
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    child.on("error", () => resolve({ code: -1, out }))
    child.on("close", (code) => resolve({ code, out }))
  })
}

export class ClaudeAccount {
  private readonly start: StartAuth

  constructor(start: StartAuth) {
    this.start = start
  }

  async state(): Promise<AccountState> {
    try {
      const child = this.start(["status", "--json"])
      child.stdin?.end()
      const { out } = await collect(child)
      return parseStatus(out)
    } catch {
      return { loggedIn: false, method: "none" }
    }
  }

  async logout(): Promise<void> {
    const child = this.start(["logout"])
    child.stdin?.end()
    await collect(child)
  }

  /** Start the subscription sign-in. `onText` gets what Claude Code writes, cleaned. */
  login(onText: (text: string) => void): LoginInProgress {
    const child = this.start(["login", "--claudeai"])
    let text = ""
    const listen = (chunk: Buffer) => {
      const t = cleanText(chunk.toString("utf8"))
      text += t
      onText(t)
    }
    child.stdout?.on("data", listen)
    child.stderr?.on("data", listen)
    const done = new Promise<{ ok: boolean; text: string }>((resolve) => {
      child.on("error", (e) => resolve({ ok: false, text: `${text}${e.message}` }))
      child.on("close", (code) => resolve({ ok: code === 0, text }))
    })
    return {
      sendCode: (code) => {
        if (!validCode(code)) throw new Error("That code does not look right. Copy it again from the Anthropic page.")
        child.stdin?.write(`${code.trim()}\n`)
      },
      cancel: () => {
        child.kill()
      },
      done,
    }
  }
}
```

`src/main/specialist/executor.ts`:

```ts
import { spawn, spawnSync, type ChildProcess } from "node:child_process"
import { createInterface } from "node:readline"
import { StreamReader, type StreamEvent, type StreamResult } from "./stream"

/*
  One specialist session (specs/claude-specialist R1): start a prepared launch — always the
  sandbox's `docker run … claude -p …` in the app, a fake CLI in tests — send turns as stream-json
  on stdin, read events from stdout, and stop it on cancel or timeout. The executor never chooses
  a binary itself, so there is no path by which the specialist runs on the host.
*/

export interface Launch {
  command: string
  args: string[]
  cwd?: string
  env?: Record<string, string>
  /** stop whatever the process stands for, e.g. `docker kill` its container */
  stop?: () => Promise<void>
}

/** `refused`: a safeguard refusal under the usage policy, never a failure to retry (specs/specialist-lifecycle R2.1) */
export type FailureKind = "auth" | "limit" | "refused" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "timeout"

/** What the user and the orchestrator read for a safeguard refusal. */
export const REFUSED = "The specialist declined this step under its usage policy (a safeguard refusal)."

export class SpecialistError extends Error {
  readonly kind: FailureKind

  constructor(kind: FailureKind, message: string) {
    super(message)
    this.name = "SpecialistError"
    this.kind = kind
  }
}

/** Turn what Claude Code reported into something the user can act on (R1.4). */
export function classifyFailure(text: string): SpecialistError {
  if (/invalid api key|please run \/login|not logged in|oauth token|authentication/i.test(text))
    return new SpecialistError("auth", "The specialist is not signed in to Claude. Sign in again in Settings.")
  if (/usage limit|hit your limit|rate.?limit|limit reached|overloaded/i.test(text)) {
    const resets = /resets?\s+(.+)/i.exec(text)?.[1]?.trim()
    return new SpecialistError("limit", `Your Claude plan's limit is reached for now${resets ? ` (resets ${resets})` : ""}.`)
  }
  return new SpecialistError("failed", `Claude Code: ${text.slice(0, 400) || "the run failed."}`)
}

export interface SessionOptions {
  onEvent?(e: StreamEvent): void
  /** every stdout line, unparsed, before it is read */
  onRaw?(line: string): void
  timeoutMs: number
  signal?: AbortSignal
}

function killTree(child: ChildProcess) {
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.pid === undefined) return
  if (process.platform === "win32") spawnSync("taskkill", ["/T", "/F", "/PID", String(child.pid)], { windowsHide: true })
  else child.kill("SIGKILL")
}

export class SpecialistSession {
  readonly reader = new StreamReader()
  private readonly child: ChildProcess
  private readonly launch: Launch
  private stderr = ""
  private pending: { resolve(r: StreamResult): void; reject(e: Error): void } | null = null
  private failure: SpecialistError | null = null
  private readonly exited: Promise<number | null>
  private readonly timer: NodeJS.Timeout
  private readonly abort: () => void
  private readonly signal?: AbortSignal

  constructor(launch: Launch, o: SessionOptions) {
    if (o.signal?.aborted) throw new SpecialistError("cancelled", "Cancelled.")
    this.launch = launch
    this.signal = o.signal
    this.child = spawn(launch.command, launch.args, { cwd: launch.cwd, env: launch.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"], windowsHide: true })
    this.child.stdin?.on("error", () => undefined)
    this.child.stderr?.on("data", (c: Buffer) => {
      this.stderr = (this.stderr + c.toString("utf8")).slice(-4000)
    })
    createInterface({ input: this.child.stdout! }).on("line", (line) => {
      o.onRaw?.(line)
      for (const e of this.reader.line(line)) {
        o.onEvent?.(e)
        if (e.kind === "result") this.settle()
      }
    })
    this.exited = new Promise((resolve) => {
      this.child.on("error", (e) => {
        this.fail(new SpecialistError("failed", `Claude Code did not start: ${e.message}`))
        resolve(null)
      })
      this.child.on("close", (code) => {
        clearTimeout(this.timer)
        this.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", this.abort)
        const last = this.stderr.trim().split("\n").pop()?.trim()
        this.fail(this.failure ?? classifyFailure(last || `Claude Code stopped without an answer (exit ${code}).`))
        resolve(code)
      })
    })
    this.timer = setTimeout(() => void this.kill("timeout"), o.timeoutMs)
    this.abort = () => void this.kill("cancelled")
    o.signal?.addEventListener("abort", this.abort, { once: true })
  }

  private settle() {
    const r = this.reader.result
    const p = this.pending
    if (!r || !p) return
    this.pending = null
    // A refusal is read from the API's stop reason, or from Claude Code's own error line on a failed turn — never from
    // anything the specialist could be steered to write.
    if (r.refused || (r.error && /^API Error:[^\n]*usage policy/i.test(r.text))) p.reject(new SpecialistError("refused", REFUSED))
    else if (r.error) p.reject(classifyFailure(r.text || r.reason || this.stderr))
    else p.resolve(r)
  }

  private fail(e: SpecialistError) {
    const p = this.pending
    this.pending = null
    p?.reject(e)
  }

  /** Send one user turn; resolves with that turn's result (R1.2). */
  send(text: string): Promise<StreamResult> {
    if (this.failure) return Promise.reject(this.failure)
    if (this.child.exitCode !== null) return Promise.reject(new SpecialistError("failed", "Claude Code is no longer running."))
    if (this.pending) return Promise.reject(new SpecialistError("failed", "A turn is already in progress."))
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      this.pending = { resolve, reject }
      this.child.stdin?.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: "user", message: { role: "user", content: text } })}\n`)
    })
  }

  /** End stdin and wait for Claude Code to exit. */
  async close(): Promise<void> {
    this.child.stdin?.end()
    await this.exited
  }

  /** Stop the container and the process tree, reporting the session as cancelled or timed out (R1.3). */
  async kill(kind: "cancelled" | "timeout"): Promise<void> {
    if (this.failure) return
    this.failure = new SpecialistError(kind, kind === "timeout" ? "The delegation exceeded its timeout and was stopped." : "Cancelled.")
    this.fail(this.failure)
    await this.launch.stop?.().catch(() => undefined)
    killTree(this.child)
    await this.exited
  }

  get outcome(): FailureKind | null {
    return this.failure?.kind ?? null
  }
}
```

`src/main/specialist/stream.ts`:

```ts
import type { EventPayload, FileTouch } from "@shared/types"

/*
  Claude Code's stream-json, line by line, into events (specs/claude-specialist R2): text, thinking,
  tool calls and results attributed to the subagent that made them, the final result with usage
  and cost, and every line the reader does not know kept rather than dropped. Ported from
  study-lab's `stream.ts` with the caps and subagent attribution of MagnoTech's `leitorDoStream.ts`.
*/

export const ARGS_CAP = 4 * 1024
export const RESULT_CAP = 16 * 1024
export const TEXT_CAP = 32 * 1024

// The text comes from files the user handed in: no control characters.
const CONTROL = /[\u0000-\u0008\u000b-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]/g

export function clean(v: unknown): string {
  return String(v ?? "").replace(CONTROL, "")
}

function cap(text: string, limit: number): { text: string; truncated: boolean } {
  return text.length > limit ? { text: text.slice(0, limit), truncated: true } : { text, truncated: false }
}

const WRITE_TOOLS = new Set(["Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"])
const READ_TOOLS = new Set(["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "LS", "NotebookRead"])
const REA_PATH_ARGS = ["path", "file_path", "binary_path", "artifact_path", "apk_path", "input_path", "target_path"]

/** `/work/src/a.ts` → `src/a.ts`; anything outside /work is reported as it is. */
export function fromWork(p: string): string {
  const s = p.replace(/\\/g, "/")
  if (s === "/work") return "."
  return s.startsWith("/work/") ? s.slice(6) : s
}

/** The files a tool call reads or writes, by source-relative path (R2.5). */
export function filesOf(tool: string, input: Record<string, unknown>): FileTouch[] {
  // REA's tools read the binary or artifact they are given, whatever its argument is called (specs/rea-native R2.1).
  if (tool.startsWith("mcp__rea__")) {
    const p = REA_PATH_ARGS.map((k) => input[k]).find((v): v is string => typeof v === "string" && v !== "")
    return p ? [{ path: fromWork(clean(p)), op: "read" }] : []
  }
  const op = WRITE_TOOLS.has(tool) ? "write" : READ_TOOLS.has(tool) ? "read" : null
  if (!op) return []
  const p = input.file_path ?? input.notebook_path ?? input.path
  return typeof p === "string" && p ? [{ path: fromWork(clean(p)), op }] : []
}

export interface StreamEvent {
  kind: "init" | "text" | "thinking" | "tool.call" | "tool.progress" | "tool.result" | "result" | "unknown"
  summary: string
  payload: EventPayload
}

export interface StreamResult {
  text: string
  error: boolean
  session: string | null
  durationMs: number
  /** Claude Code's `total_cost_usd`: an estimate against the user's plan */
  costUsd: number | null
  tokensIn: number
  tokensOut: number
  cacheTokens: number
  model: string
  /** the error subtype or API status when it failed */
  reason?: string
  /** the model stopped with a safeguard refusal (specs/specialist-lifecycle R2.1) */
  refused?: boolean
}

interface Block {
  type?: string
  text?: string
  thinking?: string
  id?: string
  name?: string
  input?: Record<string, unknown>
  tool_use_id?: string
  content?: unknown
  is_error?: boolean
}

const isObj = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> => typeof v === "object" && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v)
const num = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : 0)

const KNOWN = new Set(["system", "assistant", "user", "result", "stream_event", "rate_limit_event", "tool_progress"])

/** A tool still running is recorded again only once this many more seconds passed, so a long call adds a few events, not one per heartbeat. */
export const PROGRESS_STEP_S = 15

export class StreamReader {
  session: string | null = null
  model = ""
  /** the last result; a multi-turn session has one per turn */
  result: StreamResult | null = null
  /** an assistant message of this turn stopped with `stop_reason: "refusal"` */
  private refused = false
  private readonly subagents = new Map<string, string>()
  private readonly tools = new Map<string, string>()
  /** the elapsed seconds last recorded for each running call */
  private readonly progress = new Map<string, number>()

  /** One line of stdout: the events it brings. */
  line(raw: string): StreamEvent[] {
    if (!raw.trim()) return []
    let e: unknown
    try {
      e = JSON.parse(raw)
    } catch {
      return [{ kind: "unknown", summary: "Unparsed output line", payload: { output: cap(clean(raw), RESULT_CAP).text } }]
    }
    if (!isObj(e)) return [{ kind: "unknown", summary: "Output line that is not an object", payload: { output: cap(clean(raw), RESULT_CAP).text } }]
    if (typeof e.session_id === "string") this.session = e.session_id
    const type = clean(e.type)
    if (type === "system" && e.subtype === "init") return [this.init(e)]
    if (type === "assistant") return this.assistant(e)
    if (type === "user") return this.results(e)
    if (type === "result") return [this.finish(e)]
    if (type === "tool_progress") return this.toolProgress(e)
    if (KNOWN.has(type)) return []
    return [{ kind: "unknown", summary: `Unknown stream event type: ${type || "(none)"}`, payload: { output: cap(clean(raw), RESULT_CAP).text } }]
  }

  private init(e: Record<string, unknown>): StreamEvent {
    if (typeof e.model === "string") this.model = clean(e.model)
    const tools = Array.isArray(e.tools) ? e.tools.map(clean) : []
    return { kind: "init", summary: `Claude Code started (${this.model || "model unknown"})`, payload: { model: this.model, tools } }
  }

  private agentOf(parent: unknown): { subagent?: string } {
    if (typeof parent !== "string" || !parent) return {}
    return { subagent: this.subagents.get(parent) ?? "general-purpose" }
  }

  private blocks(e: Record<string, unknown>): Block[] {
    const m = isObj(e.message) ? e.message : {}
    return Array.isArray(m.content) ? (m.content as Block[]) : []
  }

  private assistant(e: Record<string, unknown>): StreamEvent[] {
    const out: StreamEvent[] = []
    if (isObj(e.message) && e.message.stop_reason === "refusal") this.refused = true
    const who = this.agentOf(e.parent_tool_use_id)
    for (const b of this.blocks(e)) {
      if (b.type === "thinking" && b.thinking?.trim()) {
        const t = cap(clean(b.thinking), TEXT_CAP)
        out.push({ kind: "thinking", summary: t.text.split("\n")[0], payload: { output: t.text, ...who, ...(t.truncated ? { truncated: true } : {}) } })
      } else if (b.type === "text" && b.text?.trim()) {
        const t = cap(clean(b.text), TEXT_CAP)
        out.push({ kind: "text", summary: t.text.split("\n")[0], payload: { output: t.text, ...who, ...(t.truncated ? { truncated: true } : {}) } })
      } else if (b.type === "tool_use") out.push(this.call(b, who))
    }
    return out
  }

  private call(b: Block, who: { subagent?: string }): StreamEvent {
    const id = clean(b.id)
    const tool = clean(b.name)
    this.tools.set(id, tool)
    let input = isObj(b.input) ? b.input : {}
    if (tool === "Agent" || tool === "Task") {
      const role = clean(input.subagent_type || "general-purpose")
      this.subagents.set(id, role)
      input = { subagent_type: role, description: clean(input.description ?? input.prompt) }
    }
    const files = filesOf(tool, input)
    const args = cap(JSON.stringify(input), ARGS_CAP)
    const target = files[0]?.path ?? ""
    return {
      kind: "tool.call",
      summary: `${tool}${target ? ` ${target}` : ""}`,
      payload: { tool, callId: id, input: args.text, files, ...who, ...(args.truncated ? { truncated: true } : {}) },
    }
  }

  /**
    Claude Code's heartbeat for a tool still running (specs/chat-timeline R1.4): the call it belongs to and how long it
    has run, recorded at the first heartbeat and then every PROGRESS_STEP_S seconds.
  */
  private toolProgress(e: Record<string, unknown>): StreamEvent[] {
    const id = clean(e.parent_tool_use_id) || clean(e.tool_use_id).replace(/-heartbeat-\d+$/, "")
    if (!id) return []
    const elapsed = Math.floor(num(e.elapsed_time_seconds))
    const last = this.progress.get(id)
    if (last !== undefined && elapsed - last < PROGRESS_STEP_S) return []
    this.progress.set(id, elapsed)
    const tool = this.tools.get(id) ?? clean(e.tool_name)
    return [{ kind: "tool.progress", summary: `${tool || "tool"} running for ${elapsed}s`, payload: { tool, callId: id, elapsedSeconds: elapsed } }]
  }

  private results(e: Record<string, unknown>): StreamEvent[] {
    const out: StreamEvent[] = []
    const who = this.agentOf(e.parent_tool_use_id)
    for (const b of this.blocks(e)) {
      if (b.type !== "tool_result") continue
      const id = clean(b.tool_use_id)
      const parts = typeof b.content === "string" ? [{ type: "text", text: b.content }] : Array.isArray(b.content) ? (b.content as Block[]) : []
      const text = cap(
        parts
          .filter((p) => p.type === "text")
          .map((p) => clean(p.text))
          .join("\n"),
        RESULT_CAP,
      )
      const tool = this.tools.get(id) ?? ""
      this.progress.delete(id)
      const error = b.is_error === true
      out.push({
        kind: "tool.result",
        summary: `${tool || "tool"} ${error ? "failed" : "returned"}${text.text ? `: ${text.text.split("\n")[0]}` : ""}`,
        payload: {
          tool,
          callId: id,
          output: text.text,
          ...(error ? { error: text.text.slice(0, 500) || "failed" } : {}),
          ...who,
          ...(text.truncated ? { truncated: true } : {}),
        },
      })
    }
    return out
  }

  private finish(e: Record<string, unknown>): StreamEvent {
    const u = isObj(e.usage) ? e.usage : {}
    const models = isObj(e.modelUsage) ? Object.keys(e.modelUsage) : []
    const error = e.is_error === true || (typeof e.subtype === "string" && e.subtype !== "success")
    const r: StreamResult = {
      text: clean(e.result).trim(),
      error,
      session: this.session,
      durationMs: num(e.duration_ms),
      costUsd: typeof e.total_cost_usd === "number" ? e.total_cost_usd : null,
      tokensIn: num(u.input_tokens),
      tokensOut: num(u.output_tokens),
      cacheTokens: num(u.cache_creation_input_tokens) + num(u.cache_read_input_tokens),
      model: this.model || models[0] || "claude",
      reason: error ? clean(e.api_error_status ?? e.subtype ?? "") || undefined : undefined,
      ...(this.refused ? { refused: true } : {}),
    }
    this.refused = false
    this.result = r
    const t = cap(r.text, TEXT_CAP)
    return {
      kind: "result",
      summary: error ? `Specialist failed: ${r.reason ?? (t.text.split("\n")[0] || "error")}` : `Specialist answered in ${(r.durationMs / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`,
      payload: {
        output: t.text,
        model: r.model,
        tokensIn: r.tokensIn,
        tokensOut: r.tokensOut,
        cacheTokens: r.cacheTokens,
        ...(r.costUsd !== null ? { costUsd: r.costUsd, estimate: true } : {}),
        durationMs: r.durationMs,
        session: r.session,
        ...(error ? { error: r.reason ?? "error" } : {}),
        ...(t.truncated ? { truncated: true } : {}),
      },
    }
  }
}
```

`src/main/status.ts`:

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto"
import type { LoginStatus, SandboxStatus } from "@shared/types"
import { CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION, dockerState, prepareImages, type Exec } from "./sandbox/docker"
import { ClaudeAccount, failureReason, loginUrl, type AccountState, type LoginInProgress, type StartAuth } from "./specialist/account"

/*
  What Settings shows and drives: Docker, the sandbox image and its preparation, and the specialist's
  Claude login (specs/desktop-ui R1.2, R1.3). Each change is pushed through `onChange`.
*/

/**
  A job done once across the apps on a data folder (specs/shared-data-folder R4.2, R4.3): `take` returns the release,
  or the app that holds the job when another live process is doing it.
*/
export interface OnceGuard {
  take(): (() => void) | { heldBy: string }
}

const noGuard: OnceGuard = { take: () => () => undefined }

/** How often an app waiting on another app's image build looks again. */
export const ELSEWHERE_POLL_MS = 2000

export class SandboxService {
  private readonly exec: Exec
  private readonly sandboxDir: string
  private readonly onChange: (s: SandboxStatus) => void
  /** The automatic preparation runs once per app session; after that only the user starts one (specs/sandbox-images R3.3). */
  private prepared = false
  private current: SandboxStatus = { docker: false, dockerError: "", images: false, building: false, buildLog: "", claudeVersion: CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION }

  constructor(
    exec: Exec,
    sandboxDir: string,
    onChange: (s: SandboxStatus) => void = () => undefined,
    private readonly guard: OnceGuard = noGuard,
    private readonly pollMs = ELSEWHERE_POLL_MS,
  ) {
    this.exec = exec
    this.sandboxDir = sandboxDir
    this.onChange = onChange
  }

  /** Another app is preparing the images: show it, and read the images' state again once it is done (R4.2). */
  private elsewhere(heldBy: string): { status: SandboxStatus; done: Promise<SandboxStatus> } {
    this.prepared = true
    const status = this.set({ building: true, buildLog: `The sandbox image is being prepared by ${heldBy}.\n` })
    const done = new Promise<SandboxStatus>((resolve) => {
      const look = () => {
        const g = this.guard.take()
        if ("heldBy" in g) {
          setTimeout(look, this.pollMs).unref?.()
          return
        }
        g()
        this.set({ building: false, buildLog: `${this.current.buildLog}Done in ${heldBy}.\n` })
        void this.status().then(resolve)
      }
      setTimeout(look, this.pollMs).unref?.()
    })
    return { status, done }
  }

  /**
    Only a change is pushed: a view re-reads the readiness on every push, so pushing an unchanged state would make
    each read cause the next, a loop that starts a container per turn.
  */
  private set(patch: Partial<SandboxStatus>): SandboxStatus {
    const next = { ...this.current, ...patch }
    const changed = JSON.stringify(next) !== JSON.stringify(this.current)
    this.current = next
    if (changed) this.onChange(this.current)
    return this.current
  }

  /** The current state; the first one that finds Docker running without a ready image starts preparing it (specs/sandbox-images R3.1, R3.2). */
  async status(): Promise<SandboxStatus> {
    if (this.current.building) return this.current
    const s = this.set(await dockerState(this.exec))
    if (s.docker && !s.images && !this.prepared) return this.build().status
    return s
  }

  /** Start preparing the image; resolves with the status at the start, then pushes the outcome. */
  build(): { status: SandboxStatus; done: Promise<SandboxStatus> } {
    if (this.current.building) return { status: this.current, done: Promise.resolve(this.current) }
    const g = this.guard.take()
    if ("heldBy" in g) return this.elsewhere(g.heldBy)
    this.prepared = true
    const status = this.set({
      building: true,
      buildLog: "Preparing the sandbox image: pulling the base, then adding Claude Code, downloaded and verified.\n",
    })
    const done = prepareImages(this.exec, this.sandboxDir)
      .finally(g)
      .then(async (r) => {
        this.set({ building: false, buildLog: `${this.current.buildLog}${r.log}${r.ok ? "Done.\n" : "Preparing the image failed.\n"}`.slice(-20_000) })
        return this.status()
      })
    return { status, done }
  }
}

export class LoginService {
  private readonly account: ClaudeAccount
  private readonly onChange: (s: LoginStatus) => void
  private state: AccountState = { loggedIn: false, method: "none" }
  private login: LoginInProgress | null = null
  private text = ""
  private error = ""

  constructor(
    start: StartAuth,
    onChange: (s: LoginStatus) => void = () => undefined,
    private readonly guard: OnceGuard = noGuard,
  ) {
    this.account = new ClaudeAccount(start)
    this.onChange = onChange
  }

  current(): LoginStatus {
    return {
      ...this.state,
      inProgress: !!this.login,
      url: this.login ? loginUrl(this.text) : null,
      text: this.login ? this.text.slice(-2000) : "",
      error: this.error,
    }
  }

  /** The last state pushed, so an unchanged refresh pushes nothing (see SandboxService.set). */
  private pushed = ""

  private changed(): LoginStatus {
    const s = this.current()
    const key = JSON.stringify(s)
    if (key !== this.pushed) {
      this.pushed = key
      this.onChange(s)
    }
    return s
  }

  async refresh(): Promise<LoginStatus> {
    if (!this.login) this.state = await this.account.state()
    return this.changed()
  }

  /** Start the sign-in; `done` settles when it finishes, with the refreshed state. */
  start(): { status: LoginStatus; done: Promise<LoginStatus> } {
    if (this.login) return { status: this.current(), done: Promise.resolve(this.current()) }
    // One sign-in across the apps on this data folder (specs/shared-data-folder R4.3).
    const g = this.guard.take()
    if ("heldBy" in g) throw new Error(`Claude is being signed in from ${g.heldBy}; finish it there.`)
    this.text = ""
    this.error = ""
    let l: LoginInProgress
    try {
      l = this.account.login((t) => {
        this.text += t
        this.changed()
      })
    } catch (e) {
      g()
      throw e
    }
    this.login = l
    const done = l.done.then(async ({ ok, text }) => {
      g()
      this.login = null
      this.text = ""
      this.state = await this.account.state()
      if (!ok || !this.state.loggedIn) this.error = failureReason(text)
      return this.changed()
    })
    return { status: this.changed(), done }
  }

  sendCode(code: string): LoginStatus {
    if (!this.login) throw new Error("No sign-in is in progress.")
    this.login.sendCode(code)
    return this.current()
  }

  cancel(): LoginStatus {
    this.login?.cancel()
    return this.current()
  }

  /** The Anthropic page to open, only while a sign-in runs. */
  url(): string | null {
    return this.login ? loginUrl(this.text) : null
  }

  async logout(): Promise<LoginStatus> {
    await this.account.logout().catch(() => undefined)
    return this.refresh()
  }
}

export const authId = () => randomUUID().slice(0, 8)
```
