`tests/shared-data-folder.test.ts`:

```ts
import { mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"
import { tmpdir } from "node:os"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
import type { Push } from "../src/shared/types"
import { initKey, moveKeys, readKey, useKeyStore, type KeyStore } from "../src/main/credentials"
import { closeDb, exclusive, getDb, openDb, SCHEMA_VERSION, SchemaTooNew } from "../src/main/db"
import { EventLog, eventRow, patchRow, stepRow } from "../src/main/events/log"
import { keyringStore, type KeyEntry } from "../src/main/keys"
import { ProcessRegistry, STALE_MS } from "../src/main/processes"
import { BASE_IMAGE, CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION, SPECIALIST_IMAGE, type Exec } from "../src/main/sandbox/docker"
import { LoginService, SandboxService, type OnceGuard } from "../src/main/status"
import { ChangeWatcher } from "../src/main/watch"

/* specs/shared-data-folder: several processes on one data folder. */

const tmp = () => mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "hfr-shared-"))
afterEach(() => closeDb())

describe("processes (R2.1)", () => {
  it("knows a process by pid and start time: alive while its pid runs and its heartbeat is fresh", () => {
    openDb(":memory:")
    let now = 1_000_000
    const alive = new Set([1001, 2002])
    const me = new ProcessRegistry(
      "desktop",
      "1.0.0",
      () => now,
      (pid) => alive.has(pid),
      1001,
      500,
    )
    const other = new ProcessRegistry(
      "tui",
      "1.0.0",
      () => now,
      (pid) => alive.has(pid),
      2002,
      600,
    )
    me.start()
    other.start()
    expect(me.key).toBe("1001:500")
    expect(me.isLive(me.key)).toBe(true)
    expect(me.isLive(other.key)).toBe(true)
    expect(me.isLive(null)).toBe(false)
    expect(me.isLive("2002:999")).toBe(false)
    // a heartbeat gone stale, though the pid was reused by something else
    now += STALE_MS + 1
    expect(me.isLive(other.key)).toBe(false)
    other.beat()
    expect(me.isLive(other.key)).toBe(true)
    alive.delete(2002)
    expect(me.isLive(other.key)).toBe(false)
    me.prune()
    expect((getDb().prepare("SELECT key FROM processes").all() as { key: string }[]).map((r) => r.key)).toEqual([me.key])
    me.stop()
    other.stop()
  })

  it("records a live process again at its next beat after another app pruned it while its heartbeat was stale", () => {
    openDb(":memory:")
    let now = 1_000_000
    const me = new ProcessRegistry(
      "desktop",
      "1.0.0",
      () => now,
      () => true,
      1001,
      500,
    )
    const sleeper = new ProcessRegistry(
      "tui",
      "1.0.0",
      () => now,
      () => true,
      2002,
      600,
    )
    me.start()
    sleeper.start()
    // the machine slept past the stale window; the other app pruned it at its start
    now += STALE_MS + 1
    me.beat()
    me.prune()
    expect(me.isLive(sleeper.key)).toBe(false)
    sleeper.beat()
    expect(me.isLive(sleeper.key)).toBe(true)
    me.stop()
    sleeper.stop()
  })
})

describe("recovery (R2.2)", () => {
  it("interrupts only the tasks and steps of a process that is gone", () => {
    openDb(":memory:")
    const log = new EventLog(tmp())
    log.owner = "live:1"
    const mine = log.createTask({ request: "a", sourceRoot: "C:/a", model: "m" })
    log.updateTask(mine.id, { state: "running" })
    log.owner = "gone:1"
    const theirs = log.createTask({ request: "b", sourceRoot: "C:/b", model: "m" })
    log.updateTask(theirs.id, { state: "running" })
    log.owner = null
    const legacy = log.createTask({ request: "c", sourceRoot: "C:/c", model: "m" })
    log.updateTask(legacy.id, { state: "waiting" })
    const s1 = log.addStep({ taskId: mine.id, kind: "delegation", title: "x", agent: "specialist", state: "running" })
    const s2 = log.addStep({ taskId: theirs.id, kind: "delegation", title: "y", agent: "specialist", state: "running" })

    expect(log.taskOwner(mine.id)).toBe("live:1")
    // a container named for a task this database does not hold is another data folder's (R2.3)
    expect(log.hasTask(mine.id)).toBe(true)
    expect(log.hasTask("99999999-9999-4999-8999-999999999999")).toBe(false)
    expect(log.recover((owner) => owner === "live:1")).toBe(2)
    expect(log.getTask(mine.id).state).toBe("running")
    expect(log.getTask(theirs.id).state).toBe("interrupted")
    expect(log.getTask(legacy.id).state).toBe("interrupted")
    expect(log.steps(mine.id).find((s) => s.id === s1.id)?.state).toBe("running")
    expect(log.steps(theirs.id).find((s) => s.id === s2.id)?.state).toBe("interrupted")
  })
})

describe("the database (R3)", () => {
  it("waits for another writer, migrates once, and records which app did", () => {
    const file = join(tmp(), "hfr.db")
    const d = openDb(file, { app: "tui", version: "0.2.0" })
    expect((d.prepare("PRAGMA busy_timeout").get() as { timeout: number }).timeout).toBe(5000)
    expect((d.prepare("PRAGMA user_version").get() as { user_version: number }).user_version).toBe(SCHEMA_VERSION)
    expect(JSON.parse((d.prepare("SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = 'schema.by'").get() as { value: string }).value)).toMatchObject({
      app: "tui",
      version: "0.2.0",
    })
    closeDb()
    // a second app finds it done and records nothing
    openDb(file, { app: "desktop", version: "0.2.0" })
    expect(JSON.parse((getDb().prepare("SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = 'schema.by'").get() as { value: string }).value).app).toBe("tui")
  })

  it("refuses a database a newer app migrated, naming it, and writes nothing", () => {
    const file = join(tmp(), "hfr.db")
    openDb(file, { app: "desktop", version: "0.2.0" })
    getDb().exec(`PRAGMA user_version = ${SCHEMA_VERSION + 3}`)
    getDb()
      .prepare("UPDATE settings SET value = ? WHERE key = 'schema.by'")
      .run(JSON.stringify({ app: "desktop", version: "9.1.0" }))
    closeDb()
    expect(() => openDb(file, { app: "tui", version: "0.2.0" })).toThrow(SchemaTooNew)
    expect(() => openDb(file, { app: "tui", version: "0.2.0" })).toThrow("upgraded by Harness for REA 9.1.0 (the desktop app)")
    const raw = new DatabaseSync(file)
    expect((raw.prepare("PRAGMA user_version").get() as { user_version: number }).user_version).toBe(SCHEMA_VERSION + 3)
    raw.close()
  })

  it("rolls back an exclusive write that fails", () => {
    openDb(":memory:")
    expect(() =>
      exclusive(() => {
        getDb().prepare("INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES ('x', '1')").run()
        throw new Error("no")
      }),
    ).toThrow("no")
    expect(getDb().prepare("SELECT 1 FROM settings WHERE key = 'x'").get()).toBeUndefined()
  })
})

describe("done once per machine (R4.2, R4.3)", () => {
  const docker = () => {
    const calls: string[] = []
    let ready = false
    const exec: Exec = async (args) => {
      calls.push(args.join(" "))
      if (args[0] === "version") return { code: 0, stdout: "29\n", stderr: "" }
      if (args[0] === "build") {
        ready = true
        return { code: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" }
      }
      if (args.join(" ").startsWith(`image inspect ${SPECIALIST_IMAGE}`))
        return ready ? { code: 0, stdout: `${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION} ${BASE_IMAGE}`, stderr: "" } : { code: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "No such image" }
      return { code: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" }
    }
    return { exec, calls, finish: () => (ready = true) }
  }

  it("shows another app's image build as running there, builds nothing, and reads the images again once it is done", async () => {
    const d = docker()
    let held = true
    const guard: OnceGuard = { take: () => (held ? { heldBy: "a terminal UI (process 7)" } : () => undefined) }
    const s = new SandboxService(d.exec, "/sandbox", () => undefined, guard, 5)
    const first = await s.status()
    expect(first.building).toBe(true)
    expect(first.buildLog).toContain("being prepared by a terminal UI (process 7)")
    const { done } = s.build()
    expect(d.calls.some((c) => c.startsWith("build"))).toBe(false)
    d.finish()
    held = false
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 30))
    const after = await s.status()
    expect(after.building).toBe(false)
    expect(after.images).toBe(true)
    expect(d.calls.some((c) => c.startsWith("build"))).toBe(false)
    void done
  })

  it("holds the build's guard while it builds, and releases it after", async () => {
    const d = docker()
    let released = 0
    const s = new SandboxService(d.exec, "/sandbox", () => undefined, { take: () => () => void released++ })
    await s.build().done
    expect(d.calls.filter((c) => c.startsWith("build"))).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(released).toBe(1)
  })

  it("refuses a second sign-in while another app signs Claude in, naming it", () => {
    const login = new LoginService(
      () => {
        throw new Error("never started")
      },
      () => undefined,
      { take: () => ({ heldBy: "the desktop app (process 9)" }) },
    )
    expect(() => login.start()).toThrow("Claude is being signed in from the desktop app (process 9)")
  })
})

describe("keys (R5.1, R5.2)", () => {
  const memory = (init: Record<string, string> = {}): KeyStore & { slots: Map<string, string> } => {
    const slots = new Map(Object.entries(init))
    return {
      slots,
      available: () => true,
      read: async (s) => slots.get(s) ?? null,
      write: async (s, k) => void (k === null ? slots.delete(s) : slots.set(s, k)),
    }
  }

  it("keeps each key as the UTF-8 bytes of one keychain entry per slot", async () => {
    const entries = new Map<string, number[]>()
    const make = (service: string, name: string): KeyEntry => ({
      getSecret: async () => entries.get(`${service}/${name}`) ?? null,
      setSecret: async (b) => void entries.set(`${service}/${name}`, [...b]),
      deleteCredential: async () => entries.delete(`${service}/${name}`),
    })
    const store = keyringStore("hfr-test", make)
    await store.write("openrouter.key", "sk-or-ü-1234")
    expect(Buffer.from(entries.get("hfr-test/openrouter.key")!).toString("utf8")).toBe("sk-or-ü-1234")
    expect(await store.read("openrouter.key")).toBe("sk-or-ü-1234")
    await store.write("openrouter.key", null)
    expect(await store.read("openrouter.key")).toBeNull()
    expect(keyringStore("x", null).available()).toBe(false)
  })

  it("moves the keys of a former store into the shared one, keeping one already there, and removes them", async () => {
    const former = memory({ "openrouter.key": "sk-old-openrouter", "deepseek.key": "sk-old-deepseek" })
    const shared = memory({ "deepseek.key": "sk-shared-deepseek" })
    expect(await moveKeys(former, shared)).toBe(2)
    expect(former.slots.size).toBe(0)
    expect(shared.slots.get("openrouter.key")).toBe("sk-old-openrouter")
    expect(shared.slots.get("deepseek.key")).toBe("sk-shared-deepseek")
    useKeyStore(shared)
    await initKey()
    expect(readKey("openrouter")).toBe("sk-old-openrouter")
  })
})

describe("changes made by another process (R5.3)", () => {
  it("pushes the tasks, steps, events, patches and projects another connection wrote, and deletions, once each", () => {
    const file = join(tmp(), "hfr.db")
    openDb(file)
    const pushes: Push[] = []
    const log = new EventLog(tmp())
    let holders = ""
    let keys = 0
    const w = new ChangeWatcher(
      {
        push: (p) => pushes.push(p),
        task: (id) => log.getTask(id),
        step: stepRow,
        event: eventRow,
        patch: patchRow,
        project: (id) => ({ id, name: "p", updatedAt: 0 }) as never,
        holders: () => holders,
        keysChanged: () => void keys++,
      },
      60_000,
    )
    w.start()
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(0)

    // another app, its own connection
    const other = openOther(file)
    const id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
    other.prepare("INSERT INTO tasks (id, request, source_root, model, state, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, 'r', 'C:/x', 'm', 'running', 5, 5)").run(id)
    other.prepare("INSERT INTO events (task_id, agent, at, kind, summary, payload) VALUES (?, 'app', 5, 'task.started', 's', '{}')").run(id)
    other
      .prepare(
        "INSERT INTO steps (id, task_id, ord, kind, title, agent, state, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('s1', ?, 0, 'plan', 't', 'orchestrator', 'running', 5, 5)",
      )
      .run(id)
    other.prepare("INSERT INTO patches (id, task_id, step_id, state, files, diff, created_at) VALUES ('p1', ?, 's1', 'pending', '[]', '', 5)").run(id)
    other.prepare("INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES ('keys.rev', '1')").run()
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(4)
    expect(pushes.map((p) => p.type).sort()).toEqual(["event", "patch", "step", "task"])
    expect(keys).toBe(1)
    // nothing new: nothing pushed again
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(0)

    other.prepare("DELETE FROM tasks WHERE id = ?").run(id)
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(1)
    expect(pushes.at(-1)).toEqual({ type: "taskDeleted", id })

    // a project taken by another app, seen through the locks rather than the database
    other
      .prepare(
        `INSERT INTO projects (id, name, goal, target_path, target_kind, source_root, folder, provider, model, orchestrator_effort, specialist_effort, created_at, updated_at)
       VALUES ('pr', 'n', 'understand', 'C:/t', 'folder', 'C:/t', 'C:/f', 'openrouter', 'm', 'medium', 'medium', 6, 6)`,
      )
      .run()
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(1)
    holders = "project-pr=1:1"
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(1)
    expect(pushes.at(-1)?.type).toBe("project")
    other.close()
    w.stop()
  })

  it("reads a change again when the diff that saw it failed part-way", () => {
    const file = join(tmp(), "hfr.db")
    openDb(file)
    const pushes: Push[] = []
    const log = new EventLog(tmp())
    let failOnce = true
    const w = new ChangeWatcher(
      {
        push: (p) => pushes.push(p),
        task: (id) => {
          if (failOnce) {
            failOnce = false
            throw new Error("deleted between two reads")
          }
          return log.getTask(id)
        },
        step: stepRow,
        event: eventRow,
        patch: patchRow,
        project: () => ({}) as never,
        holders: () => "",
        keysChanged: () => undefined,
      },
      60_000,
    )
    w.start()
    const other = openOther(file)
    other.prepare("INSERT INTO tasks (id, request, source_root, model, state, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('t1', 'r', 'C:/x', 'm', 'running', 5, 5)").run()
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(0)
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(1)
    expect(pushes[0]).toMatchObject({ type: "task" })
    other.close()
    w.stop()
  })

  it("does not push what this process pushed itself", () => {
    const file = join(tmp(), "hfr.db")
    openDb(file)
    const pushes: Push[] = []
    const log = new EventLog(tmp())
    const w = new ChangeWatcher({
      push: (p) => pushes.push(p),
      task: (id) => log.getTask(id),
      step: stepRow,
      event: eventRow,
      patch: patchRow,
      project: () => ({}) as never,
      holders: () => "",
      keysChanged: () => undefined,
    })
    log.setPush((p) => w.saw(p))
    w.start()
    const t = log.createTask({ request: "r", sourceRoot: "C:/x", model: "m" })
    log.append({ taskId: t.id, agent: "app", kind: "x", summary: "s" })
    // another connection commits something unrelated, so the version moves
    const other = openOther(file)
    other.prepare("INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES ('unrelated', '1')").run()
    expect(w.tick()).toBe(0)
    other.close()
    w.stop()
  })
})

function openOther(file: string): DatabaseSync {
  const d = new DatabaseSync(file)
  d.exec("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000; PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;")
  return d
}
```

```ts
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { tmpdir } from "node:os"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
import { claudeArgs } from "../src/main/sandbox/docker"
import { ClaudeAccount, spawnStart, cleanText, failureReason, isAnthropicUrl, loginUrl, parseStatus, validCode } from "../src/main/specialist/account"
import { classifyFailure, SpecialistError, SpecialistSession, type Launch } from "../src/main/specialist/executor"

/* specs/claude-specialist: the stream reader, the session over a prepared launch, and the login. */

const FAKE = join(import.meta.dirname, "fixtures", "fake-claude.mjs")

function fakeLaunch(mode: string, tools: "read" | "modify" = "read") {
  const base = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "hfr-spec-"))
  const work = join(base, "work")
  const run = join(base, "run")
  mkdirSync(join(work, "src"), { recursive: true })
  mkdirSync(run, { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(join(work, "src", "a.ts"), "export const a = 1\n")
  writeFileSync(join(run, "system.md"), "the system prompt")
  const logFile = join(base, "fake.jsonl")
  let stopped = 0
  const launch: Launch = {
    command: process.execPath,
    args: [FAKE, ...claudeArgs(tools).slice(1)],
    cwd: work,
    env: { HFR_FAKE: mode, HFR_FAKE_LOG: logFile, HFR_RUN: run, PATH: process.env.PATH ?? "", SYSTEMROOT: process.env.SYSTEMROOT ?? "" },
    stop: async () => {
      stopped++
    },
  }
  const logged = () =>
    existsSync(logFile)
      ? readFileSync(logFile, "utf8")
          .trim()
          .split("\n")
          .map((l) => JSON.parse(l))
      : []
  return { launch, work, logged, stopped: () => stopped }
}

describe("StreamReader (R2.1–R2.5)", () => {
  const line = (o: unknown) => JSON.stringify(o)

  it("reads init, text, thinking, calls and results", () => {
    const r = new StreamReader()
    expect(r.line(line({ type: "system", subtype: "init", session_id: "s1", model: "opus", tools: ["Read"] }))[0]).toMatchObject({
      kind: "init",
      payload: { model: "opus" },
    })
    const calls = r.line(
      line({
        type: "assistant",
        message: {
          content: [
            { type: "thinking", thinking: "hmm" },
            { type: "text", text: "Looking" },
            { type: "tool_use", id: "t1", name: "Read", input: { file_path: "/work/src/a.ts" } },
          ],
        },
      }),
    )
    expect(calls.map((c) => c.kind)).toEqual(["thinking", "text", "tool.call"])
    expect(calls[2]).toMatchObject({ summary: "Read src/a.ts", payload: { tool: "Read", files: [{ path: "src/a.ts", op: "read" }] } })
    const res = r.line(line({ type: "user", message: { content: [{ type: "tool_result", tool_use_id: "t1", content: [{ type: "text", text: "line 1" }] }] } }))
    expect(res[0]).toMatchObject({ kind: "tool.result", payload: { tool: "Read", output: "line 1" } })
    const err = r.line(line({ type: "user", message: { content: [{ type: "tool_result", tool_use_id: "t9", content: "boom", is_error: true }] } }))
    expect(err[0].payload.error).toBe("boom")
    expect(r.session).toBe("s1")
  })

  it("tracks a running tool's heartbeats as its progress, a few events per long call and none once it returned (specs/chat-timeline R1.4)", () => {
    const r = new StreamReader()
    r.line(line({ type: "assistant", message: { content: [{ type: "tool_use", id: "toolu_1", name: "Bash", input: { command: "make" } }] } }))
    const beat = (s: number, n: number) =>
      r.line(
        line({
          type: "tool_progress",
          tool_use_id: `toolu_1-heartbeat-${n}`,
          tool_name: "Bash",
          parent_tool_use_id: "toolu_1",
          elapsed_time_seconds: s,
          heartbeat: true,
          session_id: "s9",
        }),
      )
    const first = beat(5, 1)
    expect(first).toEqual([{ kind: "tool.progress", summary: "Bash running for 5s", payload: { tool: "Bash", callId: "toolu_1", elapsedSeconds: 5 } }])
    expect(beat(10, 2)).toEqual([])
    expect(beat(20, 3)[0].payload.elapsedSeconds).toBe(20)
    // never reported as an unknown line
    expect([...first, ...beat(59, 4)].some((e) => e.kind === "unknown")).toBe(false)
    r.line(line({ type: "user", message: { content: [{ type: "tool_result", tool_use_id: "toolu_1", content: "ok" }] } }))
    expect(beat(5, 5)[0].payload.elapsedSeconds).toBe(5)
  })

  it("attributes calls inside a subagent to it", () => {

    r.line(line({ type: "assistant", message: { content: [{ type: "tool_use", id: "ag", name: "Agent", input: { subagent_type: "Explore", prompt: "p" } }] } }))
    const inner = r.line(
      line({ type: "assistant", parent_tool_use_id: "ag", message: { content: [{ type: "tool_use", id: "g", name: "Grep", input: { path: "/work/src" } }] } }),
    )
    expect(inner[0].payload.subagent).toBe("Explore")
    const orphan = r.line(line({ type: "assistant", parent_tool_use_id: "zz", message: { content: [{ type: "text", text: "x" }] } }))
    expect(orphan[0].payload.subagent).toBe("general-purpose")
  })

  it("records tokens, cache tokens, cost as an estimate, duration and session", () => {

        subtype: "success",
        result: "done",
        session_id: "s2",
        duration_ms: 2000,

      }),
    )
    expect(e.payload).toMatchObject({ tokensIn: 10, tokensOut: 5, cacheTokens: 5, costUsd: 0.3, estimate: true, durationMs: 2000, session: "s2" })
    expect(r.result).toMatchObject({ text: "done", error: false, costUsd: 0.3 })
    const [f] = new StreamReader().line(line({ type: "result", subtype: "error_max_turns", is_error: true, usage: {} }))
    expect(f.summary).toContain("error_max_turns")
  })

  it("keeps lines it cannot read and unknown types instead of dropping them", () => {
    const r = new StreamReader()
    expect(r.line("garbage")[0]).toMatchObject({ kind: "unknown", payload: { output: "garbage" } })
    expect(r.line("[1,2]")[0].kind).toBe("unknown")
    expect(r.line(line({ type: "mystery" }))[0]).toMatchObject({ kind: "unknown", summary: "Unknown stream event type: mystery" })
    expect(r.line(line({ type: "stream_event" }))).toEqual([])
    expect(r.line("   ")).toEqual([])
  })

  it("caps text and arguments and marks them truncated", () => {
    const r = new StreamReader()
    const [t] = r.line(line({ type: "assistant", message: { content: [{ type: "text", text: "x".repeat(TEXT_CAP + 10) }] } }))
    expect((t.payload.output as string).length).toBe(TEXT_CAP)

        type: "assistant",

  it("maps /work paths back and ignores tools that touch no file", () => {

    expect(filesOf("Glob", { path: "/work/src" })).toEqual([{ path: "src", op: "read" }])
    expect(filesOf("Bash", { command: "ls" })).toEqual([])
    expect(filesOf("Read", {})).toEqual([])
    // REA's tools read what they are given, under whichever argument name
    expect(filesOf("mcp__rea__open_binary", { path: "/work/bin/app.so", detail: "summary" })).toEqual([{ path: "bin/app.so", op: "read" }])
    expect(filesOf("mcp__rea__inspect_android_package", { apk_path: "/work/game.apk" })).toEqual([{ path: "game.apk", op: "read" }])

describe("SpecialistSession (R1.1–R1.4)", () => {
  it("runs the launch it is given, sends turns on stdin and keeps the session open between them", async () => {
    const f = fakeLaunch("answer")
    const events: StreamEvent[] = []

  })

    expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(SpecialistError)
    expect(err.kind).toBe("auth")
    await expect(s.send("again")).rejects.toThrow()
  })

  it("rejects a failed result as a plan limit", async () => {
    const s = new SpecialistSession(fakeLaunch("limit").launch, { timeoutMs: 20_000 })
    await expect(s.send("hi")).rejects.toMatchObject({ kind: "limit", message: expect.stringContaining("resets 3pm") })
    await s.close()
  })

  it("rejects a safeguard refusal as its own kind, from the usage-policy message or the refusal stop reason (specs/specialist-lifecycle R2.1)", async () => {
    for (const mode of ["refusal", "refusal-quiet", "refusal-text"]) {
      const f = fakeLaunch(mode)
      const s = new SpecialistSession(f.launch, { timeoutMs: 20_000 })
      await expect(s.send("hi"), mode).rejects.toMatchObject({ kind: "refused", message: expect.stringMatching(/usage policy/i) })
      await s.close()
      // the CLI exited on its own: its container goes with it, nothing to kill (specs/specialist-lifecycle R3.1)
      expect(f.stopped()).toBe(0)
    }
  })

  it("does not take a failed turn that only talks about the usage policy for a refusal", async () => {
    const s = new SpecialistSession(fakeLaunch("policy-claim").launch, { timeoutMs: 20_000 })

  it("keeps unknown lines as events", async () => {

    await s.close()

  })

  it("stops the launch and the process on timeout and reports it", async () => {
    const f = fakeLaunch("hang")

    await expect(s.send("x")).rejects.toMatchObject({ kind: "timeout" })
    await s.kill("timeout")
    expect(s.outcome).toBe("timeout")
    expect(f.stopped()).toBe(1)
  })

  it("stops on cancel and refuses to start when already cancelled", async () => {
    const f = fakeLaunch("hang")
    const ac = new AbortController()
    const s = new SpecialistSession(f.launch, { timeoutMs: 20_000, signal: ac.signal })
    const pending = s.send("x")
    setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 200)
    await expect(pending).rejects.toMatchObject({ kind: "cancelled" })
    expect(s.outcome).toBe("cancelled")
    expect(() => new SpecialistSession(f.launch, { timeoutMs: 1000, signal: ac.signal })).toThrow(/Cancelled/)
  })

  it("reports a launch that cannot start", async () => {
    const s = new SpecialistSession({ command: join(tmpdir(), "no-such-binary.exe"), args: [] }, { timeoutMs: 5000 })
    await expect(s.send("x")).rejects.toThrow()
  })

  it("classifies failures", () => {
    expect(classifyFailure("Please run /login").kind).toBe("auth")
    expect(classifyFailure("API Error: Overloaded").kind).toBe("limit")
    expect(classifyFailure("something odd").kind).toBe("failed")
    // text alone is never a refusal: only the stream's stop reason or Claude Code's own error line is
    expect(classifyFailure("this violates our Usage Policy").kind).toBe("failed")
    expect(classifyFailure("").message).toContain("the run failed")
  })

describe("login (R3.1, R3.2)", () => {
  const account = (mode: string) =>
    new ClaudeAccount((sub) => spawn(process.execPath, [FAKE, "auth", ...sub], { env: { ...process.env, HFR_FAKE: mode }, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] }))

  it("reports the state from auth status without reading any credential", async () => {
    expect(await account("answer").state()).toEqual({ loggedIn: true, method: "claude.ai", plan: "max", email: "user@example.com" })
    expect((await account("logged-out").state()).loggedIn).toBe(false)
    expect(await new ClaudeAccount(() => spawn(join(tmpdir(), "nope.exe"))).state()).toEqual({ loggedIn: false, method: "none" })
  })

  it("exposes only the Anthropic URL and passes the code on", async () => {
    let text = ""
    const l = account("answer").login((t) => (text += t))
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400))
    expect(loginUrl(text)).toBe("https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize?code=true&state=abc")
    expect(() => l.sendCode("bad code with spaces")).toThrow(/does not look right/)
    l.sendCode("good-code-123")
    expect((await l.done).ok).toBe(true)
  })

  it("reports why a login failed", async () => {
    const l = account("answer").login(() => undefined)
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300))
    l.sendCode("wrong-code-456")
    const d = await l.done
    expect(d.ok).toBe(false)
    expect(failureReason(d.text)).toBe("OAuth error: invalid code")
  })

  it("stops what the child stands for when the login is cancelled", async () => {
    let stopped = 0
    const start = spawnStart(process.execPath, (sub) => ({ args: [FAKE, "auth", ...sub], stop: () => stopped++ }))
    const l = new ClaudeAccount(start).login(() => undefined)
    l.cancel()
    expect((await l.done).ok).toBe(false)
    expect(stopped).toBe(1)
    expect((await new ClaudeAccount(spawnStart(process.execPath, (sub) => ({ args: [FAKE, "auth", ...sub] }))).state()).loggedIn).toBe(true)
  })

  it("logs out and cancels", async () => {
    await account("answer").logout()
    const l = account("answer").login(() => undefined)
    l.cancel()
    expect((await l.done).ok).toBe(false)
  })

  it("accepts only Anthropic https pages and plausible codes", () => {
    expect(isAnthropicUrl("https://claude.ai/x")).toBe(true)
    expect(isAnthropicUrl("https://console.anthropic.com/x")).toBe(true)
    expect(isAnthropicUrl("http://claude.ai/x")).toBe(false)
    expect(isAnthropicUrl("https://claude.ai.evil.com/x")).toBe(false)
    expect(isAnthropicUrl("nope")).toBe(false)
    expect(loginUrl("visit https://evil.com/a then")).toBeNull()
    expect(validCode("abc")).toBe(false)
    expect(cleanText("\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m\x07")).toBe("red")
    expect(parseStatus('{"loggedIn":false}')).toEqual({ loggedIn: false, method: "none", plan: undefined, email: undefined })
    expect(failureReason("Opening browser\n\n")).toBe("The sign-in did not finish.")
    // What the pinned CLI prints: the outcome follows the prompt on the same line.
    expect(
      failureReason(
        "Opening browser to sign in…\nIf the browser didn't open, visit: https://claude.com/x\nPaste code here if prompted > Login failed: Request failed with status code 400\n",
      ),
    ).toBe("Login failed: Request failed with status code 400")
    expect(failureReason("Paste code here if prompted > ")).toBe("The sign-in did not finish.")
  })
})
```

```ts
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { tmpdir } from "node:os"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
import { closeDb, getDb, openDb } from "../src/main/db"
import type { EventLog } from "../src/main/events/log"
import { INSTALL_CAPS, SPECIALIST_IMAGE } from "../src/main/sandbox/docker"

  COMMAND_DEFAULT_S,
  folderSize,

  sandboxName,
  SandboxError,
  SpecialistBoxes,
  type BoxLimits,

/* specs/specialist-sandbox R1–R3: the sandboxes the orchestrator creates, controls and destroys, and their disk watch. */

let base = ""
let root = ""
let data = ""

beforeEach(() => {
  base = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "hfr-sbx-"))
  root = join(base, "repo")
  data = join(base, "data")
  mkdirSync(join(root, "src"), { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(join(root, "src", "a.bin"), Buffer.alloc(1000))
  openDb(join(data, "hfr.db"))
  // the sandboxes are recorded against their project (specs/projects R2.3)
  getDb()
    .prepare(
      `INSERT INTO projects (id, name, goal, target_path, target_kind, source_root, folder, provider, model, orchestrator_effort, specialist_effort, created_at, updated_at)
       VALUES ('p1', 'p', 'understand', ?, 'folder', ?, ?, 'openrouter', 'm', 'default', 'default', 0, 0)`,
    )
    .run(root, root, data)
})
afterEach(() => closeDb())

const limits: BoxLimits = { cpus: 4, memoryMb: 8192, diskMb: 1, pidsLimit: 512 }
const after = (args: string[], flag: string) => args.filter((_, i) => args[i - 1] === flag)

interface Fake {
  exec: ExecBuffer
  calls: { args: string[]; timeoutMs?: number }[]
  events: { kind: string; payload: Record<string, unknown> }[]
  /** what `container inspect --size` reports as the writable layer */
  layer: number
  /** the config label `inspect` reports for an existing container; none when unset */
  label?: string
}

function fake(answers: Record<string, Partial<BufferResult>> = {}): Fake {
  const f: Fake = { calls: [], events: [], layer: 0, exec: async () => ({ code: 0, stdout: Buffer.alloc(0), stderr: "" }) }
  f.exec = async (args, timeoutMs) => {
    f.calls.push({ args, timeoutMs })
    const key = args.join(" ")
    if (key.startsWith("container inspect --size")) return { code: 0, stdout: Buffer.from(`${f.layer}\n`), stderr: "" }
    if (args[0] === "inspect" && !answers.inspect)
      return f.label ? { code: 0, stdout: Buffer.from(f.label), stderr: "" } : { code: 1, stdout: Buffer.alloc(0), stderr: "Error: No such object" }
    const hit = Object.entries(answers).find(([k]) => key.startsWith(k))?.[1]
    return { code: 0, stdout: Buffer.alloc(0), stderr: "", ...hit }
  }
  return f
}

function boxes(f: Fake, everyMs = 60_000) {
  const log = {
    append: (e: { kind: string; payload?: Record<string, unknown> }) => f.events.push({ kind: e.kind, payload: e.payload ?? {} }),
  } as unknown as EventLog
  return new SpecialistBoxes({ exec: f.exec, log, dir: data, sourceRoot: root, projectId: "p1", actor: "t1", everyMs })
}

describe("a sandbox's docker run arguments (R1.1–R1.3)", () => {
  const ws = { id: "x", workspace: "C:\\d\\workspace\\x", runDir: "C:\\d\\runs\\x", snapshot: "C:\\d\\snapshots\\x", out: "C:\\d\\outputs\\x", files: [] }
  const args = sandboxArgs(sandboxName("x"), ws, limits, "C:\\d\\outputs\\x")

  it("starts a long-lived container from the specialist image with the orchestrator's limits", () => {
    expect(args.slice(0, 2)).toEqual(["run", "-d"])
    // kept when stopped, so what was installed outlives the task's end (specs/task-persistence R3.4)
    expect(args).not.toContain("--rm")
    expect(after(args, "--name")).toEqual(["hfr-sbx-x"])
    expect(after(args, "--memory")).toEqual(["8192m"])
    expect(after(args, "--cpus")).toEqual(["4"])
    expect(after(args, "--pids-limit")).toEqual(["512"])
    expect(args.slice(-2)).toEqual([SPECIALIST_IMAGE, "infinity"])
    expect(after(args, "--entrypoint")).toEqual(["sleep"])
  })

  it("runs as root:root with only the install capabilities and a writable root, on Docker's default network", () => {
    expect(after(args, "--user")).toEqual(["0:0"])
    expect(after(args, "--cap-drop")).toEqual(["ALL"])
    expect(after(args, "--cap-add")).toEqual(INSTALL_CAPS)
    expect(after(args, "--security-opt")).toEqual(["no-new-privileges"])
    expect(args).not.toContain("--read-only")
    expect(args).not.toContain("--privileged")
    expect(args).not.toContain("--network")
  })

  it("binds only its workspace, run directory, ask channel and output folder, besides the login volume (specs/task-persistence R3.3)", () => {
    expect(after(args, "--mount")).toEqual([
      "type=volume,source=hfr-claude-config,target=/home/agent/.claude-config",
      "type=bind,source=C:\\d\\workspace\\x,target=/work",
      "type=bind,source=C:\\d\\runs\\x,target=/run/hfr,readonly",
      `type=bind,source=${join("C:\\d\\runs\\x", "ask")},target=/run/hfr-ask`,
      "type=bind,source=C:\\d\\outputs\\x,target=/root/out",
    ])
    expect(args).not.toContain("-v")
    expect(args.join(" ")).not.toMatch(/docker\.sock|--tmpfs/)
  })
})

describe("creating, controlling and destroying sandboxes (R1.4, R1.5, R2)", () => {
  it("creates a sandbox, records it, and keeps nothing when Docker refuses", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    expect(f.calls[0].args).toEqual(labelled(sandboxArgs(box.name, box.ws, limits, box.outDir)))
    expect(box.outDir).toBe(join(data, "outputs", box.id))
    expect(existsSync(box.outDir)).toBe(true)
    expect(existsSync(box.ws.workspace)).toBe(true)
    expect(f.events.map((e) => e.kind)).toEqual(["sandbox.created"])
    await s.removeAll()

    const before = readdirSync(join(data, "workspace"))
    const refused = fake({ "run -d": { code: 125, stderr: "docker: Error response from daemon: range of CPUs is from 0.01 to 16.00" } })
    const r = boxes(refused)
    await expect(r.create({ ...limits, cpus: 64 })).rejects.toThrow(/Docker did not start the sandbox: .*range of CPUs/)
    expect(r.ids()).toEqual([])
    // nothing of the refused sandbox: no folder, no record
    expect(readdirSync(join(data, "workspace"))).toEqual(before)
    expect(boxes(fake()).ids()).toEqual([])
  })

  it("copies source files and scratch files into /work and refuses a path outside the source", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create({ ...limits, diskMb: 10 })
    const files = await s.copy(box.id, ["src/a.bin"], [{ path: "probe.py", content: Buffer.from("print(1)") }])
    expect(files.map((x) => x.path)).toEqual(["src/a.bin", ".orchestrator/probe.py"])
    expect(readFileSync(join(box.ws.workspace, "src", "a.bin")).length).toBe(1000)
    expect(Object.keys(readManifest(box.ws.snapshot))).toEqual(["src/a.bin"])
    await expect(s.copy(box.id, ["../outside"], [])).rejects.toThrow(PathRejected)
    expect(f.events.filter((e) => e.kind === "sandbox.copy")).toHaveLength(1)
    await s.removeAll()
  })

  it("refuses a copy that would pass the disk limit, copying nothing", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    f.layer = 1024 * 1024 - 500
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    await expect(s.copy(box.id, ["src/a.bin"], [])).rejects.toThrow(/1 MB disk limit/)
    expect(existsSync(join(box.ws.workspace, "src", "a.bin"))).toBe(false)
    await s.removeAll()
  })

  it("runs a command as root in /work under its time limit, capped, and records it", async () => {
    const f = fake({ "exec -w /work": { code: 3, stdout: Buffer.from("installed\n"), stderr: "warn" } })
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    const r = await s.run(box.id, "apt-get install -y binutils")
    expect(r).toEqual({ output: "installed\nwarn", exitCode: 3, truncated: false })
    const call = f.calls.find((c) => c.args[0] === "exec")!
    expect(call.args).toEqual(["exec", "-w", "/work", box.name, "timeout", "-s", "KILL", String(COMMAND_DEFAULT_S), "sh", "-c", "apt-get install -y binutils"])
    expect(call.timeoutMs).toBeGreaterThan(COMMAND_DEFAULT_S * 1000)
    await s.run(box.id, "true", 30)
    expect(f.calls.filter((c) => c.args[0] === "exec")[1].args[7]).toBe("30")
    expect(f.events.find((e) => e.kind === "sandbox.exec")?.payload).toMatchObject({ sandbox: box.id, command: "apt-get install -y binutils", exitCode: 3 })
    await s.removeAll()
  })

  it("refuses a sandbox this task does not have", async () => {
    const s = boxes(fake())
    expect(() => s.usable("nope")).toThrow(SandboxError)
    await expect(s.run("nope", "ls")).rejects.toThrow(/no sandbox nope in this project/)
    await expect(s.destroy("nope")).rejects.toThrow(SandboxError)
  })

  it("destroys a sandbox: container and record removed, its folders kept for the task (specs/task-persistence R4.3)", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    await s.destroy(box.id)
    expect(f.calls.at(-1)!.args).toEqual(["rm", "-f", box.name])
    expect(existsSync(box.ws.workspace)).toBe(true)
    expect(f.events.at(-1)!.kind).toBe("sandbox.destroyed")
    expect(() => s.usable(box.id)).toThrow(SandboxError)
    expect(boxes(fake()).ids()).toEqual([])
  })

  it("stops, and keeps, every sandbox of the task when it ends (specs/task-persistence R3.4)", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f)
    const a = await s.create(limits)
    const b = await s.create(limits)
    await s.stopAll()
    expect(f.calls.at(-1)!.args).toEqual(["stop", "-t", "2", a.name, b.name])
    expect(f.calls.some((c) => c.args[0] === "rm")).toBe(false)
    expect(existsSync(a.ws.workspace)).toBe(true)
  })

  it("removes every sandbox after a forced stop, keeping its record and folders to create it again (specs/task-persistence R3.8)", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f)
    const a = await s.create(limits)
    await s.dropAll()
    expect(f.calls.at(-1)!.args).toEqual(["rm", "-f", a.name])
    expect(existsSync(a.ws.workspace)).toBe(true)
    expect(getDb().prepare("SELECT 1 FROM sandboxes WHERE id = ?").get(a.id)).toBeTruthy()
    await s.removeAll()
  })

  it("stops, and keeps, the sandboxes a previous run of the app left running", async () => {
    const f = fake({ "ps --filter": { stdout: Buffer.from("hfr-sbx-aaa\nhfr-sbx-bbb\n") } })
    expect(await SpecialistBoxes.sweep(f.exec)).toBe(2)
    expect(f.calls[0].args).toEqual(["ps", "--filter", "name=^hfr-sbx-", "--format", "{{.Names}}"])
    expect(f.calls[1].args).toEqual(["rm", "-f", "hfr-sbx-aaa", "hfr-sbx-bbb"])
  })

  it("leaves running the sandboxes of a project a live app holds (specs/shared-data-folder R2.3)", async () => {
    const f = fake({ "ps --filter": { stdout: Buffer.from("hfr-sbx-aaa\nhfr-sbx-bbb\n") } })
    expect(await SpecialistBoxes.sweep(f.exec, (id) => id === "aaa")).toBe(1)
    expect(f.calls[1].args).toEqual(["rm", "-f", "hfr-sbx-bbb"])
  })

  it("holds a sandbox for one delegation at a time", async () => {
    const s = boxes(fake())
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    const held = await s.hold(box.id)
    await expect(s.hold(box.id)).rejects.toThrow(/already running a delegation/)
    await held.release()
    await (await s.hold(box.id)).release()
    await s.removeAll()
  })
})

describe("the disk limit (R3)", () => {
  it("measures the writable layer plus the workspace", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    f.layer = 4096
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create({ ...limits, diskMb: 10 })
    await s.copy(box.id, ["src/a.bin"], [])
    expect(await s.usage(box)).toBe(4096 + 1000)
    expect(folderSize(box.ws.workspace)).toBe(1000)
    // what the specialist extracts to /root/out lands on the host, and counts too (specs/rea-native R2.4)
    writeFileSync(join(box.outDir, "extracted.bin"), Buffer.alloc(300))
    expect(await s.usage(box)).toBe(4096 + 1000 + 300)
    await s.removeAll()
  })

  it("stops a sandbox past its limit after a command, records it, and refuses it afterwards", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    f.layer = 2 * 1024 * 1024
    const r = await s.run(box.id, "dd if=/dev/zero of=/big bs=1M count=2")
    expect(r.output).toMatch(/was stopped: it used 2 MB of disk, past its 1 MB limit/)
    expect(f.calls.some((c) => c.args.join(" ") === `kill ${box.name}`)).toBe(true)
    expect(f.events.find((e) => e.kind === "sandbox.stopped")?.payload).toMatchObject({ sandbox: box.id, usedMb: 2, diskMb: 1 })
    await expect(s.run(box.id, "ls")).rejects.toThrow(/was stopped: it used 2 MB/)
    await expect(s.hold(box.id)).rejects.toThrow(/was stopped/)
    await s.destroy(box.id)
  })

  it("watches on an interval while the sandbox runs", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f, 20)
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    f.layer = 5 * 1024 * 1024
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 120))
    expect(box.stopped).toMatch(/past its 1 MB limit/)
    expect(f.events.filter((e) => e.kind === "sandbox.stopped")).toHaveLength(1)
    await s.removeAll()
  })

  it("does not stop a sandbox within its limit", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    f.layer = 1000
    const s = boxes(f)
    const box = await s.create(limits)
    await s.run(box.id, "true")
    expect(box.stopped).toBeNull()
    await s.removeAll()
  })
})

describe.skipIf(!process.env.HFR_DOCKER)("SpecialistBoxes on Docker", () => {
  it("creates a root sandbox, copies in, installs and runs, and stops it past its disk", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const log = { append: (e: { kind: string }) => f.events.push({ kind: e.kind, payload: {} }) } as unknown as EventLog
    const s = new SpecialistBoxes({ exec: dockerExecBuffer, log, dir: data, sourceRoot: root, projectId: "p1", actor: "t1", everyMs: 60_000 })
    const box = await s.create({ cpus: 1, memoryMb: 512, diskMb: 64, pidsLimit: 256 })
    try {
      await s.copy(box.id, ["src/a.bin"], [])
      expect((await s.run(box.id, "id -u; id -g")).output.trim()).toBe("0\n0")
      expect((await s.run(box.id, "wc -c < /work/src/a.bin")).output.trim()).toBe("1000")
      expect((await s.run(box.id, "touch /usr/local/bin/x && echo writable")).output.trim()).toBe("writable")
      expect((await s.run(box.id, "getent hosts example.com || echo no-dns")).output).not.toContain("no-dns")
      const big = await s.run(box.id, "dd if=/dev/zero of=/root/big bs=1M count=100 2>/dev/null; echo done")
      expect(big.output).toMatch(/was stopped: .*past its 64 MB limit/)
      expect(f.events.map((e) => e.kind)).toContain("sandbox.stopped")
    } finally {
      await s.removeAll()
    }
    expect((await dockerExecBuffer(["ps", "-aq", "--filter", `name=^${box.name}$`])).stdout.toString().trim()).toBe("")
  }, 120_000)

  it("keeps what was installed and extracted across the task's end and reopening (specs/task-persistence R3.3–R3.6)", async () => {
    const log = { append: () => undefined } as unknown as EventLog
    const first = new SpecialistBoxes({ exec: dockerExecBuffer, log, dir: data, sourceRoot: root, projectId: "p1", actor: "t1" })
    const box = await first.create({})
    try {
      await first.run(box.id, "touch /usr/local/bin/installed && echo extracted > /root/out/notes.txt")
      await first.stopAll()
      const reopened = new SpecialistBoxes({ exec: dockerExecBuffer, log, dir: data, sourceRoot: root, projectId: "p1", actor: "t1" })
      expect((await reopened.run(box.id, "ls /usr/local/bin/installed; cat /root/out/notes.txt")).output).toBe("/usr/local/bin/installed\nextracted\n")
      // Docker lost it: created again, the output folder still there
      await reopened.stopAll()
      await dockerExecBuffer(["rm", "-f", box.name])
      const again = new SpecialistBoxes({ exec: dockerExecBuffer, log, dir: data, sourceRoot: root, projectId: "p1", actor: "t1" })
      expect((await again.run(box.id, "cat /root/out/notes.txt")).output).toMatch(/created again.*extracted/s)
      await again.removeAll()
    } finally {
      await dockerExecBuffer(["rm", "-f", box.name])
    }
  }, 120_000)

  it("leaves nothing when Docker refuses the limits", async () => {
    const s = new SpecialistBoxes({
      exec: dockerExecBuffer,
      log: { append: () => undefined } as unknown as EventLog,
      dir: data,
      sourceRoot: root,
      projectId: "p1",
    })
    await expect(s.create({ cpus: 4096, memoryMb: 512, diskMb: 64, pidsLimit: 256 })).rejects.toThrow(/Docker did not start the sandbox/)
  }, 60_000)
})

  })

describe("a sandbox across the task's reopening (specs/task-persistence R3.5, R3.6)", () => {
  it("is recorded, found again by a reopened task under the same id, and started again on first use", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const first = boxes(f)
    const box = await first.create(limits)
    await first.copy(box.id, ["src/a.bin"], [])
    await first.stopAll()
    // the task reopens, in this run of the app or a later one
    const again = fake({ "exec -w /work": { stdout: Buffer.from("ok\n") } })
    again.label = labelled(sandboxArgs(box.name, box.ws, limits, box.outDir))[3]
    const reopened = boxes(again)
    expect(reopened.ids()).toEqual([box.id])
    expect(reopened.usable(box.id).ws.files.map((x) => x.path)).toEqual(["src/a.bin"])
    expect(again.calls).toEqual([])
    const r = await reopened.run(box.id, "ls")
    expect(again.calls[0].args[0]).toBe("inspect")
    expect(again.calls[1].args).toEqual(["start", box.name])
    expect(r.output).toBe("ok\n")
    expect(again.events.map((e) => e.kind)).toContain("sandbox.reopened")
    // started once, not on every call
    await reopened.run(box.id, "ls")
    expect(again.calls.filter((c) => c.args[0] === "start")).toHaveLength(1)
    await reopened.removeAll()
  })

  it("is created again over its folders when Docker no longer has it, and says what was lost", async () => {
    const first = boxes(fake())
    const box = await first.create({})
    await first.stopAll()
    const gone = fake({ "exec -w /work": { stdout: Buffer.from("ok\n") } })
    const reopened = boxes(gone)
    const r = await reopened.run(box.id, "ls")
    const run = gone.calls.find((c) => c.args[0] === "run")!.args
    expect(run).toEqual(labelled(sandboxArgs(box.name, box.ws, {}, box.outDir)))
    expect(r.output).toBe(`${recreated(box.id)} ok\n`)
    expect(recreated(box.id)).toMatch(/\/work and \/root\/out were kept, anything installed is gone/)
    await reopened.removeAll()
  })

  it("is removed with its record when the task is deleted (specs/task-persistence R4.1)", async () => {
    const f = fake()
    const s = boxes(f)
    const a = await s.create(limits)
    await s.stopAll()
    const reopened = boxes(f)
    await reopened.removeAll()
    expect(f.calls.at(-1)!.args).toEqual(["rm", "-f", a.name])
    expect(boxes(fake()).ids()).toEqual([])
  })
})

describe("deleting a task's sandboxes (specs/task-persistence R4.1)", () => {
  it("removes every recorded container, even one whose folders are gone, and keeps the records when Docker fails", async () => {

  })
})
```

`tests/status.test.ts`:

```ts
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
import type { LoginStatus, SandboxStatus } from "../src/shared/types"
import { closeDb, openDb, setSetting } from "../src/main/db"
import { baseUrlFor } from "../src/main/readiness"
import { getSettings, saveSettings } from "../src/main/settings"
import { BASE_IMAGE, CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION, SPECIALIST_IMAGE, type Exec } from "../src/main/sandbox/docker"
import { LoginService, SandboxService } from "../src/main/status"
import { DEFAULT_SETTINGS } from "../src/shared/defaults"

/* specs/desktop-ui R1: what Settings reads and drives. */

const FAKE = join(import.meta.dirname, "fixtures", "fake-claude.mjs")

describe("settings (R1.1)", () => {
  beforeAll(() => openDb(":memory:"))
  afterAll(() => closeDb())

  it("returns the defaults until changed, then merges each change", () => {
    expect(getSettings()).toEqual(DEFAULT_SETTINGS)
    saveSettings({ model: "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash" })
    expect(saveSettings({ timeoutMinutes: 7 })).toEqual({ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, model: "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash", timeoutMinutes: 7 })
  })

  it("keeps each provider's base URL when the user switches provider and back (specs/orchestrator R1.10)", () => {
    saveSettings({ provider: "custom" })
    saveSettings({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:1234/v1" })
    expect(saveSettings({ provider: "openrouter" })).toMatchObject({ provider: "openrouter", baseUrl: "" })
    expect(saveSettings({ provider: "deepseek", baseUrl: "https://proxy.example/v1" }).baseUrl).toBe("https://proxy.example/v1")
    expect(saveSettings({ provider: "custom" })).toMatchObject({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:1234/v1" })
    expect(getSettings().baseUrls).toEqual({ custom: "http://localhost:1234/v1", deepseek: "https://proxy.example/v1" })
    expect(baseUrlFor("deepseek", getSettings())).toBe("https://proxy.example/v1")
  })

  it("moves a base URL saved before they were kept per provider to the provider it was saved on", () => {
    setSetting("app.settings", { provider: "custom", baseUrl: "http://old.example/v1" })
    expect(getSettings()).toMatchObject({ baseUrl: "http://old.example/v1", baseUrls: { custom: "http://old.example/v1" } })
    expect(saveSettings({ provider: "openrouter" }).baseUrls).toEqual({ custom: "http://old.example/v1" })
  })
})

describe("SandboxService (R1.2, specs/sandbox-images R3)", () => {
  /** A Docker whose image is ready or not, whose build succeeds or not, and whose version answers or not. */
  const docker = (o: { ready: boolean; build?: boolean; running?: boolean }) => {
    const calls: string[] = []
    const state = { ready: o.ready, running: o.running ?? true }
    const exec: Exec = async (args) => {
      calls.push(args.join(" "))
      if (args[0] === "version") return state.running ? { code: 0, stdout: "29\n", stderr: "" } : { code: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "not running\n" }
      if (args[0] === "build") {
        if (o.build === false) return { code: 1, stdout: "step\n", stderr: "failed to verify\n" }
        state.ready = true
        return { code: 0, stdout: "step\n", stderr: "" }
      }
      if (args.join(" ").startsWith(`image inspect ${SPECIALIST_IMAGE}`))
        return state.ready ? { code: 0, stdout: `${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION} ${BASE_IMAGE}`, stderr: "" } : { code: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "No such image" }
      return { code: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" }
    }
    return { exec, calls, state }
  }
  const builds = (calls: string[]) => calls.filter((c) => c.startsWith("build")).length

  it("does not push its state again when a read finds it as it was, so a view re-reading on each push stops", async () => {
    const seen: SandboxStatus[] = []
    const s = new SandboxService(docker({ ready: true }).exec, "/sandbox", (x) => seen.push(x))
    await s.status()
    const after = seen.length
    await s.status()
    await s.status()
    expect(seen).toHaveLength(after)
  })

  it("reports Docker and a ready image, and pushes each change, preparing nothing", async () => {
    const seen: SandboxStatus[] = []
    const d = docker({ ready: true })
    const s = new SandboxService(d.exec, "/sandbox", (x) => seen.push(x))
    expect(await s.status()).toMatchObject({ docker: true, images: true, building: false, claudeVersion: CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION })
    expect(seen).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(builds(d.calls)).toBe(0)
  })

  it("prepares a missing image on its own the first time it finds Docker running", async () => {
    const d = docker({ ready: false })
    const s = new SandboxService(d.exec, "/sandbox")
    expect(await s.status()).toMatchObject({ building: true })
    expect(d.calls).toContain(`pull ${BASE_IMAGE}`)
    const done = await s.build().done
    expect(done).toMatchObject({ building: true })
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0))
    expect(await s.status()).toMatchObject({ images: true, building: false })
    expect(builds(d.calls)).toBe(1)
  })

  it("waits for Docker when it is not running at start", async () => {
    const d = docker({ ready: false, running: false })
    const s = new SandboxService(d.exec, "/sandbox")
    expect(await s.status()).toMatchObject({ docker: false, building: false })
    d.state.running = true
    expect(await s.status()).toMatchObject({ building: true })
  })

  it("prepares once at a time and records the log", async () => {
    const s = new SandboxService(docker({ ready: true }).exec, "/sandbox")
    const b = s.build()
    expect(b.status.building).toBe(true)
    expect(s.build().status.building).toBe(true)
    expect(await s.status()).toMatchObject({ building: true })
    const done = await b.done
    expect(done.building).toBe(false)
    expect(done.buildLog).toContain("Done.")
  })

  it("keeps a failure in the log and does not prepare again until asked", async () => {
    const d = docker({ ready: false, build: false })
    const s = new SandboxService(d.exec, "/sandbox")
    const done = await s.build().done
    expect(done.buildLog).toContain("failed to verify")
    expect(done.buildLog).toContain("Preparing the image failed.")

    expect(builds(d.calls)).toBe(1)
    await s.build().done
    expect(builds(d.calls)).toBe(2)
  })

describe("LoginService (R1.3)", () => {
  const start = (mode: string) => (sub: string[]) =>
    spawn(process.execPath, [FAKE, "auth", ...sub], { env: { ...process.env, HFR_FAKE: mode }, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] })

  it("does not push the sign-in state again when a refresh finds it as it was", async () => {
    const seen: LoginStatus[] = []
    const s = new LoginService(start("answer"), (x) => seen.push(x))
    await s.refresh()
    await s.refresh()
    expect(seen).toHaveLength(1)
  })

  it("refreshes the state and logs out", async () => {
    const s = new LoginService(start("answer"))
    expect(await s.refresh()).toMatchObject({ loggedIn: true, plan: "max", inProgress: false, url: null })
    expect((await s.logout()).loggedIn).toBe(true)
    expect(() => s.sendCode("whatever-123")).toThrow(/No sign-in/)
  })

  it("shows the Anthropic URL while signing in and finishes with the code", async () => {
    const seen: LoginStatus[] = []
    const s = new LoginService(start("answer"), (x) => seen.push(x))
    const l = s.start()
    expect(l.status.inProgress).toBe(true)
    expect(s.start().status.inProgress).toBe(true)
    for (let i = 0; i < 50 && !s.url(); i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 50))
    expect(s.url()).toMatch(/^https:\/\/claude\.com\//)
    expect(seen.some((x) => x.url)).toBe(true)
    s.sendCode("good-code-123")
    const done = await l.done
    expect(done).toMatchObject({ inProgress: false, loggedIn: true, error: "" })
  })

  it("reports a failed sign-in and can cancel", async () => {
    const s = new LoginService(start("logged-out"))
    const l = s.start()
    for (let i = 0; i < 50 && !s.url(); i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 50))
    s.cancel()
    expect((await l.done).error).not.toBe("")
    expect(s.url()).toBeNull()
  })
})
```

`tests/taskbox.test.ts`:

```ts
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"

/*
  adr:0007-run-the-orchestrators-tools-in-a-task-container: the orchestrator's tools in a read-only
  task container (specs/orchestrator R2.2), and the brief it writes for the specialist
  (specs/task-sandbox R3.1, R3.2).

describe("task container arguments (R2.2)", () => {
  const args = taskBoxArgs("t1", "C:\\Users\\me\\repo", "C:\\data\\tasks\\t1\\scratch")
  const after = (flag: string) => args.filter((_, i) => args[i - 1] === flag)

  it("binds the whole source folder read-only at /workspace and the task's scratch folder at /scratch, nothing else", () => {
    // Recursively read-only: a mount nested inside the source folder stays read-only too.
    expect(after("--mount")).toEqual([
      `type=bind,source=C:\\Users\\me\\repo,target=${WORKSPACE},readonly,bind-propagation=rprivate,bind-recursive=readonly`,
      `type=bind,source=C:\\data\\tasks\\t1\\scratch,target=${SCRATCH}`,
    ])
    expect(after("-w")).toEqual([WORKSPACE])
  })

  it("has Docker's default network, root with a writable root to install software, and no limit (specs/sandbox-images R4.1, specs/specialist-sandbox R6.1)", () => {
    expect(args).not.toContain("--network")
    expect(after("--user")).toEqual(["0:0"])
    expect(after("--cap-drop")).toEqual(["ALL"])
    expect(after("--cap-add")).toEqual(["CHOWN", "DAC_OVERRIDE", "FOWNER", "FSETID", "SETUID", "SETGID", "KILL"])
    expect(args).not.toContain("--read-only")
    expect(args).not.toContain("--privileged")
    expect(after("--security-opt")).toEqual(["no-new-privileges"])
    expect(args.join(" ")).not.toMatch(/docker\.sock/)
    for (const flag of ["--memory", "--memory-swap", "--cpus", "--pids-limit", "--storage-opt"]) expect(args).not.toContain(flag)
    expect(after("--name")).toEqual([taskBoxName("t1")])
    expect(args.slice(-2)).toEqual([SPECIALIST_IMAGE, "infinity"])
    expect(after("--entrypoint")).toEqual(["sleep"])
    // kept when stopped, so what was installed outlives the task's end (specs/task-persistence R3.4)
    expect(args).not.toContain("--rm")
    expect(args).toContain("--init")
    expect(args.join(" ")).not.toMatch(/ -e |--env/)
  })

  it("refuses a source path that would add mount options", () => {
    expect(() => taskBoxArgs("t", "C:/a,b", "C:/s")).toThrow(/comma or quote/)
    expect(() => taskBoxArgs("t", "C:/a", "C:/s,x")).toThrow(/comma or quote/)
  })

  it("gives the orchestrator a writable /scratch on the host apart from the read-only source, with no size cap (specs/chat R6.3, specs/task-persistence R3.2)", () => {
    expect(args).not.toContain("--tmpfs")
    expect(SCRATCH).toBe("/scratch")
    expect(after("--mount")[0]).toContain(",readonly")
    expect(after("--mount")[1]).not.toContain("readonly")
  })
})

function fake(answers: (args: string[]) => Partial<BufferResult>): { exec: ExecBuffer; calls: string[][] } {
  const calls: string[][] = []
  return { calls, exec: async (args) => (calls.push(args), { code: 0, stdout: Buffer.from(""), stderr: "", ...answers(args) }) }
}

describe("TaskBox", () => {
  it("runs commands in the container and reports output, exit code and truncation", async () => {
    const f = fake((a) =>
      a.some((x) => x.includes("big")) ? { stdout: Buffer.from("x".repeat(OUTPUT_CAP + 5)) } : { code: 2, stdout: Buffer.from("out\n"), stderr: "err\n" },
    )
    const box = new TaskBox(f.exec, "t1")
    expect(await box.execute("ls /workspace")).toEqual({ output: "out\nerr\n", exitCode: 2, truncated: false })
    expect(f.calls[0]).toEqual(["exec", "hfr-orch-t1", "timeout", "-s", "KILL", "110", "sh", "-c", "ls /workspace"])
    const big = await box.execute("echo big")
    expect(big.truncated).toBe(true)
    expect(big.output).toHaveLength(OUTPUT_CAP)
  })

  it("writes uploads under /scratch only, and refuses every other path (specs/chat R6.3, R6.4)", async () => {
    const inputs: (Uint8Array | undefined)[] = []
    const calls: string[][] = []
    const exec: ExecBuffer = async (args, _timeout, input) => {
      calls.push(args)
      inputs.push(input)
      return { code: args.includes("/scratch/deny/x") ? 1 : 0, stdout: Buffer.from(""), stderr: "" }
    }
    const box = new TaskBox(exec, "t1")
    const bytes = new Uint8Array([104, 105])
    expect(
      await box.uploadFiles([
        ["/scratch/probe/run.py", bytes],
        ["/workspace/src/a.ts", bytes],
        ["/scratch/../workspace/a.ts", bytes],
        ["scratch/relative", bytes],
        ["/scratch", bytes],
        ["/scratch/deny/x", bytes],
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      { path: "/scratch/probe/run.py", error: null },
      { path: "/workspace/src/a.ts", error: "permission_denied" },
      { path: "/scratch/../workspace/a.ts", error: "permission_denied" },
      { path: "scratch/relative", error: "permission_denied" },
      { path: "/scratch", error: "permission_denied" },
      { path: "/scratch/deny/x", error: "permission_denied" },
    ])
    expect(calls).toHaveLength(2)
    expect(calls[0].slice(0, 4)).toEqual(["exec", "-i", "hfr-orch-t1", "sh"])
    expect(calls[0].at(-1)).toBe("/scratch/probe/run.py")
    expect(inputs[0]).toEqual(bytes)
  })

  it("downloads files through cat, reporting what is missing or a directory", async () => {
    const f = fake((a) =>
      a.at(-1) === "/workspace/a"
        ? { stdout: Buffer.from("hi") }
        : a.at(-1) === "/workspace/d"
          ? { code: 1, stderr: "cat: /workspace/d: Is a directory" }
          : { code: 1, stderr: "No such file" },
    )
    const out = await new TaskBox(f.exec, "t1").downloadFiles(["/workspace/a", "/workspace/d", "/workspace/z"])
    expect(Buffer.from(out[0].content!).toString()).toBe("hi")
    expect(out.map((o) => o.error)).toEqual([null, "is_directory", "file_not_found"])
  })

  it("marks output that hit the buffer cap as truncated, and refuses such a download", async () => {
    const f = fake(() => ({ stdout: Buffer.from("partial"), overflow: true }))
    const box = new TaskBox(f.exec, "t1")
    expect((await box.execute("yes")).truncated).toBe(true)
    expect((await box.downloadFiles(["/dev/zero"]))[0]).toEqual({ path: "/dev/zero", content: null, error: "file_not_found" })
  })

  it("stops reading a command whose output passes the cap", async () => {
    const r = await dockerExecBuffer.call(null, ["--version"])
    expect(r.overflow).toBe(false)
    expect(BUFFER_CAP).toBeGreaterThan(OUTPUT_CAP)
  })

  it("stops, and keeps, the task containers a previous run left running (specs/task-persistence R3.4)", async () => {
    const f = fake((a) => (a[0] === "ps" ? { stdout: Buffer.from("hfr-orch-abc\nhfr-orch-def\n") } : {}))
    expect(await TaskBox.sweep(f.exec)).toBe(2)
    expect(f.calls).toEqual([
      ["ps", "--filter", "name=^hfr-orch-", "--format", "{{.Names}}"],
      ["rm", "-f", "hfr-orch-abc", "hfr-orch-def"],
    ])
    const none = fake(() => ({ stdout: Buffer.from("") }))
    expect(await TaskBox.sweep(none.exec)).toBe(0)
    expect(none.calls).toHaveLength(1)
  })

  it("leaves running the task containers of a task a live app has open (specs/shared-data-folder R2.3)", async () => {
    const f = fake((a) => (a[0] === "ps" ? { stdout: Buffer.from("hfr-orch-mine\nhfr-orch-gone\n") } : {}))
    expect(await TaskBox.sweep(f.exec, (id) => id === "mine")).toBe(1)
    expect(f.calls[1]).toEqual(["rm", "-f", "hfr-orch-gone"])
    const all = fake((a) => (a[0] === "ps" ? { stdout: Buffer.from("hfr-orch-mine\n") } : {}))
    expect(await TaskBox.sweep(all.exec, () => true)).toBe(0)
    expect(all.calls).toHaveLength(1)
  })

  it("starts the container Docker still has, creates it when not, says why it could not, and stops it at the end (specs/task-persistence R3.4, R3.5)", async () => {
    const scratch = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "hfr-scr-")), "scratch")
    // what an app of this version made: started again as it is
    const label = labelled(taskBoxArgs("t1", "C:/repo", scratch))[3]
    const kept = fake((a) => (a[0] === "inspect" ? { stdout: Buffer.from(`${label}\n`) } : {}))
    const again = await TaskBox.start(kept.exec, "t1", "C:/repo", scratch)
    expect(kept.calls.map((c) => c[0])).toEqual(["inspect", "start"])
    expect(kept.calls[1]).toEqual(["start", "hfr-orch-t1"])
    expect(again.created).toBe(false)
    const gone = fake((a) => (a[0] === "inspect" ? { code: 1, stderr: "Error: No such object: hfr-orch-t1\n" } : {}))
    const box = await TaskBox.start(gone.exec, "t1", "C:/repo", scratch)
    expect(gone.calls[1].slice(0, 2)).toEqual(["run", "-d"])
    expect(box.created).toBe(true)
    expect(existsSync(scratch)).toBe(true)
    await box.dispose()
    expect(gone.calls.at(-1)).toEqual(["stop", "-t", "2", "hfr-orch-t1"])
    // a forced stop removes it; /scratch is the task's folder on the host (specs/task-persistence R3.8)
    await box.dispose({ remove: true })
    expect(gone.calls.at(-1)).toEqual(["rm", "-f", "hfr-orch-t1"])
    await expect(
      TaskBox.start(
        fake((a) =>
          a[0] === "start" ? { code: 1, stderr: "No such container" } : { code: 125, stderr: "docker: Error response from daemon: invalid mount\n" },
        ).exec,
        "t2",
        "C:/repo",
        scratch,
      ),
    ).rejects.toThrow(/invalid mount/)
    const removed = fake(() => ({}))
    await TaskBox.remove(removed.exec, "t1")
    expect(removed.calls).toEqual([["rm", "-f", "hfr-orch-t1"]])
  })

  it("brings a stopped container up again quietly, and says what was reset when it had to be created (specs/task-persistence R3.5)", async () => {
    const scratch = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "hfr-scr-")), "scratch")
    // stopped: started again, nothing to report
    let state: "up" | "stopped" | "gone" = "up"
    const label = labelled(taskBoxArgs("t1", "C:/repo", scratch))[3]
    const f = fake((a) => {
      if (a[0] === "inspect") return state === "gone" ? { code: 1, stderr: "No such object" } : { stdout: Buffer.from(label) }
      if (a[0] === "start") return state === "gone" ? { code: 1, stderr: "No such container: hfr-orch-t1" } : ((state = "up"), {})
      if (a[0] === "run") return ((state = "up"), {})
      if (a[0] === "exec" && state === "stopped") return { code: 1, stderr: "Error response from daemon: container abc is not running\n" }
      if (a[0] === "exec" && state === "gone") return { code: 1, stderr: "Error response from daemon: No such container: hfr-orch-t1\n" }
      return { stdout: Buffer.from("ok\n") }
    })
    const box = await TaskBox.start(f.exec, "t1", "C:/repo", scratch)
    state = "stopped"
    expect((await box.execute("echo ok")).output).toBe("ok\n")
    state = "gone"
    const r = await box.execute("echo ok")
    expect(r).toMatchObject({ exitCode: 0 })
    expect(r.output).toBe(`${RESTARTED} ok\n`)
    expect(RESTARTED).toMatch(/\/scratch was kept, anything installed is gone/)
    // Once the task ended, a stopped container stays stopped.
    await box.dispose()
    state = "stopped"
    expect((await box.execute("echo ok")).output).toMatch(/is not running/)
  })

  it("creates again, over the same folders, a container an older app made with another image or boundary (specs/task-persistence R3.5)", async () => {
    const scratch = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "hfr-scr-")), "scratch")
    const old = fake((a) => (a[0] === "inspect" ? { stdout: Buffer.from("hfr.config=0123456789abcdef") } : {}))
    const box = await TaskBox.start(old.exec, "t1", "C:/repo", scratch)
    expect(old.calls.map((c) => c[0])).toEqual(["inspect", "rm", "run"])
    expect(old.calls[2]).toEqual(labelled(taskBoxArgs("t1", "C:/repo", scratch)))
    expect(box.created).toBe(true)
    // the label is the fingerprint of every argument: another image or flag gives another one
    expect(labelled(["run", "-d", "a"])[3]).not.toBe(labelled(["run", "-d", "b"])[3])
    expect(labelled(["run", "-d", "a"]).slice(0, 3)).toEqual(["run", "-d", "--label"])
  })

  it("reports a container that cannot be brought up again as the error it was", async () => {
    const f = fake((a) => (a[0] === "run" ? { code: 125, stderr: "no space" } : { code: 1, stderr: "Error response from daemon: No such container: x\n" }))
    const box = new TaskBox(f.exec, "t1", async () => null)
    expect((await box.execute("ls")).output).toMatch(/No such container/)
  })
})

describe.skipIf(!process.env.HFR_DOCKER)("TaskBox on Docker", () => {
  it("serves the source read-only to root, reaches the internet, and comes back when removed", async () => {
    const src = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "hfr-box-"))
    mkdirSync(join(src, "src"))
    writeFileSync(join(src, "src", "a.js"), "one\ntwo\n")
    const id = `smoke-${Date.now()}`
    const scratch = join(src, "..", `${id}-scratch`)
    const box = await TaskBox.start(dockerExecBuffer, id, src, scratch)
    try {
      expect((await box.read("/workspace/src/a.js")).error).toBeUndefined()
      expect(JSON.stringify(await box.read("/workspace/src/a.js"))).toContain("two")
      const write = await box.execute("echo x > /workspace/new.txt")
      expect(write.exitCode).not.toBe(0)
      expect((await box.execute("getent hosts example.com || echo no-dns")).output).not.toContain("no-dns")
      expect((await box.execute("id -u")).output.trim()).toBe("0")
      // the scratch takes writes and runs them; the source still refuses them (specs/chat R6.3)
      expect((await box.write("/scratch/probe.sh", "echo probed")).error).toBeUndefined()
      expect((await box.execute("sh /scratch/probe.sh")).output.trim()).toBe("probed")
      expect((await box.write("/workspace/probe.sh", "x")).error).toBeDefined()
      expect((await box.execute("apt-get --version >/dev/null && touch /usr/local/bin/installed && echo ok")).output.trim()).toBe("ok")
      // stopped at the task's end and started on its reopen: scratch and installs both still there
      await box.dispose()
      const reopened = await TaskBox.start(dockerExecBuffer, id, src, scratch)
      expect(reopened.created).toBe(false)
      expect((await reopened.execute("cat /scratch/probe.sh; ls /usr/local/bin/installed")).output).toBe("echo probed/usr/local/bin/installed\n")
      // removed from outside: created again over the same scratch, the installs gone
      await dockerExecBuffer(["rm", "-f", taskBoxName(id)])
      expect((await reopened.execute("cat /scratch/probe.sh; ls /usr/local/bin/installed 2>/dev/null || echo none")).output).toBe(
        `${RESTARTED} echo probednone\n`,
      )
    } finally {
      await TaskBox.remove(dockerExecBuffer, id)
    }
  }, 60_000)
})
```

`tests/timeline.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
import type { EventRow, StepRow } from "@shared/types"
import type { ToolItem } from "../src/renderer/src/lib/chat"
import { stepOf, Timeline } from "../src/renderer/src/lib/timeline"

/* specs/chat-timeline R1.1, R1.3, R2.3, R3.2: the timeline folded from pages of the log. */

let n = 0
const ev = (kind: string, payload: Record<string, unknown> = {}, o: Partial<EventRow> = {}): EventRow => ({
  id: ++n,
  taskId: "t",
  stepId: null,
  agent: "orchestrator",
  at: n,
  kind,
  state: "",
  summary: kind,
  payload,
  truncated: false,
  ...o,
})
const step = (id: string, data: Record<string, unknown> = {}): StepRow => ({
  id,
  taskId: "t",
  ord: 1,
  kind: "delegation",
  title: id,
  agent: "specialist",
  state: "running",
  data,
  createdAt: 0,
  updatedAt: 0,
})

describe("the timeline (specs/chat-timeline)", () => {
  it("nests the specialist's text, thinking and tool calls under the delegation that ran them, results paired by call id", () => {
    const steps = [step("s1", { callId: "call-1" })]
    const t = new Timeline(
      steps,
      [
        ev("message.user", { output: "go" }, { agent: "app" }),
        ev("tool.call", { tool: "delegate_to_specialist", input: "{}", callId: "call-1" }),
        ev("sandbox.copy", { output: "" }, { agent: "sandbox", stepId: "s1", summary: "Copied 1 file(s)" }),
        ev("specialist.thinking", { output: "hmm" }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" }),
        ev("specialist.tool.call", { tool: "Read", callId: "r1", input: '{"file_path":"/work/a"}' }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1", summary: "Read a" }),
        ev("specialist.text", { output: "found it" }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" }),
        ev("specialist.tool.result", { tool: "Read", callId: "r1", output: "contents" }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" }),
        ev("tool.result", { tool: "delegate_to_specialist", output: "{}", callId: "call-1" }),
      ],
      true,
    )
    expect(t.items.map((i) => i.kind)).toEqual(["user", "tool"])
    const call = t.items[1] as ToolItem
    expect(call).toMatchObject({ callId: "call-1", output: "{}" })
    expect(stepOf(call, steps)?.id).toBe("s1")
    expect(t.run("s1").map((e) => `${e.kind}:${e.output ?? e.body}`)).toEqual(["note:", "thinking:hmm", "tool:contents", "text:found it"])
  })

  it("shows how long a running specialist tool has run from its heartbeats, without an entry of their own (R1.4)", () => {
    const t = new Timeline(
      [step("s1")],
      [
        ev("specialist.tool.call", { tool: "Bash", callId: "b1", input: "{}" }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" }),
        ev("specialist.tool.progress", { tool: "Bash", callId: "b1", elapsedSeconds: 30 }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" }),
      ],
      true,
    )
    expect(t.run("s1")).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(t.run("s1")[0]).toMatchObject({ kind: "tool", elapsedSeconds: 30 })
    t.append([ev("specialist.tool.result", { tool: "Bash", callId: "b1", output: "done" }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" })])
    t.append([ev("specialist.tool.progress", { tool: "Bash", callId: "b1", elapsedSeconds: 45 }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" })])
    expect(t.run("s1")[0]).toMatchObject({ output: "done", elapsedSeconds: 30 })
  })

  it("folds only events newer than the last one, adding a specialist's event under its delegation as it arrives", () => {
    const steps = [step("s1", { callId: "c" })]
    const first = [ev("tool.call", { tool: "delegate_to_specialist", callId: "c" })]
    const t = new Timeline(steps, first, true)
    const items = t.items
    expect(t.append(first)).toBe(false)
    const text = ev("specialist.text", { output: "x" }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" })
    expect(t.append([text])).toBe(true)
    expect(t.append([text])).toBe(false)
    expect(t.items).toBe(items)
    expect(t.run("s1")).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(t.events).toHaveLength(2)
  })

  it("pairs a result with its call by id even when two calls of one tool overlap", () => {
    const t = new Timeline(
      [],
      [
        ev("tool.call", { tool: "execute", callId: "a" }),
        ev("tool.call", { tool: "execute", callId: "b" }),
        ev("tool.result", { tool: "execute", callId: "b", output: "B" }),
        ev("tool.result", { tool: "execute", callId: "a", output: "ERROR: A" }),
      ],
      true,
    )
    expect(t.items.map((i) => `${(i as ToolItem).callId}:${(i as ToolItem).output}:${(i as ToolItem).failed}`)).toEqual(["a:ERROR: A:true", "b:B:false"])
  })

  it("refolds from an older page with what was loaded after it, and knows no opening request on a page that starts mid-task", () => {
    const older = [ev("message.user", { output: "first" }, { agent: "app" }), ev("tool.call", { tool: "ls", callId: "l" })]
    const newer = [ev("message.user", { output: "later" }, { agent: "app" }), ev("tool.result", { tool: "ls", callId: "l", output: "x" })]
    const page = new Timeline([], newer, false)
    expect(page.items).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ kind: "user", text: "later", read: false })])
    const whole = page.prepend(older, [], true)
    expect(whole.firstId).toBe(older[0].id)
    expect(whole.items.map((i) => i.kind)).toEqual(["user", "tool", "user"])
    expect(whole.items[0]).toMatchObject({ read: true })
    expect(whole.items[1]).toMatchObject({ output: "x" })
  })

  it("marks a failed delegation event and leaves a question in the conversation rather than in the run", () => {
    const t = new Timeline(
      [step("s1")],
      [
        ev("delegation.failed", { error: "boom" }, { agent: "sandbox", stepId: "s1" }),
        ev("specialist.result", { output: "r", error: "x" }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" }),
        ev("question.asked", { questionId: "q", question: { prompt: "p", reason: "r", kind: "text", default: "d" } }, { agent: "specialist", stepId: "s1" }),
      ],
      true,
    )
    expect(t.run("s1").map((e) => `${e.kind}:${e.failed}`)).toEqual(["note:true", "result:true"])
  })
})
```
